commits.subject: fix(plan 062 H): const assignment in loop head/body throws TypeError
commits.body:
The register-resident-local optimization elided PUTLEX_C along with the
other env-write opcodes, so a const binding had no non-writable flag in the
lex_env at runtime. Combined with the postfix INC / assignment compiler
paths emitting bare register-only opcodes for register-cached locals, a
const violation in three contexts silently succeeded:

  • for (const i = 0; i < 1; i++) {}      → i++ emitted INC r0 (no check)
  • for (const k in obj) { k = 2; }       → k = 2 emitted RESOLVEVAR + LDINT
                                           + THROW_UNRESOLVED + PUTVAR_ASSIGN
                                           but env walk found no binding,
                                           throwing "'k' is not defined"
                                           instead of TypeError
  • for (const v of arr) { v = 2; }       → v = 2 emitted LDREG only (no PUT)

Two-part fix:

  1. The env-write elision in finish() now keeps PUTLEX_C. The flag must
     survive so the runtime env walk can throw on a const. The other
     declarations (DECLVAR, DECLVAR_HOIST, PUTLEX, INITTZ) stay elided.

  2. Every register-only write site (postfix INC/DEC with result
     discarded, prefix INC/DEC, plain assignment in void and non-void
     contexts, compound assignment, and the three logical assignments
     ||= / &&= / ??=) now checks find_const_name_idx(left). If the
     target register is the home slot of a CONST binding, the site emits
     INC_VAR / DEC_VAR / PUTVAR_ASSIGN instead of the silent bare-register
     opcode, so the runtime walks the env, finds the non-writable flag,
     and throws "Assignment to constant variable '<name>'".

find_const_name_idx returns 0xFFFFFFFF as the "not found" sentinel
rather than 0 — add_string_constant legitimately returns 0 for the first
string interned into a fresh constant pool, and the previous "!= 0"
sentinel would have false-negatively treated that match as a miss.

Phase 7: 1204 → 1207 pass / 4 → 1 fail (remaining fail is for-in/S12.6.4_A7_T2,
group N). Rosetta 100/100, golden-bytecode 10/10.

commits.subject: plan 062 group N: for-in yields keys deleted during enumeration
commits.body:
collect_forin_keys snapshots the key list at INITFOR time and NEXTFOR
just walks that array, so a property deleted from the target before
its turn is still yielded (we were producing 'aa1baundefinedca3' where
spec/qjs produce 'aa1ca3' for language/statements/for-in/S12.6.4_A7_T2.js).

EnumerateObjectProperties / ForIn/OfBodyEvaluation step 4 require a
liveness re-check at yield time — Duktape does it via
duk_hobject_enumerator_next + duk_hobject_hasprop_raw on the original
target, QuickJS via JS_GetOwnPropertyInternal on the level object.

We add a forin_key_still_exists(target, key) helper called from NEXTFOR:
proxy targets bypass the check (keys are virtual), the rest fall through
has_prop_proto (proto-chain walk) for ordinary property lookup, with
special branches for TypedArray (integer index < ta_element_count,
mirrors IsValidIntegerIndex, so a shrink/detach properly drops the
out-of-range indices) and String wrapper (char index < char_length).

ForInState grows a borrowed target pointer that INITFOR temproot-pins
and NEXTFOR clears when the state is freed — the loop body can overwrite
every register and the GC must still see the target. Re-add after
delete-before-turn behaves per spec (the re-added key, never yet yielded,
is visited on the NEXTFOR that walks to its slot).

Composes with the plan 062 group F shadowing pre-passes — those still
mark every own non-enumerable key as seen so a same-named enumerable
prototype key never enters the snapshot. Deletion of an own
non-enumerable key that was just marked seen is unobservable because it
was never going to be yielded anyway; deletion of an own enumerable key
that survived the pre-pass is the case this fix targets.

commits.subject: fix(compiler): TDZ on let/const self-reference inside a function body (plan 062 G)
commits.body:
The block-scoped let/const TDZ path was correct at script top level
(is_global=true makes primary_expr emit GETVAR unconditionally) but
broken when the same shape was nested in a function body. In
`function g(){ { const x = x + 1; } }`, declare_var adds an x
entry to scope_stack BEFORE the initializer runs, so the inner
`x` resolves through resolve_var to its just-allocated register.
That register holds `undefined`, so the addition silently produces
NaN and PUTLEX_C stores it — the INITTZ sentinel installed by the
block never gets read.

Add an is_tdz flag to ScopeEntry. declare_var sets it for LET/CONST
so resolve_var returns SCOPE_ERROR during the binding's TDZ window,
forcing primary_expr to emit GETVAR (which throws against the INITTZ
sentinel, or against a missing binding if the env was elided).
emit_var_store clears it after the publishing PUTLEX/PUTLEX_C so
later reads in the same scope can return to the fast register path.

Fixes the 4 use-before-initialization-in-declaration-statement tests
and incidentally also fixes the head-let/head-const-bound-names-
fordecl-tdz for-in tests (same root cause family). Phase 7:
1184 -> 1190 pass, 21 -> 15 fail; rosetta 100/100; golden-bytecode
10/10.

commits.subject: plan 062 group K: enforce async [no LT] and escape-aware contextual keyword
commits.body:
`async` is a contextual keyword whose AsyncArrowFunction /
AsyncFunctionDeclaration productions (ES2017 §14.7) require
`[no LineTerminator here]` between `async` and what follows. The four
async-prefix detection sites were missing this check, so:

- `async\nx => {}` parsed as AsyncArrowFunction instead of being two
  expression statements (one of which is an unbound identifier
  reference).
- `async\nfunction f(){}` parsed as AsyncFunctionDeclaration instead of
  an identifier reference followed by a separate FunctionDeclaration.

In addition, an IdentifierName written with a Unicode escape
(`\u0061sync`, etc.) is a plain identifier per ES2024 §5.1.5 — terminal
symbols must appear exactly as written.  The same sites also missed
that check, so `\u0061sync\np => {}` was incorrectly accepted as an
AsyncArrowFunction.

Fix all four sites:

- src/compiler/tokens.c3
    `match_async_function` (AsyncFunctionExpression prefix) — add
    `cur.has_escape` rejection and `next_tok.line != cur.line` rejection.
    `is_async_arrow_lookahead` (AsyncArrowFunction prefix) — same checks
    for both the IDENTIFIER and LPAREN branches.

- src/compiler/statements.c3
    `statement()` async-function-declaration dispatch — same two
    checks; previously only checked `id_tok.str_value == "async"` and
    `peek_type() == FUNCTION`.

- src/compiler/functions.c3
    `hoist_decls` (function-body pre-scan) and
    `hoist_global_fn_decls` (global-scope pre-scan) — same checks;
    the pre-scan was silently marking the surrounding body as
    `is_async=true` whenever the bytes `async function` straddled a
    line break, then the same escaping bug made any `\u0061sync
    function …` an async declaration.

Phase 24 moves 1227/4 fail → 1230/1 fail (the lone remaining failure is
plan 062 group L, another agent's scope); rosetta 100/100; golden
bytecode 10/10.

commits.subject: fix(shapes): key shape transitions on flags, not just parent+key
commits.body:
Property flags were dropped from the shape-transition dedup key, so
put_prop() always transitioned as if the new property were a plain
WEC data property and then, when the caller wanted different flags
(private fields, private methods/accessors, defineProperty, etc.),
fell back to set_prop_flags() -> make_shape_private(). That path
deliberately flattens the shape chain into a standalone shape that is
never registered in the transition table, so every instance of a
class with a private field burned a fresh, uncacheable shape ID.
Because the shape-ID space is process-global, this made construction
cost scale with total private-field instance count across the whole
program (not per class) and pushed programs toward the 16-bit shape
ID ceiling much sooner than plain-property classes did.

Extend TransitionEntry with the property's flags and fold them into
the transition hash/equality check, and thread flags through
transition_shape_new_flags() (new) down into shape_extend() instead
of hardcoding PROP_FLAGS_WEC. Two objects that reach the same parent
shape and add the same key with the same flags now converge on one
shared shape, even when those flags are non-default, so classes with
private fields/methods share shapes across instances exactly like
plain-property classes do. make_shape_private() is now reserved for
genuinely object-specific mutation (seal/freeze/defineProperty on an
object that already diverged from its shared shape).

commits.subject: fix(class): private instance methods/accessors survive super() return-override
commits.body:
The spec puts private methods/accessors on the class prototype as a
memory-sharing optimization, but that's only valid when an instance's
[[Prototype]] actually is the class prototype. A derived constructor's
super() can return an unrelated object (return-override, ES2022 9.2.2 step
13.c), whose prototype chain never reaches the class prototype at all --
GETPROP_PRIVATE's chain walk then finds nothing, even though the brand is
correctly stamped on the instance (fields already handled this correctly
via per-instance INITPROP_PRIV in __field_init__).

Fix: install the SAME closure objects (read back via a hidden lexical
slot PUTLEX'd by the prototype-install loop) onto each instance's own
properties from __field_init__, using CLASS_INITPROP/CLASS_INITGET/
CLASS_INITSET. This runs before any field initializer so a field that
reads `this.#m()` still sees the per-instance install order required by
InitializeInstanceElements (methods before fields). Verified against
quickjs and node/V8 across plain methods, get/set pairs, nested/sibling
classes, and multi-level inheritance.

Un-skips
language/statements/class/subclass/private-class-field-on-nonextensible-return-override.js
(phase 15: 7107 -> 7108 pass, still 0 fail).

Also found and confirmed pre-existing on a clean checkout (unrelated to
this fix, not addressed here): installing ANY non-writable-or-similar
private member as an own property forces HObject.make_shape_private()
per instance (never registered in the shape transition table), so any
class with private fields or methods exhausts the ushort shape-ID space
after roughly 65000/N instantiations. Filed as a follow-up rather than
folded into this change since it's a distinct root cause (shape-table
design) touching all private members, not specific to return-override.

commits.subject: fix(module): resolve a pending async dependency through its cycle root
commits.body:
execute_module tracked only a single async_dep per module, naming the
directly-imported dependency that was still suspended on TLA. For a
module reachable only through one member of an async import cycle
(e.g. importing a cycle leaf whose root is a different module), this
let the importer resolve/run as soon as that leaf settled instead of
waiting for the whole cycle — one position too early, per
top-level-await/pending-async-dep-from-cycle.js.

Adds ModuleDef.cycle_root, an approximation of ECMA-262 [[CycleRoot]]:
set on a module the moment its own dependency walk hits a genuine
DFS back-edge (an ancestor still literally on the call stack, not
merely suspended elsewhere), naming that ancestor as the cycle's root.
A later dependency lookup that resolves to a pending module follows
its cycle_root (Note 2 under InnerModuleEvaluation) instead of the
module itself, unless that root is the module doing the looking up
(its own still-open cycle, not a separate wait).

whole-script fatal abort, not a per-frame signal, so calling it after
async_reject_and_pop has already settled the promise and restored the caller
abandoned that frame: with OOM forced inside a nested await, the outer
function's catch handler and the script's sync tail never ran.

fails the Nth GeneratorState allocation. Before: execute() returned VM_ERROR
and the script halted. After: the outer catch runs and execution continues.

commits.subject: fix(vm): stop double-reporting AWAIT OOM after promise rejection
commits.body:
The GeneratorState-allocation OOM path in AWAIT called async_reject_and_pop
(which rejects the async function's Promise and restores the caller frame)
and then unconditionally called vm_uncaught_error on top of it. That aborts
the whole VM with the OOM as a fatal error even after the rejection was
already delivered through the normal microtask contract, discarding the
caller frame async_reject_and_pop had just restored — so a catch around the
await never ran and script execution halted early instead of continuing.
The sibling PromiseResolve-constructor-error path only falls back to
vm_uncaught_error when async_reject_and_pop returns false (no promise to
reject at all); align the OOM path with that same convention.

Verified with a fault-injection harness that fails the GeneratorState alloc
on a real await: before the fix, execute() returned VM_ERROR and aborted
the script early; after, the promise is rejected/caught normally and the
script runs to completion, matching quickjs's ordering for throw/reject/
await-rejected/catch. All 18 phases (0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,11,12,14,15,17,21,
22,23,24) at 0 fails, phase 25 at 1 fail (baseline), golden-bytecode 10/10,
rosetta 100/100.

commits.subject: fix(module): defer dynamic import to a job and make microtask draining reentrant
commits.body:
Dynamic import ran its whole resolve/link/evaluate/settle pipeline inline with
the import() call, so it preempted the calling module's still-in-progress
static DFS evaluation order. Per §16.2.1.5.2 and §13.3.10 it must return its
promise synchronously but do the work as a separate job.

Deferring it alone was not enough: execute_module_async waits for a
top-level-await module by polling drain_microtasks, whose boolean reentrancy
guard silently no-ops when called from inside a job already being drained — so
a dynamic import of an async module returned "settled" while still pending.
Both halves land together here.

commits.subject: vm(generators): extract async_reject_and_pop, dedup AWAIT teardown
commits.body:
AWAIT's two failure paths — a PromiseResolve constructor-lookup error and
a GeneratorState allocation failure (OOM) — each inlined the same ~30
lines to reject the current async function's Promise, pop its
activation, and restore the caller's dispatch state (valstack, current
function/bytecode pointers, curr_pc) in ds. Extract this into
async_reject_and_pop(), preserving both callers' distinct post-conditions
exactly: the constructor-error path resumes the caller when a promise was
rejected and only calls vm_uncaught_error on the no-promise fallback; the
OOM path still unconditionally calls vm_uncaught_error afterward (except

commits.body:

§16.2.1.7.1 ParseModule step 10.1 (Table 59), an ExportEntry whose LocalName
matches an ImportEntry's LocalName must instead become an INDIRECT export
sourced directly from that ImportEntry's own ModuleRequest/ImportName — the
re-export bypasses the importing module's local binding entirely.

Added mod_find_import_by_local to cross-reference the export-name list
against the module's already-registered import entries at compile time, and
route a match through mod_register_export's indirect path (reusing the
existing "*" local_name convention for a re-exported namespace import).

with aliasing, `export *`, a live binding mutated after import, and
namespace key ordering — output matches exactly.

and the two namespace-unambiguous-if-*-and-export.js tests now pass
(phase 25: 401->404 pass, 7->4 fail).

commits.subject: fix(module): direct self-import of a class binding must see TDZ, not undefined
commits.body:
Two compounding bugs left `import { C as D } from './self.js'; export class C {}`
(and the anonymous `export default class {}` self-import variant) reading
`undefined` instead of throwing a TDZ ReferenceError:

1. link_module's early import-resolution loop eagerly copied the source
   module's current env value at *link* time, before that module's own
   export/TDZ pre-declaration loop had run. For a self-import this raced
   against — and clobbered — the module's own not-yet-declared `class`
   binding, and the later pre-declaration loop's `env_has` check then skipped
   re-seeding the TDZ sentinel because a binding already existed. Removed the
   copy: the only import-time work link_module needs to do is the JSON-module
   named-export validation; actual binding installation (including self-
   imports) already happens correctly in execute_module's live-binding loop,
   which runs after every module's TDZ pre-declaration has completed.

2. `export default class {}` registered its export as non-lexical, even
   though the class's own outer binding is always `let`-style/TDZ
   (class_declaration always uses LET for the outer class_reg, named or
   anonymous). This meant the export pre-declaration loop seeded a plain
   `undefined` instead of the TDZ sentinel even once bug 1 was fixed.

Verified against qjs: both self-import forms now throw ReferenceError before
the class declaration runs, matching qjs's behavior.

instn-named-bndng-dflt-cls.js now pass (phase 25: 399->401 pass, 9->7 fail).

commits.subject: fix(compiler): direct eval inside an ordinary function can see `arguments`
commits.body:
`eval('arguments.length')` called directly from inside a plain function
threw ReferenceError because the enclosing function's uses_arguments flag
is only set when `arguments` is referenced in the function's own parsed
text — never when it's only referenced inside a nested eval() string,
which the compiler can't see into. Without that flag the VM never
materializes the arguments object, so the eval body's runtime GETVAR
lookup for "arguments" fails.

Force uses_arguments whenever a compiled function contains a direct eval
call, except for arrows and eval bodies themselves (neither has its own
arguments binding): arrows propagate has_direct_eval up to the nearest
enclosing ordinary function instead, and eval's CALL re-dispatch always
runs with 0 args, so setting the flag on an eval body's own CF would
create a bogus empty arguments object shadowing the real one.

Pre-existing bug, confirmed by building commit 10a0a74b (immediately
before bc64d706, which only added the unrelated forbid_arguments/
ContainsArguments class-field-initializer check) and reproducing the
same ReferenceError there.

commits.subject: fix(hobject): free async function GeneratorState via shared refcount
commits.body:
resume_fn and reject_fn (the .then reaction closures an AWAIT suspend
attaches to the awaited Promise) both stash the same GeneratorState in
var_env, but neither is a single owning HObject the way a GENERATOR
instance owns its GeneratorState — they are two independently
mark-and-swept FUNCTION objects. hobject_free never freed this GS at all,
leaking the struct (and its saved_regs/this_binding) on every async
function that suspends at least once. Give GeneratorState a ref_count (set
to 2 when the pair is created) and decrement it in hobject_free; only the
second of the pair to die actually frees the struct, so the survivor never
sees a dangling var_env.

Landing this safely required two more fixes surfaced while testing it under
GC pressure (both pre-existing, exposed once GeneratorState was actually
freed instead of leaked forever):

- mark_hobject's FUNCTION case unconditionally read
  (*obj.extra_ptr()).func.var_env.bindings before checking is_async_state,
  misinterpreting a GeneratorState* as an EnvRecord* (reading gs.func through
  the EnvRecord.bindings offset) and calling mark_hobject on a
  CompiledFunction*. Skip that walk entirely for is_async_state functions,
  and mark the real var_env/lex_env bindings from inside
  mark_generator_state instead (via a new hobject::env_record_bindings
  helper, since heap.c3 can't import env.c3 directly).

- The PROMISE case's reaction-chain walk read `reaction.next`
  (HeapHeader.next — the unrelated heap_allocated GC-list thread pointer)
  instead of the reaction's actual "next" link, which is a hidden TVal
  property (see reaction_set_next). This left pending reactions essentially
  untracked by the mark phase. Fixed via a cached
  hobject::promise_reaction_next_key, set once during Promise init.

Confirmed with a debug alloc/free counter: dbg_gs_allocs == dbg_gs_frees
after a full GC pass for 2000 completed, 2000 rejected-and-caught, 2000
abandoned (never-settling), and 2000 x 3-awaits async functions (all
previously 100% leaked). The unmodified baseline binary (4fe6cfe9)
segfaults outright on the same completed-2000 repro once a full
mark-and-sweep pass runs, from the reaction-chain `.next` bug above — this
fix resolves that crash as a side effect, not just the leak.

commits.subject: fix(heap): make pinned-string refcount immutable to stop incref/decref drift
commits.body:
int_to_hstring's small-int cache (and builtin strings / well-known symbols)
pin a string's refcount so RC/sweep never frees it, but ordinary incref/decref
traffic from transient register/TVal borrows (e.g. GETPROP_CACHE's
ToPropertyKey writeback into the key register, later clobbered by a raw
LDINT on the next loop iteration without a matching decref) still mutated
the raw refcount field. This is harmless in isolation - pinned strings never
reach 0 - but it is unbounded and, in principle, could wrap a uint. Give
incref/decref an explicit contract: on a pinned string, they are no-ops.
Pinning now goes through HeapHeader.set_pinned()/is_pinned() instead of a
bare refcount assignment.

Confirmed the refcount that previously drifted by +2/iteration across
a[0]-style property reads now stays fixed at STRING_PINNED_REFCOUNT
indefinitely.

That surfaced a second, more fundamental bug: the deferred brand
symbol/object registers were captured from parse-time temporaries
rather than persistent registers, so a getter invoked while reading
the source property (`src.a`) clobbered them — invoke_getter writes
its callee/this pair at [result_reg, result_reg + 1] before the call
even runs, exactly where those temporaries could land. Any private
field destructuring target with an accessor source property broke,
independent of derived classes or return-override — the class-fields-
private-in test that surfaced it merely happened to exercise both.
Both registers are now allocated persistently (member_obj_reg's
existing slot for the object; a new pre-scan slot for the brand

commits.subject: fix(compiler): reject arguments in direct eval called from field initializers
commits.body:
ES2022 15.7.10 step 14 (ContainsArguments) requires that a direct eval
called from inside a class field/static initializer or static block
reject a bare `arguments` reference in the eval SOURCE at eval-call
time. Our forbid_arguments flag only rejected `arguments` in the
initializer's own parsed text, so `eval('arguments')` ran to
completion (any side effects included) before failing.

Rather than a full ContainsArguments static-analysis pass, stamp
forbid_arguments onto every CompiledFunction and have direct eval
(builtin_eval -> compile_eval) inherit it from the calling activation's
CompiledFunction -- covering nested eval-in-eval for free, since a
nested eval body carries the same flag on its own CF. Arrow bodies
also propagate the enclosing forbid_arguments, since an arrow has no
`arguments` binding of its own.

commits.subject: fix(module): stop indirect re-exports from leaking as local identifiers, fix relative-path module identity
commits.body:
Two compounding bugs caused a module-namespace TDZ ReferenceError from an
accessor getter to escape an enclosing try/catch (test262
language/module-code/instn-iee-bndng-*):

1. call_resolve_name only stripped a leading "./" from a relative specifier
   when base_name itself had a directory component. A top-level module
   loaded with no base directory (e.g. "a.js") and the same file reached via
   a same-directory sibling's "./a.js" import normalized to two different
   cache keys, so a cyclic self-reference got its own separate, never-linked
   ModuleDef with stale pre-linked TDZ export bindings.

2. link_module and execute_module each declared indirect re-export names
   (`export { x as y } from './z'`) as live accessor bindings directly in
   the re-exporting module's own env. Per ECMA-262 §16.2.1.6.2, an indirect
   export installs no binding at all in its own module — it's only
   observable externally via ResolveExport / the namespace object, both of
   which already resolve it directly through export-entry metadata. The
   spurious local binding turned an internal reference to the re-exported
   name into a TDZ read instead of a plain unresolved-reference throw, and a
   second TDZ throw from the same accessor inside a catch handler (which
   runs through the accessor getter's re-entrant nested Vm.run) had nothing
   left to catch it.

commits.subject: fix(module): module top-level `this` is always undefined
commits.body:
Module Environment Records have HasThisBinding() = true but
GetThisBinding() always returns undefined (ECMA-262 §8.1.1.5.4) — a
module's top-level `this` is never globalThis, unlike a script's. All
three module-body execution entry points (execute_in_env,
execute_module_async, execute_module_nested) unconditionally bound `this`
to the global object instead, the same as Vm.execute (the script path).

(cherry picked from commit ed04048607762e6272c841c677ff17da07e2ee74)

commits.subject: fix(compiler): correctly detect an already-hoisted top-level generator declaration
commits.body:
function_declaration()'s "was this name already hoisted?" check read the
token after `function` to get the declared name, but for `function* f()`
it pushed the `*` back onto the lexer's single-slot pushback buffer and
then immediately called next_token() again — which just returns the same
pushed-back `*`, never advancing to `f`. name_opt.type was always STAR for
a generator, so the hoisted-name lookup could never match and every
top-level generator declaration silently fell through to recompile and
re-run CLOSURE+DECLVAR/DECLGLOBALFUNC a second time at its own textual
position, re-instantiating (and re-binding) a closure that hoisting had
already installed once — observable as a module-scope generator's
identity/prior-assignment not surviving to its declaration's textual
position.

Uses the CompilerContext token pushback stack (already used elsewhere for
"peek N, put back all N") instead of the lexer's single-slot pushback, so
both the `*` and the identifier can be un-consumed in order.

(cherry picked from commit bdc90ae921023b24624d255533a27fc906bd0f3b)

commits.subject: fix(compiler): correct generator flag and async source-span in top-level function hoisting
commits.body:
hoist_decls/hoist_global_fn_decls pre-compile every top-level function
declaration so a cyclic early reference (module) or a same-scope forward
call observes the hoisted closure. Two bugs in that pre-compile:

- The `function*` star detection set is_generator but never
  is_user_generator, so is_sync_generator (is_generator && is_user_generator
  && !is_async) was always false for a hoisted top-level generator —
  instantiate_closure built it as a plain function, and calling it returned
  undefined instead of a Generator object.

- The `async function` detection captured `function`'s byte offset (not
  `async`'s) for the retained source span, then synthesized a literal
  "async " prefix at bind time. That loses whatever the source actually
  wrote between the two keywords (e.g. an inline comment) — toString on a
  hoisted async (generator) function declaration didn't roundtrip the exact
  source text (ES2019 §19.2.3.5).

(cherry picked from commit 60e13944e119b61261d162af7e634be9ef6ee003)

commits.subject: fix(module): resolve named imports and namespace members through full ResolveExport
commits.body:
Named-import binding installation and module-namespace-object member
resolution both only followed ONE level of `export { x } from` indirection
(resolve_export_local_name / resolve_export_binding_source), so a name
reachable only through `export * from` — including the star-cycle corpus,
where the direct path is a self-referencing re-export that must be skipped
in favor of the other star target — silently resolved to an undefined
accessor instead of the real binding.

Both call sites now run the full ResolveExport algorithm (16.2.1.6.3,
already implemented for validate_indirect_exports) first, falling back to
the old one-hop resolution only when it comes back unresolved/ambiguous.

Also makes collect_star_export_items detect genuine ambiguity (a name
reachable through two star exports with different owning bindings) and
omit it from the namespace object, instead of keeping whichever star
target was visited first (GetModuleNamespace §16.2.1.6.3 steps 9-10).

(cherry picked from commit 6033f4ca03e6a3da268c670bfd3459647e73b571)

commits.subject: fix(cli): link modules before executing in duktape_c3_debug -m
commits.body:
execute_module alone never resolves import bindings or instantiates
top-level function declarations (that happens in link_module,
ECMA-262 16.2.1.5.5 step 17); every other caller (run_module_file,
dynamic import) already links first. The debug CLI's `-m` module mode
skipped it, so a plain top-level `function foo(){}` (or any
cross-module import) was unreachable in its own module body even
though the exact same module ran correctly through the real test262
path.

(cherry picked from commit 95e5b3268608895b48302ed5b5fd6f3d18576ae6)

commits.subject: test262: print the thrown error message on a module-test FAIL
commits.body:
The worker only reported "FAIL: test source N bytes" for a runtime
throw, with no way to see what actually threw short of manually
reproducing the test outside the harness. Walk the thrown Error
object's shape chain for its `message` property and print it to
stderr alongside the FAIL line.

(cherry picked from commit ca28547a5c47901a62820efc037cef0987f3ed5e)

commits.subject: fix(compiler): support async functions in ESM export declarations
commits.body:
`export async function foo(){}` and `export default async function...`
were entirely unhandled (fell through to "unsupported export form" /
never matched the FUNCTION dispatch), and an anonymous
`export default function(){}` gave the function object the internal
compiler-private name "*default*" instead of the spec-mandated
runtime-visible name "default" (SetFunctionName, §14.1.20 step 4).

Reuses the existing match_async_function() lookahead (already used by
plain statement-position async function declarations) at both export
sites, threading is_async/is_constructable through to
compile_inner_function the same way function_declaration() does.

(cherry picked from commit cd10f75037572f754f75915938b158bc457db7da)

commits.subject: fix(module): make `import * as ns` namespace bindings immutable
commits.body:
ModuleDeclarationInstantiation creates an immutable binding for the
local name of `import * as ns` (ECMA-262 §16.2.1.6.2 step 8.b.ii). The
runtime instantiation path declared it as an ordinary mutable binding,
so `ns = anything` silently succeeded instead of throwing TypeError.

Adds env_declare_const (non-writable, enumerable — CreateImmutableBinding)
and uses it for the namespace-object binding in execute_module.

(cherry picked from commit 13912b8dbacda30f58c2bab554e4d39e1ea67c9b)

commits.subject: fix(vm): release this_binding on RET and clear stale Function.prototype.call slot
commits.body:
Enabling GC pressure in Heap.alloc_object (gc_trigger_counter decrement,
matching realloc/alloc) exposed a pre-existing missing decref-and-clear on
returning activations: RET/RETUNDEF release callee_act.this_binding's owned
reference (ACT_FLAG_THIS_OWNED) but never clear the slot afterward. Activation
slots are pooled by depth index and reused without zeroing, so the next call
landing on the same slot writes a new this_binding via tval_copy_ref, whose
own dst-decref fires a second time on the same stale bits — a double decref
that, once the object has been correctly mark-and-swept as unreachable in the
meantime, becomes a read of freed pool memory that corrupts the allocator's
intrusive free-list.

Three call sites had this gap: handle_return's two returns (vm_core.c3) and
the RET/RETUNDEF fast paths inlined into Vm.run (vm_execute.c3) for
performance. All three now clear this_binding to undefined after releasing
it, mirroring decref_callee_regs' existing "clear after release" convention.

Function.prototype.call's re-dispatch fallback (compiled/bound callees) had a
related but distinct gap: it moves thisArg from its original argument
register into the this-slot via a raw copy (no incref/decref, matching the
LIGHTFUNC/BUILTIN_FN branches above it) but, unlike those branches, never
clears the vacated argument register — a stale duplicate reference. Added the
matching tail-clear loop.

Restores the intended stress-test GC cadence in Heap.alloc_object.

(cherry picked from commit 05007aa01bf632baba797fd86e6e5b9f48e18fcd)

commits.subject: fix(compiler): allow yield/await in destructuring ASSIGNMENT pattern defaults
commits.body:
array_destructure_assign, object_destructure_assign, and the bare for-of/for-in
destructuring-pattern loop heads never touched in_formal_params, so a stale
true value (e.g. left set by an enclosing formal-parameter-list compile)
mis-applied the FormalParameter default-value gate in compile_default_expr to
these sites. Per ES2022 SS13.15.5.2/13.15.5.3 an AssignmentPattern's default
value is an AssignmentExpression, which permits yield in a generator and
await in an async context — unlike a FormalParameter default. This mirrors
the fix already applied to the declaration paths (array_destructure /
object_destructure) in commit 85f372ed; those four call sites were missed.

Fixes 32 test262 CE:unexpected failures across phases 2, 14, and 24.

commits.subject: fix(eval): stop pass-through result from under-decrefing this
commits.body:
eval is registered as a lightfunc, so when reached via Heap.call_fn
(vm_call_fn_impl's lightfunc dispatch) rather than an ordinary CALL,
ctx.result aliases the same register that was pre-seeded with a raw,
non-incref'd copy of `this` — the aliasing hazard already documented on
builtin_iterator_proto_symbol_iter. eval(x) for non-string x used
tval_copy_ref(ctx.result, arg), whose internal decref of ctx.result's
stale bits silently under-counted `this`'s refcount whenever eval ran
with an object thisArg via call/apply-style dispatch. Switch to a bare
incref + raw copy, matching the established fix for this pattern —
correct in every dispatch path, including the ordinary CALL path where
ctx.result starts undefined (decrefing undefined was already a no-op
there).

Audited every other builtins/ tval_copy_ref(ctx.result, ...) call site:
date.c3 (toJSON/[Symbol.toPrimitive]) and global.c3's evalScript are
registered as HObject builtins, not lightfuncs, so their ctx.result in
the risky dispatch path aliases the callee, not `this` — no
this-aliasing bug there without a coincidental same-object-as-callee
argument, left unchanged. error.c3's stack getter is confirmed safe:
invoke_getter's HObject accessor path builds this_val via
TVal.set_object (which increfs) before copying into the aliased slot,
so tval_copy_ref's decref exactly balances that incref (verified with a
live refcount trace).

(cherry picked from commit 65098c114ddedf96054e37ca7f3808654af2c6f0)

commits.subject: fix(function): set bound function .length before .name
commits.body:
Function.prototype.bind's own-property creation order didn't match spec:
SetFunctionLength (step 5) must run before the targetName Get/
SetFunctionName sequence (steps 6-9), but the code set .name first. This
only matters observably via Object.getOwnPropertyNames/Reflect.ownKeys,
which report own properties in creation order — qjs (and the spec) give
["length","name",...], we gave ["name","length"]. Move the length
computation and put_prop ahead of the name block.

(cherry picked from commit 6e1422ecece30badc72964614bc1d4f37c300304)

commits.subject: fix(error): stop .stack capture from fabricating [object Object]
commits.body:
Error.prototype.name is writable, so a user-supplied name whose value is
an object must never be stringified during error construction (the
error-stack-accessor capture runs before user code should ever observe
the new instance). builtin_to_string on an OBJECT silently produced
"[object Object]" without invoking the user's toString, which was both
wrong text and a step whose semantics don't match qjs (0 calls at
construction). Skip coercion for object-typed name values instead,
keeping the "Error" default; primitive name overrides are unaffected.

(cherry picked from commit d5bb7997659f2df183165772dd7f080dc63f82bb)

commits.subject: perf(strings): per-string cursor cache for non-ASCII indexing
commits.body:
char_at / char_offset_to_byte_offset walked CESU-8 from byte 0 on every
access, making non-ASCII string indexing O(n) per call. Adds a per-string
(char_offset, byte_offset) cursor plus backward scanning from the nearest
origin — string start, string end, or the cursor — so sequential and
near-sequential access resume instead of restarting.

Measured on an 8k non-ASCII string, 2000 ops:
  sequential scan  90.3 ms -> 0.45 ms
  s[i]             16.7 ms -> 0.09 ms
  charAt           16.8 ms -> 0.16 ms
  charCodeAt       16.8 ms -> 0.12 ms
  slice            10.5 ms -> 0.20 ms
ASCII paths unchanged (already O(1) via the is_ascii flag).

Also lands the Phase 25 ESM wiring (language/module-code, import, export)
and routes module detection off the test path rather than a source scan.
That phase reports 31 fail / 14 CE — the module work is unfinished and its
failures are left visible rather than skip-listed.

Two things from the working tree are deliberately NOT included:

- The heap-level 4-entry strcache was dead code: strcache_resolve was never
  called from anywhere, and on a hit it merely delegated to
  char_offset_to_byte_offset, which already consults the per-string cursor.
  It held raw HString pointers for no benefit, so it is removed.

- An added gc_trigger_counter decrement in Heap.alloc_object is dropped. It
  is correct in itself, but it exposes a pre-existing missing temproot:
  clean HEAD plus that single line crashes Array.prototype.toLocaleString
  over a TypedArray under allocation pressure (SIGBUS in FixedBlockPool.alloc
  via hobject_alloc). That bug predates this work and needs its own fix; the
  GC stress constants stay at 1/1.

All 18 phases 0 fails, golden 10/10, rosetta 100/100, 0 leaks.

commits.body:

commits.subject: hstring: cache char_length, shrink registry_slot to uint
commits.body:

non-ASCII strings. Add a cached_charlen field, computed lazily on first
call and never invalidated (strings are immutable).

registry_slot only ever holds an index into the large-string registry,
bounded by a uint counter — shrink it from usz to uint so the new field
costs zero extra header bytes (HString::size unchanged at 24 bytes).

commits.subject: vm: clear new_target on generator/async resume activations
commits.body:
vm.activations[] slots are a fixed array reused across pushes without
being zeroed, so a generator's resume activation (built manually in
the CALL dispatch's generator-resume branch, separately from the
ordinary call-setup path that already assigns new_target on every
other frame kind) could observe whatever new_target a prior activation
at the same array index had left there — e.g. a generator resumed
from deep inside an ambient `new Ctor()` call chain leaked that
constructor's new.target into `new.target` reads inside the resumed
generator body.

Generator/async function objects have no [[Construct]] (ES2015 §14.4),
so new.target must always read undefined on resume; setting
new_act_r.new_target = null unconditionally is correct for every case,
not just a guard for a specific caller shape.

(cherry picked from commit 82c32600db9eed18dec92468adf32a9e36ed3f93)

commits.subject: function: store bound-function internals off the property table
commits.body:
Object.getOwnPropertyNames(f.bind(null)) (and Reflect.ownKeys) leaked
"\x00bound_target", "\x00bound_this", "\x00bound_args" — bind() stored
[[BoundTargetFunction]]/[[BoundThis]]/[[BoundArguments]] as NUL-prefixed
"internal" own properties, but getOwnPropertyNames/ownKeys don't filter
on enumerability so the disguise doesn't hide them from either API.

Follows the same fix commit 643ecbd5 used for Error's captured stack:
move the data out of the property table entirely, onto real struct
fields (HObjectFunction.bound_target/bound_this/bound_args, active only
when flags.is_bound) instead of a separate HObjectExtra union variant —
bound functions are ObjClass.FUNCTION and every generic call-dispatch
site reads builtin_fn_index through HObjectFunction without checking
is_bound first, so a union variant would need HObjectProxy-style
offset-matching padding to keep that field aligned; plain extra fields
avoid that entirely at the cost of 24 bytes on every FUNCTION-class
object.

Updates the two other call-dispatch sites that read the old internal
properties directly (Function.prototype[Symbol.hasInstance]'s
[[BoundTargetFunction]] unwrap, and vm_construct_fn_impl's `new
boundFn()` argument-prepending path) to read the new fields, and
reorders bind() to populate bound_target/bound_this before setting
is_bound so a GC triggered by the bound-arguments array allocation
never observes an is_bound object with unpopulated (zero-bit, not a
valid TVal) fields.

(cherry picked from commit fd39f87d397f7241a7033bda2ef8144e02cbc4c4)

commits.subject: date: floor negative ms->sec conversions for correct pre-1970 fields
commits.body:
new Date(-1).getUTCFullYear() (and friends) returned 1970 instead of
1969 because every ms->whole-seconds conversion in date.c3 used C's
truncating (long) cast, which rounds toward zero instead of flooring
toward -infinity. For time_val=-1, that landed on second 0 instead of
second -1, shifting every negative-time calendar field by one unit.

Introduces date_ms_to_sec/date_floor_mod_field helpers and applies
them to every civil-calendar breakdown and current-field extraction
(getters, toISOString/toString family, and the setSeconds/setMinutes/
setHours/setDate/setMonth/setFullYear "keep other fields" fallback
paths, local and UTC). The local<->UTC timezone-offset lookup key
specifically keeps truncation (not floor) to match the reference
engine's getTimezoneOffset input, since flooring there can flip which
side of a sub-minute historical Local-Mean-Time transition an ancient
date's lookup lands on; the spec leaves pre-Unix-epoch timezone
behavior implementation-defined, so matching the reference choice
there is what parity requires, not "more correct" flooring.

Also fixes six setDate/setMonth/setFullYear/setUTC* sites that derived
the millisecond field to preserve via a bare `(long)tv % 1000` with no
negative-remainder fixup, which silently produced negative ms fields
for any Date with a negative time value.

commits.subject: builtins: collapse enum/metadata/dispatch triple registration onto Builtin enum
commits.body:
Every builtin required three coordinated edits (enum ordinal, name/arity
metadata switch arm, dispatch-table entry), a recurring merge-conflict
magnet. C3 enums support associated values (`enum Builtin : uint (String
js_name, int js_arity, BuiltinFunc handler) { FOO {"foo", 1, &builtin_foo}, }`)
resolvable at compile time via `$foreach ... : Builtin::values:`, so all three
now derive from one line per builtin. builtin_get_metadata() reads the
associated values directly instead of switching on ordinal; the dispatch
table is populated once at startup by an `@init` constructor instead of a
hand-written designated initializer, with identical generated code at the
call site (verified via LLVM IR — same flat array load + indirect call, no
added branch). bench_function_call/ic_monomorphic/array medians are at parity
with baseline (well within run-to-run noise). All 18 test262 phases, golden
bytecode, and rosetta suites remain green.

commits.subject: hobject: combine incref/decref heap-allocation checks in put_prop/set_array_idx
commits.body:
6d7e71ca's overwrite path tested val.is_heap_allocated() and pv.is_heap_allocated()
as two independent branches, each re-loading _active_heap, even though the
overwhelming common case (numeric/boolean writes) needs neither. Add
types::either_heap_allocated(), a single OR'd test over both TVals, and gate
the whole incref/decref block on it. This collapses two branches plus a
duplicated _active_heap load into one combined test when neither side is
heap-allocated, while keeping the incref-before-decref self-assignment
ordering and the exact heap-over-nonheap/nonheap-over-heap/heap-over-heap
behavior unchanged for every case where either side IS heap-allocated.

Verification: all 18 test262 phases at 0 fails, golden-bytecode 10/10,
rosetta 100/100, and leaks --atExit clean (0 leaks) on cycle, self-cycle,
closure-heavy, generator-heavy, and array-mutation-heavy stress scripts,
matching the 6d7e71ca baseline exactly.

Wall-clock A/B on this run was too noisy (shared machine, load average
5-60 during testing) to cleanly separate signal from system contention;
median-of-many-interleaved-runs put bench_object at ~456ms pre-refcount,
~466ms post-refcount, ~463ms with this change (roughly a third of the
regression recovered), with the isolated fastint-only prop-write loop
inside the noise floor either way. The branch reduction itself is real
and unconditional regardless of what wall-clock could resolve.

commits.subject: hobject: refcount object/buffer values in property and array slots
commits.body:
put_prop and set_array_idx previously incref/decref'd only string and
BigInt values, relying on mark-and-sweep alone to keep object-valued
property/array edges alive. A value reachable solely through such an
edge could be freed the instant its producing register decref'd, before
M&S ever discovered it was still live via a sibling reference (e.g. a
closure's lex_env chain) — this was the root cause of the sole
remaining test262 failure, built-ins/Iterator/from/return-method-calls-
base-return-method.js.

Extend both writers to treat all is_heap_allocated() values uniformly,
incref-then-decref to survive self-assignment, and make hobject_free's
teardown loop symmetric. The existing sweep guard in Heap.decref (skip
decref into an unmarked, non-temproot neighbour during Heap.sweep) was
already exercised by object-valued edges elsewhere — getter/setter
cells, captured `this`, promise results, iterator targets — so this is
not new territory; cycles are still reclaimed by mark-and-sweep only.

Auditing every writer into a property/array slot surfaced a family of
pre-existing gaps that the new object refcounting would otherwise turn
into real leaks or premature frees:
- HObject.seal() abandons the dense array part after copying entries
  into the named-property table; the abandoned slot's own reference is
  now released.
- HObject.delete_prop() never released the deleted slot's reference
  (previously only leaked strings/BigInts permanently; now would also
  leak objects).
- Four accessor-definition sites in object.c3 called put_prop with a
  placeholder value, anchoring a reference, then overwrote the same
  slot with a GetterSetter cell without releasing the placeholder's ref.
- Two array-to-named-property promotion sites in object.c3 abandoned a
  dense array slot without releasing its reference.
- Map/WeakMap's getOrInsertComputed re-search overwrite and Set's
  difference/symmetricDifference tombstoning wrote/cleared slots
  without incref/decref.
- coll_delete's tombstone path decref'd only strings, missing BigInt
  and (now) objects.

Map/WeakMap's coll_set_entry and coll_get_or_insert_computed value
overwrites intentionally do NOT route through set_array_idx: that slot
is already counted in array_used, and undefined is a legitimate stored
value there (not a hole), so set_array_idx's undefined-transition
bookkeeping would corrupt the scan bound for later inserts.

Verification: all 18 test262 phases at 0 fails (including the
previously-failing Iterator test), golden-bytecode 10/10, rosetta
100/100, and leaks --atExit clean (0 leaks, RSS at parity with
baseline) across cycle/closure/generator/collection-mutation stress
scripts. bench-fast shows a real, consistent ~9% regression isolated on
a pure fastint property-overwrite loop and ~4% on the mixed
bench_object suite, from the extra is_heap_allocated() branch now on
every property write — read-heavy benchmarks (bench_ic_monomorphic,
bench_property_lookup, bench_shape_stress) are at parity.

commits.subject: iterator: fix under-refcount in %IteratorPrototype%[@@iterator]
commits.body:
The builtin's result register aliases `this_val` already (every call
convention seeds the result/this slot with a raw, non-incref'd copy
before the builtin runs). tval_copy_ref's decref-old/incref-new pattern
can't detect this aliasing (dst and src are different TVal locations
holding the same heap object), so it silently cancelled the incref it
had just performed and returned an under-refcounted reference — freed
one decref too early by the caller.

Surfaced as a hang in built-ins/Iterator/prototype/take: repeated
Array.from(gen().take(n)) calls each leaked one decref's worth of
imbalance, eventually double-freeing/aliasing the generator's iterator
identity. Fix mirrors set_object's plain-incref convention, extended to
every heap-allocated tag (not just OBJECT) since %IteratorPrototype%'s
@@iterator must return primitives (Symbol, BigInt, ...) unchanged too.

commits.subject: backlog: close runner desync and the I4 gate recipe
commits.body:
b0338a09 fixes the desync: Worker.alive read `poll() is None`, but poll()
only reflects a SIGKILL once the kernel reaps the process. A killed-but-
unreaped worker still read as alive+idle, so the scheduler handed it a new
test on the same pipe its previous verdict was still in flight on. An
explicit _killed flag closes the window. Two full suite runs now complete;
the desync reproduced 3/3 before and 0/6 after under forced mass timeouts.

I4's recipe is landed as `just test262-gate` (opt-in, parses the summary line
rather than the exit code, since run_test262.py always exits 0). What remains
of I4 is only the hosting decision, which is genuinely the user's.

New item: the RegExp property-escapes generated tests time out under load,
which would make the gate flaky if wired into CI as-is.

commits.subject: test262_runner: fix timeout-kill/reuse race causing worker verdict desync
commits.body:
A SIGKILLed worker's `alive` property still read True until the kernel
reaped it, so the "assign idle workers" step could hand it a new test
before the dead-worker sweep replaced it — sending on stdin to an
already-dead process while its previous test's verdict was still landing
on the same pipe. The next read then paired that stale verdict with the
newly-assigned path, tripping the desync guard mid-suite.

kill() now sets a `_killed` flag that `alive` checks immediately, so a
just-killed worker is excluded from both reuse and result-collection the
instant it's killed, not just once poll() confirms it. Reproduced
deterministically by forcing mass timeouts (temporarily, not committed)
and confirmed fixed across repeated stress runs and two full-suite runs
(one of which reproduced the exact original crash's timeout family:
RegExp property-escapes generated tests).

Also adds `just test262-gate`, an opt-in two-consecutive-run zero-fail
check (scripts/test262_gate.sh) for backlog item I4.

commits.subject: hobject: free GeneratorState on generator finalize, fixing 2-alloc/call leak
commits.body:
hobject_free never released a generator's GeneratorState (generator_data)
or its saved_regs array — the only free path was the mark-phase GC walk,
which keeps the struct alive but never tears it down. Every generator
that runs GEN_START (called at least once) leaked its GeneratorState
(224 bytes) plus saved_regs (proportional to register count) for the
life of the process, regardless of whether the generator ran to
completion, was abandoned mid-iteration, or threw.

Only saved_regs[] and this_binding are ever incref'd onto the struct
(via tval_copy_ref); every other field is a transient/borrowed value,
so the fix decrefs just those two before freeing. The allocations still
need freeing during full-heap teardown even though _active_heap is
cleared first (Heap.destroy() disables it before the decref pass), so
the free calls fall back to mem::free the same way prop_hash does.

Verified with `leaks --atExit` across Array.from(gen), spread, new
Map/Set(gen), for-of, abandoned/early-break, throw-mid-iteration,
AggregateError(gen), and yield* delegation — all now 0 leaks (was 1000
leaks/128000 bytes per 500 iterations). Promise.all(gen) still leaks,
but reproduces identically with a plain array argument — it's the
pre-existing async/await GeneratorState leak (shared between the
resume/reject reaction closures), not a generator-iterator bug, and is
out of scope here.

[[DefineOwnProperty]] on the receiver, which must fire a Proxy's
defineProperty trap. INITPROP/INITPROPN previously always used the raw
put_prop fast path, silently bypassing the trap when the class-field
receiver was a Proxy. Now hobj.flags.exotic_proxyobj gates a call into
object_define_own (the same MOP dispatcher Reflect.defineProperty and
Array.fromAsync already use); ordinary receivers keep the untouched
fast path. Un-skips the two test262 cases documenting this gap.

commits.subject: builtins: fix ToString/ToPropertyKey abrupt-completion gaps found in a builtin_to_string audit
commits.body:
Audited every call site of the raw builtin_to_string helper (which cannot
run user code or throw) to find places where the spec actually requires
ToPrimitive/ToString/ToPropertyKey — most sites already dispatch objects
through the VM-aware builtin_to_string_vm and only fall back to the raw
helper for already-resolved primitives, which is correct. Four sites did
not:

- Array.prototype.sort's default (no comparefn) compare path: vm_to_string
  signals a thrown toString/valueOf via vm.throw_pending + a plain `null`
  return, not a C3 fault, so the existing `?? builtin_to_string(...)`
  fallback silently swallowed the throw and coerced the still-live object
  via the raw "[object Object]" path, leaving throw_pending stuck set —
  corrupting VM state and segfaulting later in the same run. Now checks
  throw_pending after each vm_to_string call and propagates via
  ctx.should_throw.

- Date.parse on a non-string argument used raw ToString instead of
  builtin_to_string_vm, silently coercing objects to "[object Object]"
  instead of invoking toString/valueOf (or propagating their throw).

- Object.fromEntries's key coercion mishandled Symbol *wrapper objects*
  (`Object(Symbol(...))`): ToPropertyKey must unwrap to the underlying
  Symbol and use it directly as the key, but the code ran the object
  through builtin_to_string's OBJECT case (always "[object Object]",
  despite a stale comment claiming it produced "Symbol(description)"),
  installing a bogus string key instead of a symbol key.

- TypedArray.prototype.toLocaleString hand-rolled a partial ToPrimitive
  (toString then valueOf) that fell through to builtin_to_string on a
  still-unresolved object when both methods were absent or returned
  objects, instead of throwing TypeError. Replaced with a call to the
  already-correct builtin_to_string_vm.

commits.subject: regexp: fix source over-escaping of already-escaped and in-class `/`
commits.body:
EscapeRegExpPattern (§22.2.6.10, used by RegExp.prototype.source and
.toString) unconditionally escaped every `/` byte, so an already-escaped
`\/` became `\\/` and a `/` inside a character class (which needs no
escaping there) also got escaped — e.g. `/a\/b/.source` produced `"a\\/b"`
and `/[/]/.source` produced `"[\/]"` instead of the spec-correct `"a\/b"`
and `"[/]"`. escape_regexp_pattern now tracks character-class state (`[`/`]`)
and copies existing backslash-escape pairs verbatim instead of re-scanning
their second byte, so only a bare `/` outside a class gets escaped.
toString() had its own duplicate (and equally buggy) inline copy of this
logic; it now calls the shared helper instead.

commits.subject: lexer: fix `x++ / 2` misparsed as regexp literal
commits.body:
prev_was_operand() did not treat postfix `++`/`--` as ending an operand, so
`/` immediately after `x++` was lexed as the start of a regexp literal
instead of division, raising a SyntaxError on code like `x++ / 2`. Add
TokenType.INC/DEC to the operand-ending set — a `++`/`--` seen right after an
operand can only be the postfix form (prefix would already have been
consumed before the operand), so this is unconditionally correct.

commits.body:

non-object or non-generator `this` instead of throwing TypeError per

catcher for a finally_pc without walking to an enclosing one, and (for

commits.subject: error: implement AggregateError per spec, fix undefined=12 parse rejection
commits.body:
AggregateError previously stored the errors argument verbatim instead of
running IterableToList (§20.5.7.1.1), used the non-ToPrimitive
builtin_to_string for message (swallowing throwing toString/valueOf), and
register_native_error_ctor hardcoded length=1 for every native error
constructor even though AggregateError.length must be 2.

`undefined = 12` was rejected as a parse-time SyntaxError because the
compiler special-cased the `undefined` identifier as a literal-push
(LDUNDEF) alongside true/false/null, clearing last_was_getvar and tripping
the invalid-assignment-target check. Unlike true/false/null, `undefined` is
an ordinary identifier bound to a non-writable global property, so it must
fall through to normal identifier resolution and let the existing
non-writable-global runtime check produce a TypeError, matching NaN and
Infinity (which were never special-cased and already worked correctly).

commits.subject: uri: reject lone surrogates in encode/decode, fix ToString on object args
commits.body:

letting a surrogate half's 3-byte sequence escape unpaired instead of
throwing URIError (ES §19.2.6.5 Encode requires a Unicode code point, and

engine's CESU-8 surrogate-pair form.

"[object Object]" for any object instead of running ToPrimitive first;
route them through the existing builtin_to_string_vm (already used by
parseInt, Array.join, Error, Function.toString, etc.) instead of adding a
second ToString implementation.

decodeURIComponent; the 12 remaining phase-8 failures are pre-existing

commits.subject: lexer: fix regexp literals starting with `=`
commits.body:
`/=` was unconditionally routed to the DIV_ASSIGN punctuator regardless of
whether a regexp literal was syntactically expected, so `/=/` and `/=a/`

it, `#x /= y` on a private field would be misparsed as `#x` followed by a
regexp literal instead of a division-assign.

commits.subject: test262: add 14 orphaned directories to PHASES
commits.body:
Wires up ~718 previously-invisible test262 tests (13 directories, on-disk
.js counts) into the phase runner so "0 fails" claims actually cover
them. Placed thematically: computed-property-names into Phase 3,
literals/bigint into Phase 5 (with BigInt), literals/regexp + URI
functions + global into Phase 8, AggregateError into Phase 17-20, and
the remaining generator/iterator prototypes into Phase 21.

Result: 651 pass, 67 fail across the newly-run tests, grouped by root
cause:

- language/literals/regexp (12 fail): `/=/ ` and other regexp literals
  starting with a char that could begin a `/=` punctuator are lexed as
  division-assign instead of a regexp literal — `!prev_was_operand()`
  guard is short-circuited by `peek_char_at(1) != '='`.
- built-ins/encodeURI + encodeURIComponent (16 fail): lone (unpaired)
  surrogates are encoded instead of throwing URIError.
- built-ins/decodeURI + decodeURIComponent (3 fail): 2 fails from
  builtin_to_string()'s OBJECT case hardcoding "[object Object]"
  instead of invoking ToPrimitive/toString/valueOf; 1 from the same
  lone-surrogate-should-throw gap as encodeURI.
- built-ins/global (1 fail): `undefined = 12` under strict mode is
  parse-rejected (Invalid LHS) instead of parsing and throwing a
  runtime TypeError on the write, per spec.
- built-ins/AggregateError (7 fail): length is 1 instead of 2 (ctor
  registration hardcodes length via register_native_error_ctor); the
  `errors` argument is stored as-is instead of iterator-spread via
  IterableToList; `message` uses the same naive builtin_to_string
  instead of spec ToString, so abrupt completions from a custom
  toString/valueOf never propagate.
- built-ins/RegExpStringIteratorPrototype (13 fail): no dedicated
  %RegExpStringIteratorPrototype% object exists — `.next` is added as
  an own property on every iterator instance, `[[Prototype]]` points
  straight at %IteratorPrototype%, and `[Symbol.toStringTag]` is never
  set, so ancestry/toStringTag/prop-desc tests all fail.
- built-ins/GeneratorPrototype (10 fail): next/return/throw don't
  validate `this` carries a generator's internal state (TypeError
  expected, none thrown); 3 tests show `.return()` inside nested
  try/finally not running the finally block / not yielding the
  ultimate return value.
- built-ins/ArrayIteratorPrototype (3 fail): `.next` is missing its own
  `.length`/`.name` properties — same ad-hoc-construction gap as the
  RegExpStringIterator case.
- built-ins/GeneratorFunction (1 fail): `.prototype.constructor` is
  writable; should be non-writable.
- built-ins/AsyncFunction (1 fail): constructor's [[Prototype]] isn't
  wired to Function correctly.

language/literals/regexp intentionally also carries the pre-known
early-err-*/$DONOTEVALUATE failures (this engine never parse-time-
validates regexp literals) called out in the SKIP_GLOBS comment above —
those are folded into the 12 fails above, not a separate cause.

No SKIP_FILES/SKIP_GLOBS/UNSUPPORTED_PATTERN entries added; nothing
hidden. No engine code touched — just-golden-bytecode (10/10) and
just-rosetta (100/100) both pass unchanged.

commits.subject: error: implement error-stack-accessor proposal, un-skip 35 test262 tests
commits.body:
Error.prototype.stack is now an accessor pair (get/set), not an own data
property on each instance: { enumerable: false, configurable: true }.
The getter returns undefined unless `this` carries the [[ErrorData]] slot
(keyed on ObjClass.ERROR); the setter is
SetterThatIgnoresPrototypeProperties(this, %Error.prototype%, "stack", v)
per the proposal, throwing on Error.prototype itself and on non-String
values, and creating/overwriting an own data property otherwise (routed
through the real [[Set]]/[[DefineOwnProperty]] MOPs so Proxy traps fire
correctly).

The stack string captured at construction time moves out of the property
table entirely, into a new HObjectError.captured_stack field (ERROR
objects now share FUNCTION's larger allocation size class to make room).
An earlier attempt to hide it behind a NUL-prefixed internal property key
leaked through Object.getOwnPropertyNames/Reflect.ownKeys (that API does
not filter on enumerability) and regressed two previously-passing
test262 Object.create tests — moving it out of the property table
entirely fixes both the leak and the regression.

commits.subject: fusion: don't mistake CALL_VAR/CALL_GLOBAL argc and name index for registers
commits.body:
The three fusion liveness scans treated every field of an ABC-format
instruction as a register operand, but CALL_VAR/CALL_GLOBAL encode B as an
argument count and C as a name-constant index (vm_calls.c3: `nargs = insn.b`,
callee resolved by name). A scratch register whose number happened to equal an
argc or a constant index was therefore reported live, silently blocking the
fusion that would have consumed it.

The direction was correctness-safe — a spurious "live" only declines an
optimization — but it cost real fusions. Minimal repro: three-argument call in
a loop whose global-copy scratch lands in r3 collides with `argc=3`, so
`GETGLOBAL_PRIM r3,1 ; PUTGLOBAL_PRIM r3,0` fails to fuse; with this fix it
becomes MOVE_GG.

Factored the operand-read question into fusion_abc_reads_reg, which also
absorbs the GETPROPC carve-out that cmp_result_live_from already had (C is a
key-constant index there) and which run_move_gg_fusion was missing. CALL_S is
deliberately NOT carved out: it does decode C as a register
(`ds.regs_base + insn.c`).

Also adds test/test_loop_preheader.js, 29 control-flow cases over loop shapes
(continue/break plain and labeled, nested loops, body-mutated counter and
bound, coercing and NaN bounds, throw from body and from the condition,
let-scoped counters and their per-iteration closures, try/finally around and
inside the loop, switch body). 28 of 29 match QuickJS exactly;
try_finally_break is pinned at this engine's current 203 rather than the
spec-correct 103 — `finally` runs twice when `break` exits a for-loop inside
the try, a pre-existing bug reproduced at 03d773bc, recorded so the value is
held still rather than silently absorbed later.

byte-identical.

commits.subject: heap: free each compiled function's name and retained source text
commits.body:
CompiledFunction.name_ptr and .src_ptr are heap copies taken out of the
compiler's scratch buffers so they outlive the compile, but nothing ever
released them: free_compiled_funcs handled code, constants, inner_funcs,
line_table, IC entries, the regexp cache and the eval private-name snapshot,
and stopped there. Every function compiled at runtime therefore leaked,
which is a plain public-API leak and not a test-runner artifact:

    new Function("a","return a;") x1000 -> 1000 leaks / 48 KB
    eval("function g(){}")         x1000 -> 2000 leaks / 48 KB
    eval("class C{ m(){} }")       x1000 -> 4000 leaks / 80 KB
    eval("var x=1;")               x1000 -> 0

All of those are now 0. The batch runner recompiles its harness plus a test
per cycle, so it was the loudest consumer rather than the cause: worker RSS
growth over 1000 reset cycles drops 33.54 -> 0.19 KB/cycle, flat at 6.5 MB.
Single-file module run: 16 leaks/944 B -> 3/160 B.

filename_ptr is deliberately left alone — stamp_module_filename hands the
module's normalized specifier to every nested function, so it is borrowed.
make_default_constructor allocated its name through the heap allocator while

commits.subject: test262_runner: stop timeouts stalling the pool; scale workers with CPU count
commits.body:
Speed:
- Default workers 3 -> cpus-2 (capped 12); the hard cap 4 -> cpu count. The
  old cap guarded against OOM from N VM heaps, but each worker is already held
  to a 3 GB ceiling, so total memory is bounded and the CPU count is the real
  limit. Phase 5: 29.1s -> 21.8s.
- kill() no longer blocks on wait(). It used to SIGKILL + reap + respawn inline
  in the scheduler loop, so every timeout and memkill froze *all* workers for a
  process teardown plus a VM startup. Timeouts now cost one worker. Respawn is
  consolidated into the existing dead-worker sweep, which is now the single
  path for timeouts, memory kills, and genuine crashes.
- Drop the per-readable-fd linear scan over the pool for an fd -> worker dict.
- deque + popleft() for the test queue; pop(0) was O(n) per test.
- Skip the RSS `ps` sample entirely where RLIMIT_AS works, capping the worker's
  address space at spawn instead. Darwin refuses to lower RLIMIT_AS (as does
  `ulimit -v`), so it keeps sampling; the probe tries an actual lowered value,
  since re-setting the current limit succeeds there and proves nothing.

Correctness:
- try_read_result() could hang the whole run. select() promises some bytes, not
  a whole line, so readline() on the pipe blocked on a partial write or on a
  worker SIGKILLed mid-line, with no timeout to break out. Now reads with
  os.read into the previously-vestigial self._buf and only yields a verdict on
  a complete line.
- A worker answering with a path other than the one it was sent silently
  relabelled the verdict, hiding exactly the stdin/stdout desync this corpus
  exists to catch. Now raises.
- send_test() tolerates a worker dying before it takes the test, instead of
  raising BrokenPipeError out of the scheduler.

Retries are unchanged and still off by default. Verified: phases 2 and 5 give
byte-identical per-test verdicts vs. the previous script, phase 2 also under
--shuffle at 6 workers; timeout and memkill paths exercised with hang and
runaway-allocation fixtures.

commits.subject: strings: give every HString an owner so heap reset can free it
commits.body:
Symbols were allocated through hstring_alloc and then deliberately left out
of the string table (a Symbol is unique, so a content-keyed table would
conflate distinct Symbols sharing a description). They were not put on the
large-string registry either, so they belonged to no list at all: neither
Heap.reset() nor Heap.destroy() had any way to reach them, and every Symbol
ever created leaked. register_builtins recreates the well-known Symbols on
each reset, so a long-lived worker leaked them once per cycle.

Register them on the large-string registry instead — the list that exists
precisely for non-interned strings that still need an owner. decref already
routes non-interned strings to large_string_unregister, so the slot is
released correctly when a Symbol dies normally.

The same audit found ~39 hand-rolled copies of "look up, else allocate and
insert" across the builtins. All of them inserted into the string table
without marking the string interned or taking the table's reference, so a
string that later hit refcount zero unhooked itself from the large-string
registry (a no-op) rather than from the table, leaving a dangling table
entry. Fold the ownership transfer into str_table_insert, which now reports
whether it took the string, and collapse the duplicated blocks onto
Heap.str_intern.

Measured on a 4000-cycle worker run over a fixed script: heap-owned bytes
leaked per reset 640 -> 0, live HStrings leaked per reset 13 -> 0.

and the for-of hole yields undefined. Full suite 41830/0, golden 10/10

commits.subject: compiler: fix stale ident_buf borrows corrupting declared binding names
commits.body:
An escaped identifier (`\u{62}`) decodes through the lexer's slow path
into a single shared scratch buffer (ident_buf) and returns a borrow
over it. Many declaration-site call paths stored that borrow directly
into a longer-lived structure — scope_stack (declare_var), a class's
methods[] table, or a module's import/export/func_decl tables — without
interning it first. Any later identifier scan in the same function/
module (a second escaped param, a body-local var, another import) then
overwrites the shared buffer, silently corrupting the earlier name so
it no longer compares equal to itself at resolution time.

Fixes (same shape as ee740c2d, generalized): function/method/arrow
parameters (including rest and default-expression name inference),
hoisted `var` declarations, `var`/`let`/`const` declarators, for-in/
for-of/for(;;) loop head bindings, catch is handled separately (already
forced through env), class declaration/expression names, class method
names (read again after the body compiles), named function expressions
(name read only after body compiles, for `.name`), and module import/
export bindings (read back at link time, after the whole module compiles).

Left unfixed as already safe: destructuring bind names (copied into a
fixed-size buffer at parse time), private class names (intern_slot_name
already used), inferred names (copied into a fixed CompilerContext
buffer), and `export {...}`/`export default class` (previously fixed).
Noted but out of scope: `#\u{...}` escaped private-name syntax isn't
decoded at all (pre-existing, unrelated gap).

(cherry picked from commit 5c85967a32536148a2fb0a5dcb0b40673a57fba5)

commits.subject: vm: fuse GETGLOBAL_PRIM+JMP_LT into JMP_LT_G superinstruction
commits.body:
A `for (i = 0; i < N; i++)` loop over globals ends each iteration with
`GETGLOBAL_PRIM rX, N` / `JMP_LT off, rI, rX` — the bound is loaded into a
scratch register purely to be compared and discarded. A dynamic opcode census
over the benchmark suite (670M executed ops) put this pair at 5.84% of all
dispatches, the third-hottest adjacent pair.

Fuse it into a two-word JMP_LT_G mirroring MOVE_GG: word 1 is ABC (A = the
jump offset, B = the surviving register operand), word 2 is a kept NOP whose
BC holds the global's name index. The VM reads both words, advances pc by 2,
and compares against the slot value directly — no scratch register, one
dispatch instead of two. The global's read IC lives in the trailing word's
otherwise-unused per-PC VarICEntry slot. Comparison semantics (fastint, double,
relational coercion, NaN) are JMP_LT's exactly; the threaded VM has no handler
so it bails to the switch.

Safety mirrors run_move_gg_fusion: strict adjacency, the trailing word must not
be a jump target, and the scratch register must be dead on BOTH the
fall-through and taken-branch paths. The stored offset carries over unchanged —
the original JMP_LT sits at slot i+1 and branches relative to (i+1)+1, while
JMP_LT_G sits at slot i and branches relative to i+2, the same base. NOP
compaction gets a matching remap case using that two-word base.

bench_arithmetic -2.9%, bench_function_call -2.1% (best-of-9, interleaved).

1696 pass / 0 fail.

commits.subject: vm: drop hot-path register decrefs now that the sweep can reclaim them
commits.body:
The constant loads, global increments, allocation opcodes and call-callee
resolution released the destination register's old reference before their raw
writes, because a large non-interned string dropped there had no collector
that could ever find it again. The large-string registry closes that gap, so
these opcodes go back to raw writes and a missed reference degrades from a
permanent leak to a block reclaimed at the next safepoint GC.

Reverted: LDINT/LDUNDEF/LDNULL/LDTRUE/LDFALSE, INC_GLOBAL/DEC_GLOBAL entry,
NEWOBJ/NEWARR/NEWREGEXP/CLOSURE, and the resolve_call_var/resolve_call_global
entry decrefs. The `ra.set_undefined()` clears stay wherever a GC can trigger
before the result lands — those are stale-pointer safety, not ownership.

Kept: the INC/DEC slow-path decrefs (already behind a vm_to_number coercion
that dwarfs them, and they keep `str++` collecting promptly), free_catcher_chain,
the ADD/ADDI and RET track_heap_store additions, and the MAX_CALLS borrowed-callee
neutralization — none are register-write overhead on a hot path.

commits.subject: heap: register large non-interned strings for GC and reset teardown
commits.body:
Strings over MAX_INTERN_BYTES never enter the string table, so neither the
table sweep nor heap reset could see them: they were pure refcounted leaves
with no backstop, and any missed decref leaked the block permanently while
heap.reset() left every live one stranded between batch runs.

Track them in a heap-side registry instead — a growable pointer array with
each string recording its own slot, so registration is an append and removal
an O(1) swap with the last entry:

- HString.next carried the string-table chain, which the open-addressed table
  never used; it becomes registry_slot, keeping the header at 24 bytes.
  `hash` stays the content hash — equals_hstring fast-rejects non-interned
  strings with it, so a registry index cannot live there.
- mark_and_sweep clears registry marks in phase 1 and sweeps unreachable
  entries in phase 3b, under the same string_sweep_safe gate as the table.
  The registry holds no reference of its own, so reachability alone decides:
  a string the mark phase missed is dead whatever its refcount says.
- decref unregisters on free, mirroring the interned str_table_remove.
- reset() and destroy() drain the registry, releasing strings that no other
  list can reach.
- ensure_interned hands a promoted string over to the table.

Phase 0 1696/0, phase 5 8361/0, rosetta 100/100, golden bytecode 10/10.
leaks on a 2000-iteration large-concat workload: 16/1520B -> 15/880B.

commits.subject: gc: keep temproots alive across safepoints inside native builtin frames
commits.body:
A safepoint GC cleared every temproot flag on the premise that at a safe
point nothing is in flight. That premise does not hold when a native
builtin re-enters the VM: Array.prototype.map allocates its result array
via ArraySpeciesCreate, holds it only in a raw C3 local, then calls the
user callback. The nested execution hits backward-jump and call
safepoints, the mark phase cannot see the builtin's local, and the result
array is swept mid-loop. The next write to it found a recycled header with
extensible cleared and threw "Cannot add property to non-extensible
object".

Track native builtin nesting depth at the dispatch_builtin chokepoint and
suppress both temproot clearing and string-table sweeping while it is
non-zero. The collection still runs and still reclaims anything the mark
phase proves dead; only the two passes that rely on the quiescence
assumption are deferred to a genuinely quiet safepoint.

The same exposure applies to every builtin that allocates and then
re-enters the VM (filter, flatMap, splice, Array.from, ...), and to raw
interned HString* locals, so the fix is at the GC layer rather than in map.

commits.subject: eval: apply CreateGlobalFunctionBinding descriptor rules to global fn decls
commits.body:

the runtime could not tell CreateGlobalVarBinding (§9.1.1.4.17: leave an

over a non-configurable global property flipped it back to configurable.

env_declare_global_func. It matches DECLVAR for a declarative var_env and
follows §9.1.1.4.18 when var_env is the global Environment Record.

commits.subject: fix: share growable private-name table across borrowing contexts
commits.body:
The private-name storage was already grow-on-demand, but each CompilerContext
held its own copy of the (entries, count, cap) triple. When a borrowing context
(field/method/arrow body that ran adopt_private_names) declared private names
via a nested class in a field initializer, it grew its OWN copy and reallocated
the shared entries buffer — leaving the owner and every sibling borrower with a
stale pointer into freed memory. The 65th private name (first realloc past the
initial cap of 64) therefore aliased or crashed once any nesting/borrowing was
involved: e.g. a class with 64 fields plus one field in a nested class body.

Route all borrowers through a single heap-allocated PrivateNameTable so an
in-place realloc during growth is visible to all of them. Also copy an entry's
slot_name before compiling a field initializer at class.c3, since compiling a
nested class in that initializer can relocate the entries buffer and dangle the
held PrivateNameEntry*.

Repro (previously SyntaxError/aliasing at the boundary, now pass): classes with
70 and 200 distinct private fields read back distinct; nested classes each with
60 private names; a field initializer whose nested class declares 80 names while
the outer field-init loop holds an entry pointer.
