commits.subject: fix: plug large-string leaks — owned-register discipline + catcher-chain free
commits.body:
Large non-interned strings (concat results > MAX_INTERN_BYTES) are pure
refcounted leaves with no string-table or mark-sweep backstop: any register
write that clobbers the last owned reference leaks the block permanently.
Close every such path found by leaks/ASan workloads:

- resolve_call_var / resolve_call_global: release the callee register's old
  OWNED value at entry — the borrowed fast paths write raw and leaked the
  previous contents (e.g. the prior iteration's call-result string).
- ADD/ADDI string-concat sites: track_heap_store the result so
  decref_callee_regs actually sweeps the register at frame teardown.
- RET write-back (inline RET + handle_return): raise the caller's
  max_heap_reg when a heap result lands in an untracked caller register.
- LDINT/LDUNDEF/LDNULL/LDTRUE/LDFALSE, INC/DEC slow paths,
  INC_GLOBAL/DEC_GLOBAL, NEWOBJ/NEWARR/NEWREGEXP/CLOSURE: release the old
  owned register value before their raw result writes (LDREG/LDCONST
  already did).
- free_catcher_chain: a `return` from inside a try never reaches
  CATCH/ENDTRY's pop paths, leaking the TRY-allocated Catcher (plus its
  parked thrown_val) on every such frame; free the chain at every frame-pop
  site (RET/RETUNDEF/handle_return/ENDFINALLY-return/throw-unwind pops).
- Heap.alloc_no_gc: large string allocations now burn the GC trigger
  counter (weighted by KB) so string-heavy garbage referenced by
  short-lived objects reaches a safepoint GC instead of growing without
  bound. Small strings deliberately excluded (interned, table backstop).
- Borrow safety: the committed CALL_VAR/CALL_GLOBAL borrow left raw in the
  callee register on the MAX_CALLS throw path is now neutralized, so a
  caught RangeError can no longer expose the non-owned value to register
  sweeps or the new entry decrefs.

Measured with `leaks --atExit` (2000-iteration workloads): call-result
string 2015→15, discarded-result 2015→15, concat-into-number 2015→15,
`t = 1` over string 2017→17, return-from-try Catcher 5015→15,
array-held strings 417→20 (flat at 5x iterations). ASan clean (no
over-release/UAF) on a borrowed-callee GC-pressure stress incl. deep
recursion through MAX_CALLS. test262 phase 0 (1696/0) and phase 5
(8361/0) match main; rosetta 100/100; golden bytecode 10/10.
bench-fast: arithmetic/string/object flat; recursion/function_call/loop
+3-7% from the added ownership checks on the hot paths.

commits.subject: fix: make global-slot perf optimization sound (4 root causes)
commits.body:
The rebased global-slot perf stack introduced correctness regressions.
Each is fixed narrowly, preserving the optimization for the common case.

1. Global-slot IC returned/stored stale values across a same-alloc shape
   transition (af5ae8c). The VarRef fast path replaced the shape_id guard
   with a bare prop_alloc pointer compare + a cached absolute slot
   pointer; a shape transition reusing the same property-table allocation
   passed the guard while prop_idx named a stale binding. Restore the
   shape_id compare and recompute &prop_values()[prop_idx] each access.
   Drops the dead varref_ptr/varref_alloc IC fields.

2. Global-slot IC served a stale sibling environment (surfaced when this
   stack was rebased onto current main's resizable-ArrayBuffer tests).
   GETGLOBAL/PUTGLOBAL/GETGLOBAL_PRIM/PUTGLOBAL_PRIM/MOVE_GG/INC_GLOBAL/
   DEC_GLOBAL and the CALL_GLOBAL callee resolver assumed act.lex_env is
   always the permanent global object, so they omitted an env-identity
   guard. But GETGLOBAL is emitted for globals read from within a fresh
   lexical scope — e.g. the body of `for (let ctor of ctors)` in the RAB
   harness — where act.lex_env is a per-iteration scope. Two per-iteration
   scopes are distinct objects sharing one shape_id, so the shape_id-only
   guard read the previous iteration's slot (RAB tests: 27 phase-5 fails).
   Add the search_head == act.lex_env guard (as GETVAR already does) to
   every global-IC read/write fast path, in both the switch and threaded
   VMs, and set search_head at every populate site.

3. Sloppy-function `this` was forced undefined (1f44fa4). The
   undefined-this fast path skipped the ES5 §10.4.3 global-object coercion
   for non-strict callees. Gate the shortcut on target_fast.is_strict();
   sloppy bodies (e.g. Function('return this;')) take the coercion path.

4. Functions could fall off the end into adjacent bytecode (b622f1d).
   Dropping the per-instruction curr_pc >= code_end guard assumed every
   function ends in a RET, but a syntactically-final conditional return
   (`if (x) return v;`) leaves the last opcode a RET while a forward
   branch targets code_end. Emit the trailing RETUNDEF whenever any branch
   targets the fall-off-end position (new branch_targets_fall_off_end),
   at all five implicit-return sites.

Validation (vs current main): phase 5 = 8340 pass / 3 fail (identical to
main — zero new failures, the 3 are pre-existing); phases 0/2/3/4 = 0 new
fails; the 4 original targets + all 27 RAB tests pass; golden bytecode
10/10; default and threaded targets build clean. (Phase-6 Math.f16round
fails are a pre-existing missing-builtin version gap in the branch base,
unrelated to this change.)

plain bare-global call (call_prop_obj_reg == MAX_REGISTERS) — last_was_getglobal,
unlike last_was_getvar, is not cleared on member access, so the non-method
guard is required to avoid stripping a stale GETGLOBAL from a method-call
callee chain.

commits.subject: vm: fuse GETGLOBAL_PRIM+PUTGLOBAL_PRIM into MOVE_GG superinstruction
commits.body:
A plain `a = b` between two proven primitive-only globals compiled to a
GETGLOBAL_PRIM rX,S / PUTGLOBAL_PRIM rX,D pair: a scratch round-trip and two
dispatches. Fuse the adjacent pair into one two-word MOVE_GG (word 1 A-BC holds
the destination name; a kept trailing NOP holds the source name in its BC),
halving the op count for global-to-global copies.

Two-word encoding mirrors TRY's finally slot: the VM reads the trailing word
via *pc, advances pc by 2; the NOP-compaction pass keeps the trailing word
(nop_keep) so it survives offset remapping. Dual inline cache: dst write IC at
pc_off, src read IC at pc_off+1. On a hit both slots are proven primitive so
the copy is a raw *dst=*src with no is_heap check, no refcount, no
track_heap_store; on a miss the switch VM resolves both slots via the env walk
and populates both ICs. Threaded VM has a hot-path-only handler that bails to
the switch VM on any miss.

Fusion peephole runs after all register-elision passes and before NOP
compaction. It requires the pair strictly adjacent (the VM reads the
immediately-next word as the source), skips fusion when the trailing word is a
jump target (a jump landing there would skip the read half), and proves the
scratch register dead after the pair. The MOVE_GG word itself may be a jump
target (a loop back-edge landing on it re-executes the full copy correctly).

assign60 loop body drops from 11 ops/iter to 7 (four assignments 8->4 ops).

commits.subject: compiler+vm: guard-free primitive-only global slots (GETGLOBAL_PRIM/PUTGLOBAL_PRIM)
commits.body:

global as primitive-only — every assignment to it anywhere (including nested
functions) stores a provably-primitive value, and the unit has no eval/
globalThis/window/Function/with/this observability. Reads/writes of a proven
primitive-only global emit GETGLOBAL_PRIM/PUTGLOBAL_PRIM, which do a raw slot

track_heap_store (the destination register is still decref'd if it holds heap,
to avoid a missed-decref leak). Both the switch and threaded VMs handle the new
opcodes; INC_GLOBAL/DEC_GLOBAL fusion is preserved for primitive-only counters.

The proof is conservative: any construct it cannot classify (unknown-identifier
RHS, member/call/new, destructuring/for-of/for-in target, function decl,
capacity overflow) falls back to the guarded GETGLOBAL/PUTGLOBAL path. `let`/
`const` globals are excluded (TDZ read must throw).

commits.subject: compiler: remove unsound LDREG-before-INC/DEC peephole
commits.body:
This peephole NOP'd a LDREG rT=rX immediately preceding INC/DEC rX,
assuming the pair was a discarded postfix save. But a genuine postfix
save always has TONUMERIC between the LDREG and the INC, so the
adjacent pattern never actually described a postfix save — it only
ever matched a real body assignment (localVar = loopVar) that happened
to sit right before the loop's increment, e.g. the last statement of
'for (i=0;i<n;i++) { s = i; }'. Its forward deadness scan also
mis-parsed fused compare-and-jump opcodes (JMP_LT etc.) as ABC,
reading the packed jump offset as a register write; when the assigned
variable was r0 the offset field aliased it and the scan wrongly
concluded the value was dead, dropping the assignment.

The result was a silent miscompile of that loop shape (body dropped)
for single-instruction increments (++i, and i-- / --i). Making
discarded postfix i++ compile to the same single INC newly exposed it
for the most common loop in JS. The old-value-materialization removal
in postfix_expr already eliminates the LDREG this peephole targeted,
so it is now pure dead-and-unsound code.

commits.subject: compiler: elide resolvability guard for statically-declared global assignments
commits.body:
A strict-mode plain assignment to a bare global identifier compiled to a
7-opcode sequence: RESOLVEVAR (two uncached env hash lookups) + GETGLOBAL +
IF_TRUE + THROW_REF + moves + PUTGLOBAL. The RESOLVEVAR/THROW_REF guard exists
because PutValue must capture LHS resolvability before the RHS runs, so an
assignment to an as-yet-undeclared global still throws.

But when the LHS names a global this compilation unit itself hoisted (the
names for which the check-prologue emits CHKGLOBALVAR/CHKGLOBALFUNC),
resolvability is statically guaranteed true and the guard is provably dead.
Record those names' constant-pool indices during the hoist passes and, at a
strict GETGLOBAL-LHS assignment whose name is in that set, strip the read and
skip the guard — emitting just GETGLOBAL (RHS) + PUTGLOBAL. Undeclared targets
keep the full guard, so `undeclared = (this.undeclared = 5)` still throws.

At true global scope (is_global && cur_lex_depth == 0), lex_env ==
global_lex_env and var_env == global_env are both permanent GC roots, so a
bare identifier is guaranteed to resolve in one of the two global objects.
Emit GETGLOBAL/PUTGLOBAL instead of GETVAR/PUTVAR_ASSIGN there. Their per-PC
inline cache records (bindings, shape_id, prop_idx); a hit is a single
shape-id compare plus a direct indexed load/store into the global object's
property storage — no name compare, no env-chain walk, no generation
dependent-load, no accessor-flag check (only data slots are cached; a
data->accessor or delete conversion changes shape_id and thus misses).

Globals remain real, observable globalThis properties, so globalThis.x /
this.x, eval, cross-script realm sharing, delete/enumerate/redefine, TDZ, and
const-assignment throws all keep working without any observability pre-scan.

The C-style for-let/for-const head PUSH_LEX now also bumps cur_lex_depth so a
global identifier inside the loop body correctly stays on the name path
(GETVAR); this was a latent inconsistency that only became load-bearing once
cur_lex_depth started gating opcode selection.

commits.subject: vm: borrow global callee in CALL_VAR to cut per-call refcount churn
commits.body:
A CALL_VAR to a top-level function (fib->fib, any f() where f is a
global var/function) previously incref'd the callee closure into its
register and decref'd it on return — pure churn, since a global binding
is a permanent GC root that cannot be freed during its own call. Borrow
it instead: plain copy, no incref, no track_heap_store.

Safety: the executing body references the callee only via a borrowed
CompiledFunction* (Activation.func) which is owned by the heap-level
compiled_funcs registry, not the closure HObject — so reassigning the
global mid-call (fib = null) and freeing the closure cannot free the
running code. The borrowed register is never read as an object again;
the result overwrites it on return (write-backs taught to skip decref of
the non-owned old value via ACT_FLAG_BORROWED_CALLEE), and abnormal
unwinds clear the borrowed slot before any range-sweep can touch it.
Restricted to sync compiled-fn callees resolved in the global env; any
other callee kind un-borrows (incref+track) before dispatch.

commits.subject: vm: scope halt/restart checks + drop per-instruction fall-off-end check (~10% tight loop)
commits.body:
The inner dispatch loop in Vm.run evaluated three branches on EVERY
instruction before the switch jump-table: ds.halt, ds.needs_restart (loop
condition), and a curr_pc >= code_end fall-off-end bounds check. QuickJS's
computed-goto loop pays none of these per-instruction. Neither of ours needs
to be per-instruction:

- halt/needs_restart can only be SET by the ~5 opcode families that call out
  to sub-dispatch (dispatch_calls, dispatch_generators, dispatch_returns,
  dispatch_exceptions) — verified exhaustively by grepping every `ds.halt =
  true` / restart site incl. transitive ones in vm_control/vm_generators/
  vm_exceptions/vm_calls. Check them only after those call sites, not on
  every plain arithmetic/load/branch op.
- fall-off-end: every compiled function ends with a guaranteed trailing RET/
  RETUNDEF, so the bounds check is dead for well-formed bytecode; rely on the
  terminating opcode instead of comparing curr_pc to code_end each iteration.

Net -42 lines (the loop is simpler, not just faster). This is the first
interpreter-CORE win this session — it helps ALL code, not just calls:
~10% on a call-free tight arithmetic loop, ~4% on fib. The remaining ~2.3x
vs QuickJS on tight loops is the switch-vs-computed-goto decode overhead.

commits.subject: vm: fuse GETVAR+CALL_UNDEF_THIS into CALL_VAR for bare-identifier calls (~2%)
commits.body:
Named function calls (the fib recursion shape) emit GETVAR to load the
callee followed by CALL_UNDEF_THIS to invoke it. CALL_VAR collapses both
into one dispatch: the compiler strips the callee's GETVAR from the code
stream (it's provably dead — nothing reads callee_reg's value before the
call) and emits CALL_VAR, which resolves the callee by name via the same
per-pc VarIC path GETVAR uses (so the IC hit rate is unaffected) and then
performs the plain-undefined-this call.

Fusion only applies when: the callee is a bare identifier (not a local
variable register), the call has no spread arguments, the callee register
isn't relocated for this call, and the name's constant-pool index fits in
CALL_VAR's 8-bit C field. All other shapes fall back to plain
GETVAR + CALL_UNDEF_THIS unchanged.

Measured ~2% on fib(32)/fib(34) (smaller than the ~5% CALL_UNDEF_THIS
win, since the VarIC lookup work itself still runs — only the extra
fetch+dispatch is eliminated, not the underlying lookup cost).

@inline helper (try_fast_compiled_call) that Vm.run's CALL/CALL_S/

untouched and still route through dispatch_calls.

did not. A plain call reusing a slot last occupied by a generator body at
the same depth would inherit a stale non-null async_gen_state, which the
throw-unwind walk (vm_throw.c3) and YIELD paths read unconditionally.

was the lone inconsistency among all call paths. One store, 0% measured

commits.subject: vm: CALL_UNDEF_THIS opcode elides per-call LDUNDEF this-load (~5% on calls)
commits.body:

the compiler emitted an `LDUNDEF callee_reg+1` dispatch on every such call

opcode: the compiler reserves the this-slot without writing it and emits
CALL_UNDEF_THIS, and the VM sets the receiver undefined once in the call
handler (before any fast/slow path reads the slot). One fewer dispatch per
plain call.

commits.subject: compiler: liveness-based move elimination (producer+LDREG -> retargeted producer)
commits.body:
Retargets a producer instruction to write its consumer's LDREG destination
directly and NOPs the LDREG, killing redundant register-to-register copies
(e.g. call-argument moves: `SUBI rT=n,1 ; LDREG rArg=rT` -> `SUBI rArg=n,1`).

Uses real whole-function backward liveness (live-in/live-out bitsets over
the CFG) rather than a local scan, since retargeting safety depends on two
facts a local scan from the pair itself cannot prove: the source register
is not live-out of the copy, and the destination register is not live-in
at the producer's site. An earlier local-scan-only peephole measured the
same win but corrupted state in 3 tests for exactly this reason.

across the test/benchmark corpus (15.7% reduction). 0 differential diffs
across test/*.js + benchmarks/*.js against baseline; test262 phase 0
unchanged (1155 pass / 24 fail, identical to baseline).

Wires the DYN_IMPORT opcode's options operand, spec-correct abrupt-completion

- ToString(specifier) abrupt completion rejects the promise (IfAbruptRejectPromise)

- Requested-module evaluation errors reject with the thrown value; all error
  channels are cleared so the enclosing script/module sees no lingering fault.

  and marked non-extensible (§10.4.6).
- `export default function name`/`class Foo` bind their declared name in module
  scope with "default" as a live binding of it; anonymous `export default <expr>`
  gets the inferred name "default".

assignment used in value position returned a freed register (read back as
undefined); now copies the assigned value into a live temp.

commits.subject: fix: refresh token_start for async-fn-decl source span (fixes fromAsync+async-gen crash)
commits.body:
An `async function*` declaration nested inside another async function body
crashed the compiler (exit 138 / OOB read at functions.c3:3216) when the
retained-source span was computed. The dispatch in statement() read
`self.lexer.token_start` to capture the `async` keyword's offset, but that
field is stale when the identifier is still a peeked lookahead — it reflected
a far-ahead consumed token. The bogus src_start (past the function body) made
`inner_body_end_pos - src_start` underflow to a huge unsigned length, and the
copy loop read off the end of source.

Call refresh_token_start() before capturing the offset (mirrors the existing
class-body pattern), and defensively guard the span on inner_body_end_pos >
src_start so any future stale offset degrades to "no retained source" instead
of an OOB read.

Surfaced by Array.fromAsync tests consuming a real async generator
(asyncitems-asynciterator-exists, async-iterable-async-mapped-awaits-once,
async-iterable-input-iteration-err) — a purely compile-time bug, not the
runtime reaction-interleave originally suspected.

commits.subject: fix: keep finally-owning catcher alive through ENDTRY
commits.body:
ENDTRY unconditionally popped and freed the catcher on the normal
fall-through out of a try body. For a try-with-finally, the following
FINALLY/ENDFINALLY still need that catcher (its saved_lex_env, its
pending-completion flags, and ENDFINALLY's own pop). When an enclosing
try sat above — e.g. a for-of iterator-close guard wrapping a
block-scoped array destructuring (`for (let x of e) { let arr=...;
let [a]=arr; }`) — the destructuring's iterator-close FINALLY then read
the *enclosing* catcher and restored ITS saved_lex_env, popping the
block's lexical environment early. The destructured binding vanished
from the env chain, so a later read threw "a is not defined".

Only pop catchers without a finally in ENDTRY; leave finally-owning
catchers for ENDFINALLY. Abrupt completions never run ENDTRY, so their
catcher already survives — this only fixes the normal path.

(the TA/resizable machinery was already correct; the failure was this
generic try/finally + lexical-scope unwinding bug).

commits.subject: fix: async yield* NEXT-delegation edges (received threading, next caching, no double-unwrap)
commits.body:
Now that the [...arguments] re-entrant blocker is fixed, the async yield*
NEXT-delegation family runs to completion and exposed three edges in the
YIELD_STAR_ASYNC state machine and the AsyncFromSync adapter:

1. First delegated .next() must use undefined (§14.4.14 step 6): the
   argument the consumer passed to the async generator's first .next() is
   discarded — only resumptions after a delegated yield thread the value.
2. Cache the delegate's [[NextMethod]] once (§14.4.14 step 1 / GetIterator):
   the YIELD_STAR_ASYNC opcode read iterator.next every iteration, firing a
   `next` accessor getter repeatedly. New gs.ays_next_method (GC-marked,
   alongside the previously-unmarked ays_received) caches it.
3. Do NOT re-run AsyncGeneratorUnwrapYieldResumption (§27.6.3.7) in the
   opcode: the async-gen drain already Awaits a RETURN resumption's value
   (async_gen_yield_return_await + YRET reactions) before resuming the body,
   so the opcode awaiting it again added an extra Await — breaking the
   observable tick/getter order (yield-star-return-then-getter-ticks).

Also cache the wrapped sync iterator's [[NextMethod]] in the
%AsyncFromSyncIterator% adapter at wrap time (§7.4.2 GetIterator /
§27.1.4.1), so a sync-source delegate's `next` accessor fires once, not per
.next(); a throwing getter now propagates from GET_ITER_ASYNC and
Array.fromAsync's sync-wrap path.

commits.subject: fix: abort finally body after its own return (all function kinds)
commits.body:
A `return`/`break`/`continue`/`throw` inside a `finally` block must abort
the remaining finally statements. break/continue/throw already did (they
emit direct jumps / unwind the catcher), but `return` inside a finally only
updated the pending return value and fell through the dispatch loop to the
next instruction — so statements after the finally's own `return` still ran.

Fix: cache the matching ENDFINALLY pc on the Catcher (lazily, in the FINALLY
opcode via a nesting-balanced forward scan) and, when RET/RET_GEN/RETUNDEF_GEN
detect they are executing inside the finally body (IN_FINALLY), jump to that
ENDFINALLY to abort the rest of the body and complete the (overriding) return.
Covers plain functions, sync generators, and async generators; nested-finally
override semantics preserved.

commits.subject: fix: AsyncFromSync next/return/throw edge semantics (§27.1.4)
commits.body:

the spec's IfAbruptRejectPromise / IteratorClose behaviour:

  instead of throwing synchronously

  "value" is a rejected promise and done is false (closeOnRejection); return
  does not — carried on the reject-forward closure via a "\xFFcloseIter" slot

  before rejecting with a TypeError; a throwing close replaces the reason
- poisoned done/value getters in the continuation reject the promise
- next/return/throw pass `value` to the sync method only when present
- shared finish-continuation helper + AsyncFromSyncCloseResult/close_normal

19 return/throw fails are blocked upstream: async `yield*` delegation
(emit_async_yield_star in statements.c3) implements only the `next` loop and
never invokes AsyncFromSync.throw/return — verified those builtins are never
reached via the async yield-star path. Sync yield* (YIELD_STAR opcode) does
delegate; the async path needs the same throw/return injection.

commits.subject: perf: O(1) get_prop_flags for default-attribute objects
commits.body:
Reads of a property on a large "dictionary-mode" object (built by
`for (i) obj[i]=v`) were O(N): each distinct property adds one shape
node, so the shape chain grows N deep, and get_prop_flags(idx) walks it
from head to the shape owning `idx`. Small/early indices sit at the far
(deep) end, so probing their flags is O(N) — and it is done on every
property read (accessor check in get_prop_or_accessor_proto and IC
population), making bulk reads O(N^2). This made three
TypedArray/copyWithin detached-buffer test262 tests (which build a
10000-element array-like via obj[i]=arr[i] then `new TA(obj)`) take
3.5-7.6s each and time out under load.

Track a per-object flag has_nondefault_flags, set (never cleared)
whenever a property with attributes other than the default WEC data
descriptor is installed (accessor, read-only, non-enumerable,
non-configurable). When it is false — the overwhelmingly common case —
get_prop_flags returns PROP_FLAGS_WEC in O(1) without touching the shape
chain. All non-default flags flow through put_prop / set_prop_flags, the
only two writers, so the flag is authoritative.

Each of the three tests drops from 3-4s to ~0.4s. Phase 22 is 2653/0
with 0 timeouts across two runs; phase 3 unchanged (3 pre-existing
fails); golden bytecode 9/9; array/object/property benches flat to
slightly faster.

commits.subject: fix: root vm.return_val/throw_value in GC + two TypedArray/Array join heap bugs
commits.body:
Three heap-safety bugs surfaced by batch-run flakiness in the phase-22
TypedArray join/set tests:

1. GC rooting gap (the assigned bug): vm.return_val and vm.throw_value are
   VM-level TVal scratch fields, not part of the valstack scanned by
   mark_roots. A closure returned into vm.return_val by a top-level RET
   survived instantiate_closure via its temproot flag, but the next
   safepoint GC clears all temproots and, finding no root for the slot,
   collected it -- the following decref of the stale slot was a
   use-after-poison (deterministic ASan repro:
   TypedArray/prototype/set/src-typedarray-big-throws.js). Fix: mark both
   fields in vm_mark_activations.

2. builtin_ta_proto_join inserted its result string into the string table
   via a bare str_table_insert -- without the table's owning incref or
   is_interned flag that str_intern_normalized applies. The table entry was
   backed by no reference, so the result register's later decref freed the
   string while it was still in the table, double-freeing at heap reset.
   The join result is a transient; strict-eq compares string content, so
   interning is unnecessary. Fix: drop the insert, return the transient
   (store_builtin_result handles the refcount-1 string).

3. builtin_array_proto_join copied the separator with sep[0] guarded only
   by i>0, not sep.len>0. An empty separator makes sep a zero-length slice;
   sep[0] traps under the O0 bounds-checked ASan build (benign in the
   optimized build). Fix: add the sep.len>0 guard, matching the TypedArray
   join sites.

commits.subject: fix: two-phase GC sweep + full-frame register rooting (resizable-buffer UAF)
commits.body:
Sweep-order use-after-free: when a garbage object's hobject_free decref'd a
neighbour (getter/setter, captured_this, promise result, bigint leaf) that the
same sweep had already freed, decref read a dead header. Fixed with a two-phase
sweep — Phase A unlinks all dying nodes, Phase B runs every teardown while their
memory (and mark bits) are still valid, Phase C frees headers last — plus a
decref sweep-guard that skips references into unmarked/dying non-string nodes.
hobject_free gains a free_header flag; header release is split into
hobject_free_header for the deferred pass.

Fixing the sweep bug exposed a latent GC rooting gap: valstack_top is only a
high-water mark for the deepest frame and can sit below an outer frame's
register span or below scratch slots holding staged call arguments, so a live
value there (e.g. a BigInt box from ta_load_element held across a callee) was
collected then read as freed memory. vm_mark_activations now marks each live
JS frame's full register/scratch span (innermost frame scanned to valstack_end,
which is zero-initialised past live data so the extra marks are no-ops).

Phase 22 now stable across 3 runs at 2598 pass / 2 fail (was crashing/flaking);
the resizable-buffer set repro prints a genuine PASS. Phases 0/5/21 unchanged
vs baseline; golden bytecode 9/9; bench_memory_heavy and bench_object flat.

commits.body:
The lexer's string and template escape slow paths returned token
str_value/raw_value slices into 64KB stack buffers (scan_string,
scan_template_content). Those slices are use-after-return: a token stays
live in current/lookahead/pushed_back and through pre-scan re-lexing long
after the scanning frame returns. ASan flagged it as a stack-buffer-overflow
READ in has_raw_utf8_astral; in normal builds it intermittently corrupted
the malloc freelist (SIGTRAP) on escape-bearing sources.

Give the Lexer a heap-backed growable arena (chain of blocks, grow-only for
one compilation) via a shared LexArena holder referenced by pointer. The
holder is shared by value-copied lexers (destructuring speculative scans,
deferred-target snapshots) so a block allocated by any copy is tracked and
freed by the original. Escape slow paths decode into a transient stack
buffer as before, then copy the result into the arena; the fast no-escape
path (slice into source) is unchanged. The whole arena is freed via
Lexer.free_arena(), deferred at every compilation entry point (module, eval,
Function/generator constructors, compiled proto methods, all three CLIs).

Remove the dead str_owns_memory Token flag — arena ownership is per-
compilation, not per-token.

commits.subject: fix: clear duplicated tail arg slots in Function.prototype.call shift
commits.body:
Function.prototype.call shifts the argument registers left by one to drop
thisArg before dispatching a builtin/lightfunc downstream. The raw copy
left the vacated tail slot still holding the last argument, so a
refcounted arg (e.g. the callback passed to Array.prototype.every.call)
was physically present in two registers of the call frame. At RET,
decref_callee_regs releases every slot once, double-releasing that arg —
an eventual "pointer being freed was not allocated" abort after a handful
of such calls.

Clear the now-duplicated tail slots (base_reg+remaining .. base_reg+argc-1)
after the shift so each refcounted argument is decref'd exactly once.

Fixes the crash behind Array.prototype.{every,some,includes,entries}
called on a TypedArray receiver via .call, and any repeated
`builtin.call(recv, refcountedArg)` pattern on plain objects.

commits.subject: fix: trailing arg after a spread no longer collides with the spread
commits.body:
A trailing non-spread argument after a spread call
(`f(1, ...[2,3,4,5], 99)`) was miscompiled: the assignment_expr that
evaluates the trailing arg allocated its value register only two slots
past the spread destination window, so a 4-element spread overwrote
the trailing arg's register with `99` again before PUTARG could read it
— producing `[1,2,3,4,99,99]` instead of `[1,2,3,4,5,99]`.

The argument loop was already reserving a "count" register below the
spread window (the begin_spread_args relocation) and copying the
trailing arg through a dedicated spread_val_reg before PUTARG — but
the value had to first survive in its native register. Raise the
post-SPREAD_ARG next_reg floor to SPREAD_MAX_SLOTS (256) so the
trailing arg's evaluation register lands above the worst-case spread
area. Real code rarely passes 200+ element spreads; pathological
cases still need argument-array lowering per the plan.

commits.subject: fix: reject ArrowFunction as a binary operand at parse time
commits.body:
ArrowFunction is an AssignmentExpression-level production and must not
appear as a binary operand without parentheses (ES §13.16, §13.15):
`1 + () => 2` and `#x in () => {}` are SyntaxErrors. The Pratt parser
accepted both because the inner binary_expr RHS recursion consumes the
arrow and returns silently.

parse_arrow_function and parse_arrow_function_reparse now set a shared
last_was_arrow_expr marker on the parent context right before returning.
binary_expr clears the marker on entry (so a sub-expression's arrow
does not leak out) and calls check_no_arrow_rhs() after every RHS
recursive call — that rejects `1 + () => 2`. Lone arrows such as
`[1].map(() => 1)` and `(a, () => 1)` still parse because the
expression / assignment / conditional entry points reset the marker
and there is no binary operator following the arrow in those contexts.

Also unblocks the `expressions/in/private-field-*` and `rhs-yield-absent`
negative-parse tests in test262.

commits.subject: fix: parse-time validation of regexp literals
commits.body:

NEWREGEXP path keeps its current behavior — invalid patterns are
now unreachable in the strict-only engine.

commits.subject: fix: preserve lexical for-loop var register in condition/increment codegen
commits.body:
A C-style for-loop with a let/const init variable and a member-expression in
the condition (e.g. `for (let i = 0; i < obj.length; ++i)`) miscompiled: the
re-compiled condition and increment reset the register floor to the pre-head
saved_reg, which sits BELOW the live loop-var register. The GETPROP key load for
`obj.length` then allocated the loop var's own register, clobbering `i` before
the compare — so the loop either never entered (i overwritten by a larger value)
or spun forever (i never advanced). Capture cond_floor as the high-water mark
AFTER all for-head declarations and clamp the condition/increment temporaries to
it, keeping lexical loop variables live.

This surfaced only inside functions (loop var register-resident, read via
LDREG/resolve_var) with a property/computed condition bound; it caused the two
map/resizable-buffer.js infinite loops and many resizable-buffer iteration
failures whose harness loops over `ta.length`.

Also (typedarray.c3): join re-reads elements through the current pointer and
emits empty string for out-of-bounds indices (original length retained); at()
and with() validate the index against the current length after coercion while
keeping the pre-coercion length for result sizing / negative-index normalization;
reverse() uses ta_element_count instead of the raw stored byte_length.

both former infinite-loop tests pass, 0 regressions. Golden bytecode 9/9.

commits.subject: fix: PUTLEX param prologue used r0 as source for every captured param
commits.body:

earlier non-default parameter, the params are pushed into a function-level
lexical env so the closure can reach them. The prologue emitted PUTLEX with
a hardcoded source register 0 for every pre-default (and post-default
non-default) param, storing the first param's value (r0) into the lex
bindings for key, val, etc. The captured closure then read the wrong values.

Params occupy registers r0..rN in declaration order, so the source register
must be the param's own arg index (ai). Fixed all three duplicated param
prologues: parse_function_body, compile_inner_function, and
compile_arrow_inner_reparse (pre-default loop + post-default non-default
loop each).

Class getter and setter accessors reference `arguments` in their bodies
get ReferenceError instead of an empty arguments object. The fast path
for ordinary CALL/CALL_PROP declares the arguments object when the
target has uses_arguments=true (src/vm/vm_execute.c3:569,
src/vm/vm_calls.c3:435/1260/1485/2426/1959), but the two accessor
invocation paths (`invoke_getter` in vm_core.c3 and the two own/inherited
setter paths in vm_property.c3) skipped the declaration entirely. Setters
always receive exactly one user arg (the assigned value); getters never
receive any, so the object is sized to 0 or 1 accordingly.

Closes the static-init-arguments-methods.js fail in Phase 15 (Classes),
which exercises a getter, a setter, a method, a generator method, and
an async method, each with `arguments` in both body and parameter-default.
Verified: rosetta 100/100, Phase 15 4055/0, full test262 unchanged
on every other phase (the 8 pre-existing CE:unexpected static-init-await
tests are unrelated parser bugs already on HEAD).

commits.subject: fix: reject let/var redeclaration at the same block level
commits.body:
ES2024 §13.2.1 (Block Static Semantics: Early Errors) requires that
LexicallyDeclaredNames and VarDeclaredNames of a BlockStatement be
disjoint — a `let x; var x;` (in any order) at the same block level
is a SyntaxError. The compiler pre-scanned lexical declarations for
TDZ-initialization but had no equivalent pass for var declarations, so
the conflict went undetected and the engine silently let the lexical
binding shadow the var hoisting (or vice versa).

block() now invokes a new pre_scan_var_decls after the existing
pre_scan_lexical_decls and rejects the block if any name appears in
both sets. The var scanner collects names at any brace_depth (per
§13.2.5 VarDeclaredNames recursively descends into nested Blocks),
but tracks nested function/class bodies via a depth stack and skips
their interior vars — those belong to the nested function/class's
own VarDeclaredNames scope (§13.2.13 / §14.5), not the outer block's.

Closes static-init-invalid-lex-var.js and the block-scope/syntax/
redeclaration family (`let f; var f;`, `{ let f; { var f; } }`,
`{ var f; let f; }`, etc.). Verified: rosetta 100/100, all phases
0/15 unchanged in raw counts (the affected tests are $DONOTEVALUATE
parse-only tests that the runner skips from the pass/fail totals by
design; before the fix they would FAIL if the runner ever lost its
DONOTEVALUATE exclusion, now they CE which is the correct outcome).

commits.subject: feat: support `#x in obj` ergonomic brand checks (plan 054 P6)
commits.body:
The `class-fields-private-in` proposal lets a method test "does this
object come from my class?" with a single-token probe: `#x in obj`
returns a boolean instead of the throw-and-catch dance around
`obj.#x`. The grammar gives PrivateIdentifier as a standalone LHS of
the `in` operator — `#x` is not a value expression by itself, so the
Pratt binary parser needs a dedicated entry point.

Implementation:
- New bytecode opcode `HAS_BRAND` (ABC: A=dst, B=object, C=brand-reg).
  Same own-only property check as `CHK_BRAND` but writes a boolean
  result instead of throwing on miss. Throws TypeError when the RHS
  is not an object (spec §13.10.1 step 4).
- `binary_expr` peeks for `HASH_IDENT in` before the normal Pratt
  loop, resolves `#x` to its brand slot via the existing
  `resolve_private_name` machinery, then emits `HAS_BRAND`. A bare
  `#x` not followed by `in` is pushed back so the parser surfaces a
  real SyntaxError rather than silently consuming the token.
- `class-fields-private-in` removed from `UNSUPPORTED_PATTERN` in
  `scripts/run_test262.py`. The `class-fields-private` flag (already
  landed) covers the underlying private-name support.

Verified: rosetta 100/100, Phase 7 586→596 (+10 pass), full test262
35,734→35,744 (+10 raw pass; the one new CE:unexpected in phase 7
is the pre-existing "await as function name at script scope" parser
gap unrelated to this change — un-skipped by the pattern removal).

commits.subject: fix: spread into a call must not place control/arg regs in the argv window
commits.body:
A spread argument writes an unbounded number of values into the argument
register window [first_arg, first_arg+count). The running-count register (also
CALL_S's nargs source) and any plain argument that follows a spread were
allocated *inside* that window, so a spread of 5+ elements overwrote them:
Math.min(...[5,4,3,2,1]) returned 2 because the count store clobbered the last
argument slot, and the freed value was read back as nargs.

begin_spread_args now shifts the callee frame up by two registers and places the
count register and a PUTARG value scratch in the freed slots below first_arg,
where they survive an arbitrarily large spread. All three lowering sites (call,
new, super) funnel through it.

SPREAD_ARG also copied each iterated element into the argv slot as a *borrowed*
reference; the call frame teardown (decref_callee_regs) then over-decref'd it,
freeing an element still owned by the source iterable (array element turned into
an empty object). It now tval_copy_refs the element like FWD_ARGS and ordinary
argument evaluation, leaving an owned reference.

commits.subject: fix: release builtin transient's ref for non-interned string results
commits.body:
Builtins populate ctx.result via increffing setters, then the VM copies
that transient into a register with tval_copy_ref (a second incref). The
transient's own reference from the setter is never balanced. For objects
(GC-reclaimed) and interned strings (string-table backstop) this is
harmless, but a large non-interned string — a pure refcounted leaf with
no backstop — leaks permanently. This is the dominant leak behind the
RegExp property-escapes RSS growth: String.fromCodePoint results built by
the regExpUtils buildString harness.

Add Heap.store_builtin_result, which after the register copy releases the
transient's reference iff the result is a non-interned, non-symbol string
the setter solely owns (refcount == 1). The is_interned/is_symbol/refcount
gate is deliberately narrow: an earlier unconditional version freed live
Symbol backing strings (Symbol() returns an HString at refcount 1 that
other code still references), a use-after-free ASan caught over the Symbol
tests. Swap the 9 builtin/bound/ctor result-copy sites in dispatch_calls
and the getter-result copy in invoke_getter to the new helper.

Measured (RegExp property-escapes Grapheme_Base, per test): fromCodePoint
leak 281 -> 4 objects (~6.4MB -> ~180KB). ASan: no UAF over 185+
string/property-escapes/Symbol tests. phase 6 & 8: 0 fails. golden
bytecode 9/9. bench_string/bench_memory_heavy flat.

commits.subject: fix: accept await/yield as BindingIdentifier at nested non-async function boundaries
commits.body:
Per ES2024 §13.1, `await`/`yield` are valid identifiers outside a module/async
function (await) and outside a generator (yield). A class static block reserves
them at its own top level, but that reservation resets at nested function/arrow
boundaries — mirroring how the spec re-fixes the [Yield]/[Await] grammar params.

Positions that were gated wrong (rejected await/yield unconditionally):
- function declaration name, function-expression / generator-expression name
- FormalParameters (function, method, accessor, generator; outer + inner)
- catch parameter, array/object binding patterns (var/param), object rest
- object-literal `{ await }` / `{ yield }` shorthand IdentifierReference

Arrow functions inherit the enclosing [Await]/[Yield] for their PARAMETERS
(ContainsAwait reaches arrow param defaults) but reset for the BODY, so
`((x = await) => 0)` in a static block is still a SyntaxError while
`(() => ({ await }))` is valid. New CompilerContext.expect_binding_identifier
centralizes the context-aware acceptance.

commits.subject: fix: relocate entry_act.bottom and caller_valstack_top on valstack growth
commits.body:
Vm.execute()/execute_in_env()/execute_module_async() captured
entry_act.bottom = vm.valstack before calling ensure_valstack(vm, nregs),
so a growing realloc there left the entry activation's bottom pointer
into the freed old buffer for the rest of the run. ensure_valstack_grow's
relocation pass also missed Activation.caller_valstack_top, so any call
that triggered a grow left its caller's restore-on-RET pointer stale too.
Together these desynced vm.valstack_top from vm.valstack, corrupting the
next CALL's `needed` slot count into billions and blowing the valstack
out to gigabytes — surfacing as the non-deterministic property-escapes /
CharacterClassEscapes test262 failures (worker MEMKILL/timeout) that only
showed up once the batch runner's shared heap+VM had compiled a large
enough top-level script to force at least one valstack grow.

Verified under test262_runner_asan (AddressSanitizer): the previously
reliable 2-iteration heap-buffer-overflow repro on
RegExp/property-escapes/generated/Script_Extensions_-_Nushu.js is gone
after the fix, and phase 8 (built-ins/RegExp, JSON, Date, parseInt,
parseFloat) passes 3 consecutive parallel runs plus a 2205-test
single-process property-escapes stress run with 0 fails and bounded
memory (previously unbounded growth to 3-4GB+ and MEMKILL/ASan abort).
Golden bytecode (9/9) and rosetta (100/100) unaffected.

commits.subject: fix: Await always ticks via PromiseResolve — fix for-await-of tick-ordering tests
commits.body:
AWAIT now routes every value (Promise or not) through PromiseResolve(%Promise%,
value) and always defers the resume through a queued reaction, matching
ES2017 §27.7.5.3 — the previous FULFILLED short-circuit skipped both the
observable `constructor` lookup and the microtask tick.

Fixing this exposed three latent, independent bugs that only became
observable once every await reliably ticks:
- vm_call_fn_impl drained the microtask queue after every native→VM call,
  even when nested inside an outer script/async frame still mid-statement,
  running unrelated queued jobs out of order. Now only drains when it is the
  outermost such reentry.
- The compiler unconditionally emitted AWAIT after ITER_CLOSE_ASYNC, even
  when there was no .return() to close (previously masked because AWAIT on
  undefined was a no-op). ITER_CLOSE_ASYNC now reports via rc whether a real
  result needs awaiting, and codegen skips AWAIT/LOAD_RESUME when it doesn't.
- for-of/for-await-of called IteratorClose/AsyncIteratorClose on normal
  iterator exhaustion, not just abrupt completion, spuriously invoking
  .return() (and, for async, an extra Await) after a loop finished normally.
- %AsyncFromSyncIteratorPrototype%.next wrapped its value with the internal
  [[Resolve]] procedure directly instead of the full PromiseResolve
  operation, skipping the constructor observability check.

Fixes the 3 remaining for-await-of ticks-with-*-constructor-lookup* tests
(phase 24: 3 fails -> 0) with no regressions in phases 24, 21, 17-20, 14, 12-13,
rosetta, or golden-bytecode.

commits.body:
The length-shrink branch of the shared ArraySetLength helper (used by
Object.defineProperty on Array.length and by plain `arr.length = v`
assignment) walked every integer from oldLen-1 down to newLen looking for
own array-index properties to delete. For sparse arrays with a huge oldLen
(e.g. after storing at index 4294967294, or after propertyHelper.js's
isWritable probe temporarily sets length to 2^32-1), this iterates ~4
billion times, hanging or exhausting memory via int_to_hstring interning a
key per index.

[[Delete]] on an absent index is an unobservable no-op, so only the
object's own array-index property-table entries matter. The fix scans the
property table (bounded by prop_count) to find the highest non-configurable
index in range — which is exactly the index the spec's downward walk would
first refuse to delete — then deletes every configurable own array-index
key above that floor.

test262/test/built-ins/Array/length/S15.4.5.2_A3_T4.js and
test262/test/built-ins/Object/defineProperty/15.2.3.6-4-116.js now pass
in milliseconds instead of timing out. Phase 3: 3->0 fails, Phase 5: 2->0
fails.

commits.subject: fix: keep block-bodied arrows in template substitutions from truncating functions
commits.body:
Function-body skip and hoist scans treated any `}` while inside a
`${...}` template substitution as the substitution's closing brace. A
block-bodied arrow inside the substitution has its own `{...}` body, so
those scanners called the template scanner at the arrow body's closing
brace and consumed the rest of the function/source as template text.

Track nested JavaScript brace depth while inside template substitutions
and only scan the next template part when the substitution's own closing
brace is reached. This preserves code after a function containing
`${ (() => { ... })() }`.

commits.subject: fix: capture identifiers in parameter-default expressions of nested functions
commits.body:
The capture pre-scan (pre_scan_captures) only collected identifiers
inside callable bodies (region_depth >= 0) or expression-bodied arrows
(expr_region_depth >= 0). Identifiers in parameter-default expressions
appeared before the `{` that opens the body, so they were invisible to
the scan. A local like `p` in `function w(){ var p; (function(_ = p = 6){})(); }`
stayed register-resident; the inner function's default thunk wrote to
the env copy via PUTVAR, but `return p` in the outer body read the
stale register.

Fix: buffer identifiers seen inside non-control `(...)` regions. When
`{` follows `)` (confirming a param list), flush the buffer into the
captured set. If any other token follows `)`, discard the buffer (the
paren was a call/grouping, not a param list).

commits.subject: perf: VarIC for RESOLVEVAR + fuse strict unresolvable-throw into one opcode
commits.body:
RESOLVEVAR (strict plain-assignment LHS resolvability capture, added in
3424bd4) walked the full env chain on every execution and paired with an
IF_TRUE + THROW_REF sequence after the RHS. Hot strict-mode global-
assignment loops paid a chain walk plus two extra dispatches per store on
top of PUTVAR_ASSIGN's already-IC'd write.

- RESOLVEVAR now has a VarIC using the same key/search_head/shape/
  generation guards as GETVAR. Only existence is captured, so a hit needs
  no flag checks; a delete anywhere in the bindings object bumps the
  generation and falls back to the walk (keeping the deleted-during-RHS
  ReferenceError of §9.1.1.2.5 step 3 intact). The slow path now records
  the owning env instead of calling env_has twice.
- New THROW_UNRESOLVED A,BC opcode replaces the compiler's IF_TRUE +
  THROW_REF pair (and its extra register + message constant): throws
  ReferenceError "'name' is not defined" unless register A is true, so
  the message now names the identifier instead of "Unresolvable
  reference".

Design per the RESOLVEVAR plan review: the riskier alternative (priming
PUTVAR_ASSIGN's IC from RESOLVEVAR) only helps cold executions once both
sides have ICs, and carries cross-activation/chained-assignment hazards,
so it was dropped. Note V8 deviates from spec here (no throw when the RHS
creates the global); test262 assign-to-global-undefined.js asserts the
spec behavior this engine implements.

covers pre-RHS capture, delete-during-RHS, delete-then-recreate, chained

commits.subject: backlog: fix R1 RegExp SIGABRT on regexps with >32 capture groups (BACKLOG R1)
commits.body:
The QuickJS libregexp `lre_exec` reads the regex's capture count from the
compiled bytecode header and NULL-initialises every `capture[]` slot
before matching, so the caller's buffer must be sized to
`capture_count * 2` pointers. The wrapper hard-coded a 64-slot stack
array (RE_MAX_CAPTURES=32); any regex with more than 31 capture groups
silently overflowed that buffer and tripped the stack canary on the
next function call (exit 134 with no stderr).

Two-part fix:
1. Bump RE_MAX_CAPTURES to 256 in both libregexp/re_wrapper.h and
   src/re_bindings.c3. The 200-group test S15.10.2.8_A3_T15 still fits
   the stack; deeper patterns heap-allocate.
2. re_exec now heap-allocates the capture[] buffer when the compiled
   regex carries more captures than the stack array can hold, and frees
   it on every return path (match, no-match, error).

Verified: S15.10.2.8_A3_T15.js + S15.10.2_A1_T1.js now PASS; the
CharacterClassEscapes + sticky/this-val-regexp siblings that surfaced
on the same phase run also pass (transient RegExp flakiness, not
regressions). Rosetta 100/100 maintained.

commits.subject: backlog: fix escaped-arrow super() lexical-this re-binding (plan 059 §4)
commits.body:
A derived constructor's `this` is initialised the first time its body calls
super() (§8.1.1.3.1 BindThisValue step 3). A second super() call must throw
ReferenceError even when the call site is an arrow that closed over the
derived ctor's `this` and ran after the ctor's frame was popped.

The existing super_init_this_chain walks the live activation chain to
detect the already-initialised state; that walk returns false once the
derived ctor's frame is gone. Fix: stamp a "super called" boolean on the
newly-bound instance (the derived ctor's `this`) when super() returns, and
in the SUPER_CTOR RET path consult the caller's `this_binding` (which for
arrows equals the captured this) for that flag before calling the walk. The
flag is the only signal that survives ctor return, and the per-instance
location matches the spec's per-`thisER` semantics (the env's
[[thisBindingStatus]] is no longer reachable; the cell must be on the
record-bearing object itself).

Verified: rosetta 100/100, full test262 35,166 pass / 11 fail / 0 CE
(was 35,156/21/0); lexical-super-call-from-within-constructor.js now
passes with the spec's two-step semantics — the second super() runs
Construct (count becomes 2) and then throws.

commits.body:
test262/built-ins/String/prototype/localeCompare/15.5.4.9_CE.js
asserts that canonically-equivalent Unicode strings (e.g. "o\u0308"
vs "ö") compare as 0 per ES2018 §12.3.3.2. Our prior byte-level
compare treated them as different (combining-mark vs precomposed
sequences differ in UTF-8 bytes).

codepoint sequences. Stack-allocate a 4096-codepoint scratch
buffer; spill to the heap only for >4096 codepoints (well over the
expected pair size for typical .localeCompare calls). The byte-equal
short-circuit at the top covers the ASCII/pre-normalized fast path
so the existing `Intl.Collator`-backed comparisons and array.sort
call sites stay fast.

commits.subject: backlog: fix builtin ctor [[Prototype]] for Function.toString grammar
commits.body:
The engine's built-in ctor HObjects (ArrayBuffer, Map, Set, Symbol,
Promise, WeakMap, WeakSet) were created via `heap.alloc_object(FUNCTION)`
without setting the HObjectBase.prototype field, so their
`[[Prototype]]` was null. The engine-installed `Object.prototype.__proto__`
accessor pair had the same bug because `register_object_constructor`
runs before `register_function_constructor` allocates
`heap.function_proto`.

Test262's `built-ins/Function/prototype/toString/built-in-function-object.js`
walks every well-known intrinsic's `Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptors`
output, including the `__proto__` accessor's `get`/`set` HObjects, and
asserts each one returns a `[native code]` source string — which routes
through `Function.prototype.toString`. A function with no `[[Prototype]]`
inherits nothing, so the call throws "undefined is not a function".

Three coordinated fixes:
1. Each `register_*_ctor` now sets `ctor.prototype = heap.function_proto`
   so the ctor inherits `Function.prototype.{apply,call,bind,toString}`.
2. `register_object_constructor` stashes the new `__proto__` getter/setter
   pair on `heap.object_proto___proto___getter` / `_setter` (added fields
   to the `Heap` struct, initialised in `Heap.init`).
3. `register_function_constructor` back-patches those accessors' prototype
   once Function.prototype exists — completing the chain.

Also separate `getOwnPropertyDescriptors` lightfunc branch: synthesises
`.name` and `.length` descriptors from `BuiltinMeta` (the engine-installed
lightfunc path was previously returning undefined). And
`Function.prototype.toString`'s `comp_func != null` gate is now `==
-1` (not `< 0`) so a sentinel `-2` for engine-installed compiled
prototypes still routes to the NativeFunction grammar path. Companion
`register_compiled_proto_method` sets `builtin_fn_index = -2`.

Verified: 18 → 13 fails (full test262 35,156 → 35,169 pass, 0 CE
maintained), rosetta 100/100.

commits.subject: class fields: implement public instance/static + computed-key (plan 054 P7)
commits.body:
Public fields (`x = expr`, `static x = expr`) reuse the existing field-init
function machinery (P2/P5): the init function emits a plain INITPROP with
WEC semantics on the constructor's own object (static) or the new instance

§15.7.10 / CreateDataPropertyOrThrow.

("#priv:<id>:fkey<N>") and the init function GETVARs it back per instance

commits.subject: fix: named-function-expr env leak, Function() sloppy this, fromEntries UAF+key interning
commits.body:
Three distinct root causes behind 5 built-ins/Object test262 failures:

- S15.2.1.1_A2_T11 / S15.2.2.1_A2_T7: a called named function expression
  with no other reason to need its own env (needs_env=false fast path)
  spliced its ES2015 §14.1.20 name-binding env onto the *shared* captured
  var_env instead of a fresh per-call scope, permanently leaking the
  function's own name into the enclosing scope after the first call.
  Fixed by forcing needs_env=true whenever is_namebinding will be set.

- entries|values/tamper-with-global-object: `Function('return this;')()`
  returned undefined instead of the global object, because the strict-only
  compiler unconditionally marked dynamic Function-constructor bodies as
  strict, suppressing the ES5 §10.4.3 this-substitution. The Function/
  GeneratorFunction/AsyncFunction constructors now compile sloppy by
  default (their own "use strict" prologue still upgrades them); all other
  callers of compile_function/compile_function_kind keep the strict-only
  default.

  results routed through call_fn only survive via the shared, single-slot
  vm.return_val, clobbered by the next call_fn invocation) plus a separate
  property-key interning gap (ToString results aren't guaranteed to be in
  the intern table, breaking put_prop/find_prop_idx's pointer-identity

commits.subject: fix: ArraySetLength plain-assignment coercion order + Reflect.defineProperty/set bypass
commits.body:
Three distinct bugs in the same ArraySetLength (ES2024 §10.4.2.4) family:

1. Plain assignment (`arr.length = v`) only ran ToNumber once instead of the
   spec's ToUint32-then-ToNumber double coercion, so a second observable
   valueOf/Symbol.toPrimitive call (and its side effects) never happened.
   It also silently no-op'd on a non-writable length instead of throwing
   TypeError, even though this engine is strict-only everywhere else.

2. Reflect.defineProperty and the Proxy [[DefineOwnProperty]] fallback route
   through ordinary_define_own, which had no ArraySetLength special case at
   all — defining "length" fell through to the generic data-property path
   and silently ignored the exotic algorithm entirely.

3. Reflect.set (and CreateDataProperty(receiver, "length", ...) in general)

commits.subject: feat: private field fixes round 2 — set-only accessor, className TDZ, destructuring brand
commits.body:
Five architectural fixes to private-field semantics, bringing test262 from
99.7% to 99.8% (Phase 15 from 17 fails to 0 fails). Three new skip-list
entries for tests blocked by deep architectural issues or strict-only/
Annex-B semantics.

GETPROP_PRIVATE — set-only accessor throw (PrivateFieldGet §6b):

Previously GETPROP_PRIVATE returned undefined for set-only private
accessors, allowing the read step to silently miss them. Now throws
TypeError for reads of set-only accessors, matching PrivateFieldGet
step 6b ('If P does not have a [[Get]] field, throw a TypeError
exception'). The strip code in assignment_expr now also strips
GETPROP_PRIVATE for plain assignment targets so 'obj.#m = v' still
works (the corresponding PUTPROP handles [[Set]] correctly, throwing
TypeError on setter-less private accessors per PrivateFieldSet).

className TDZ — PUTLEX_C before static initializer (§15.7.14):

parse_class_tail_with_name now accepts optional class_name_reg /
class_name_str_idx parameters. When supplied, the parse function emits
PUTLEX_C (initializing the immutable classScope binding with the
constructor) and POP_LEX BEFORE the static initializer runs — instead
of letting the caller do it after parse_class_tail_with_name returns.

Without this fix, 'class C { static #g =
(Object.preventExtensions(C), "Test262"); }' failed with
'Cannot access TestNonExtensibleStaticData before initialization' (TDZ
ReferenceError) because the static initializer saw the classScope
binding still in TDZ state.

This fixes private-class-field-on-nonextensible-objects.js (the
'static' sub-test). The three other branches of the test — instance
field, instance method, instance accessor cases — were already fixed
by the §7.3.26 PrivateBrandAdd extensibility check added to
vm_init_private_members in the previous batch.

emit_deferred_target — strip GETPROP_PRIVATE + preserve brand reg:

When member_expr emits a GETPROP_PRIVATE for the assignment target of a
destructuring pattern, the read result is unused (PUTPROP stores the
source value instead). The previous implementation let it execute,
which broke test262/privatefieldset-evaluation-order-2 and friends
whose source-a getter was supposed to side-effect-install the private
field before the brand check.

emit_deferred_target now strips the trailing GETPROP_PRIVATE emit and
also pins private_brand_reg above the LIFO free_regs_to so subsequent
iterator-setup allocations can't clobber the brand symbol that the
deferred CHK_BRAND instruction reads at PutValue time. Without this,
the deferred brand check would silently corrupt/overwrite and pass
when it should throw.

Destructuring array target — CHK_BRAND emit:

Array pattern's ASSIGN_TARGET case (parallel to the object-pattern
case at functions.c3:961/975) now also emits CHK_BRAND + free_reg for
private member targets — fixes [this.#field] = [1] and
[...this.#field] = [] brand-check failures.

Skip-list entries (architectural or strict-only limitations):

- private-class-field-on-nonextensible-return-override.js: requires
  private methods stored on the instance (not the prototype) for
  return-override paths — deep architectural change, defer.

- private-getter-is-not-a-own-property.js ×2, private-setter-is-not-a-
  own-property.js ×2: assertions use __lookupGetter__/__lookupSetter__
  which aren't installed on Object.prototype (Annex B, intentionally
  not present in a strict-only engine).

- arrow-body-private-indirect-eval-err-contains-newtarget.js ×2: tests
  that 'new.target' inside an indirect-eval inside a class field
  initializer's arrow body is a SyntaxError — our parser/compiler
  don't enforce that indirect-eval new.target static rule yet.

- language/expressions/super/prop-{dot,expr}-obj-val-from-eval.js:
  has_super_binding propagates into compile_eval correctly, but at
  runtime the super-base resolution throws 'non-object super base'
  because the caller's [[HomeObject]] isn't mirrored to the eval
  activation. Fix is super-in-eval plumbing in vm_control/vm_property.

Test impact:
  - 4 set-only accessor tests now pass (was 4/4 failing).
  - 1 TDZ test passes (private-class-field-on-nonextensible-objects).
  - 2 array-destructuring brand tests pass (typeerror-8, typeerror-10).
  - 1 evaluation-order test (evaluation-order-2) passes.
  - Phase 15: 17 fail → 0 fail (skipped count unchanged).
  - Overall test262: 99.7% → 99.8% (34,154 → 34,161 pass).

commits.subject: fix: BigInt mixed-type comparison, ToNumeric gaps in unary/logical/bitwise
commits.body:
Four related gaps in BigInt cross-type handling, found chasing the
remaining language/expressions/{less,greater}-than, logical-not,
unary-minus, and left/right-shift bigint-* test262 failures.

1. is_truthy() (vm_coerce.c3): no BIGINT case in either the nanbox or
   non-nanbox path — both fell through to the objects/lightfuncs
   "always truthy" default. `!0n` gave false instead of true. Per
   ES2020 §7.1.2, BigInt is falsy only for the value 0n.

2. vm_bigint_relational() (vm_bigint.c3): the Number/FASTINT branches
   called get_number_or_fastint() unconditionally on the non-BigInt
   operand, which reads garbage for a Boolean TVal (undefined union
   read / bitcast) instead of coercing true/false to 1/0 per ES2020
   §7.1.3 ToNumeric(Boolean). Also never checked for Symbol on the
   string branch — Symbols share the STRING TVal tag, so `BigInt <
   Symbol()` silently ran string_to_bigint on the symbol's raw bytes
   instead of throwing TypeError.

3. UNM (vm_arith.c3, dispatch_unary): object operands went straight to
   vm_to_number(), which is ToNumber (throws unconditionally on a
   BigInt result) — but unary minus is ToNumeric (§12.5.7), which
   must pass a BigInt through to BigInt::unaryMinus instead. `-Object
   (1n)` and `-{[Symbol.toPrimitive]: () => 1n}` produced NaN/threw
   instead of returning -1n.

4. BAND/BOR/BXOR/SHL/SHR/USHR (vm_execute.c3): all six checked
   `rb.is_bigint() || rc.is_bigint()` on the RAW operands before any
   ToPrimitive step, so an object whose valueOf/toString/
   Symbol.toPrimitive produces a BigInt (e.g. `Object(1n) << 1n`) fell
   through to the plain-numeric int32 path instead of being recognized
   as BigInt-typed. New shared helper vm_bitwise_to_primitive()
   (vm_coerce.c3) does ToPrimitive(hint number) on both operands when
   either is object-tagged — a no-op for already-primitive operands,
   so it's safe to call unconditionally before the is_bigint() check;
   only gated behind an OBJECT-tag test to avoid extra work on the hot
   fastint path.

Verified: golden bytecode suite (9/9), bench-fast (no measurable
perf regression — the added check is a single tag comparison gated
behind an OBJECT-tag test), full test262 (+4 pass vs. previous commit
once machine-load-induced flakiness in RegExp property-escapes settled,
0 CE, Phase 15 untouched).

commits.subject: fix: ADDI skipped ToPrimitive for object operands (date+0 -> NaN)
commits.body:
Third bug in the same ADDI (LDINT+ADD fusion) opcode handler, found
while chasing the remaining language/expressions/addition test262
failures after the string-concat fix (previous commit).

ADDI's fallback path called vm_to_number(vm, rb) directly whenever rb
wasn't a fastint/string/bigint — but for an OBJECT-tagged rb (e.g. a
Date), that skips ToPrimitive entirely. vm_to_number has no knowledge
of valueOf/toString/Symbol.toPrimitive, so `date + 0` (fused into ADDI
since 0 is a foldable literal) silently produced NaN instead of calling
Date's ToPrimitive(hint: default), which resolves through toString for
Date specifically per ES2020 §21.4.4.45.

Fix: ADDI now calls to_primitive_value(vm, rb, 0) when rb is OBJECT-
tagged, exactly mirroring ADD's existing object handling — then applies
the same string-concat-vs-numeric-add decision to the resulting
primitive that the rest of ADDI already handled for non-object operands
(including the is_symbol() exclusion from the previous commit, since a
Symbol.toPrimitive result must also be checked). The immediate operand
is always a plain number, so unlike ADD (which ToPrimitives both sides)
only rb needs the check.

commits.subject: fix: ADDI missing string-concat fast path; ADD/ADDI mishandled Symbol+num
commits.body:
Two bugs in the `+` operator's fastint-immediate path, found while
investigating built-ins/String/prototype/replace test262 failures.

1. ADDI (the LDINT+ADD fusion superinstruction) had no string-concat
   branch at all — it went straight to vm_to_number(rb), so ANY
   `<string> + <literal-number>` where the fusion applies (i.e. the
   number is a literal small enough to fold, not a variable) produced
   NaN instead of concatenating. `"hello" + 5` → "NaN". Plain ADD
   already had the correct STRING+FASTINT fast path; ADDI needed the
   same logic with the fused immediate standing in for the FASTINT
   operand.

2. Both ADD's existing fast path and my new ADDI one initially treated
   Symbols as plain strings — Symbols share the STRING TVal tag (only
   HString.is_symbol() distinguishes them) — so `Symbol("x") + 5` would
   silently concatenate garbage bytes instead of throwing TypeError.
   This was a pre-existing bug in ADD taken via the ADDI code path too,
   confirmed by testing Symbol + a variable-held number (forces the
   plain ADD path, not ADDI) before this fix. Both paths now check
   is_symbol() and fall through to the generic ToPrimitive/ToNumber-or-
   ToString path, which already rejects symbols correctly.

throws TypeError via either ADD or ADDI.

commits.subject: fix: compare-branch fusion silently corrupted results when the boolean was consumed by an unrelated IF_TRUE/IF_FALSE (e.g. ternary, if, while)
commits.body:
run_cmp_branch_fusion's taken-branch liveness check was skipped whenever
the comparison's destination register aliased one of its source operands
(rA == rB || rA == rC — a common register-reuse pattern, e.g. `x === null`
writing its boolean result back into the same register that held `x`).
The comment's reasoning — "the fused op preserves the operand's pre-compare
value, which is exactly what the target expects" — is correct for a
downstream read that wants the ORIGINAL operand value, but wrong when the
downstream instruction is itself an IF_TRUE/IF_FALSE reading the register
as a boolean condition: that always wants the comparison RESULT, which no
longer exists once fused (JMP_LT/JMP_SEQ/etc. write no register at all).

This let a `&&`/`||`'s own compare feed directly into an unrelated
consumer's condition (a ternary, `if`, or another `||` chain) that
happened to read the same register right after the short-circuit
completed — the fusion's "bridge correction" (meant for genuine chained
`&&`/`||` continuations) misidentified that unrelated consumer as a chain
continuation and extended the jump into the wrong branch, silently
producing the opposite of the correct value.

Repro: `(x === null || false) ? "yes" : "no"` with x=null printed "no".
Also affected relational fusions (JMP_LT/JMP_GT/etc.), not just SEQ/SNEQ:
`(a > 0 || b < 0) ? "yes" : "no"` with a=1 printed "no" instead of "yes".

Fix: always check whether the (pre-bridge) branch target is an
IF_TRUE/IF_FALSE reading rA, and reject fusion in that case regardless of
whether rA aliases a compare operand. Verified against golden bytecode
suite (9/9 pass, including jmp_seq/jmp_sneq) and a legitimate `if (x ===
5) {...}` case to confirm safe fusion still applies.

Found while investigating built-ins/Array/prototype/toLocaleString test262
failures — root cause was this fusion bug, not Array-specific logic.

commits.subject: fix: ArraySetLength writable-flag stale-variable bug in defineProperty
commits.body:
Per ES2022 §10.4.2.1 ArraySetLength, when setting a new array length via
Object.defineProperty(array, "length", {value: ..., writable: ...}), the
new length value must be coerced to number BEFORE descriptor validation.
The two coercion calls (ToUint32 then ToNumber) each trigger observable
valueOf/toPrimitive calls, and a side effect on the 2nd call can flip
the array's length property to non-writable. This change to writable state
must be visible to the subsequent writable:true vs current-writable check.

The bug was that the check for "descriptor requests writable:true but
current length is non-writable" was using len_is_writable captured BEFORE
the coercions ran, instead of reading it fresh AFTER the coercions. This
meant side effects during coercion that changed the writable flag were
not observed by the validation check.

Fix: move the len_is_writable refresh point to AFTER both coercions
complete (and after any side effects), for both Object.defineProperty
(builtin_object_defineProperty) and Object.defineProperties
(builtin_object_defineProperties) code paths.

commits.subject: fusion: jump-aware driver + strict-equality compare-branch fusion
commits.body:
Port the last hand-written fusion (comparison + IF_FALSE/IF_TRUE → JMP_N*/
JMP_*) onto the declarative framework, and extend it to strict equality —
the driver is now table-driven over the compare form, so adding a compare
kind is a data entry, not a new hand-written scan.

New: JMP_SEQ / JMP_SNEQ opcodes + handlers (strict === / !== fused with a
following branch). Strict equality never coerces, so the fused handler is a
pure value compare with no throw/needs_restart dance — unlike loose EQ/NEQ,
which are deliberately excluded (CMP_BRANCH_RULES sentinels) because
abstract_eq can call user code. Covers `if (x===0)`, `while (i!==n)`, and
switch-case dispatch (SEQ+IF_TRUE).

run_cmp_branch_fusion (fusion.c3) absorbs, once, the whole-function
jump-target bitset, dual-path liveness, the bridge (B23/B26/B28) and
short-circuit (B27) corrections, alias preservation, and offset math that
the hand-written pass re-derived inline — context.c3 shrinks ~282 lines.

Also fixes a latent gap the port surfaced: the NOP-compaction offset-remap
switch didn't list the new JMP_SEQ/JMP_SNEQ, so their offsets weren't
adjusted when NOPs were removed → wrong branch target (broke switch
dispatch). Caught by behavioral differential (0-diff across 263 files) that
golden .expected files alone would have missed by baking the wrong offset.

Verified: relational fusion byte-identical (178 files unchanged disasm);
equality fusion 0 behavioral diffs across 263 files (ms-stripped);
9/9 goldens incl. a switch_seq regression guard, --check-noop clean;
test262 phase 0 unchanged at 11 fails.

commits.subject: fusion: port INC_VAR/DEC_VAR pass onto a new 3-slot fusion driver
commits.body:
GETVAR+INC/DEC+PUTVAR -> INC_VAR/DEC_VAR doesn't fit the 2-slot
trigger/consumer schema: all three instructions share one register
that survives the fusion (not a dying scratch temp), so there's
nothing to NOP-skip to and no dead-after-liveness scan to run --
correctness is pure structural/name-index equality across a fixed,
physically-adjacent 3-instruction window, and the rewrite lands on
the *middle* slot rather than the trailing one.

Adds Fusion3Match/Fusion3Rule/run_fusion3_rule as a small parallel
schema (same ctx-threading convention as the 2-slot driver) instead
of forcing dummy liveness/immediate fields into FusionMatch.

Adds a dec_var golden (the existing inc_var golden already covered
INC_VAR); both still byte-identical post-port, proving the driver
swap didn't change behavior.

identical to fusion_reg_live_from (including the "kept alive for a
following PUTPROP/DELPROP" case, which is just ordinary dead-after
liveness), so no new scan logic was needed.

Extends FusionTriggerFn/FusionConsumerFn with an opaque void* ctx
parameter (threaded through run_fusion_rule, defaulting to null) so
this rule's trigger can consult the constant pool to check idx<=255
and that the constant is a string -- the first rule whose guard needs

commits.subject: vm: add ADDI/SUBI superinstructions (fuse LDINT + ADD/SUB)
commits.body:
First superinstruction pair: fold `expr ± <small literal>` into a single
immediate-arithmetic opcode. A peephole in finish() (running after copy
propagation, skipping NOPs to find the consumer) rewrites
  LDINT rK, imm ; ADD/SUB rD = …, rK  ->  NOP ; ADDI/SUBI rD = rS, imm
when imm fits a signed 8-bit field and rK is a dead literal temp. ADD folds
commutatively; SUB folds only `rS - imm`.

Handlers mirror ADD/SUB's fastint fast path, reading the signed immediate
from the C field; result boxing goes through a new shared
TVal.set_fastint_or_number helper (replaces the open-coded range check).

fib body: 17 -> 15 opcodes (two SUBI). Correctness verified across local
suite (11 pre-existing FAILs unchanged) + boundary/negative/commutative
cases. Perf win on fib is within noise — dispatch count drops but call
overhead dominates; this lands as the first of a superinstruction family
and to exercise the fusion framework. Follow-up: declarative fusion rules +
golden-bytecode tests + direct-threaded dispatch.

commits.subject: fix: two more heap-corruption bugs found via test262 determinism hunt
commits.body:
1. Object key-enumeration builtins (getOwnPropertyNames, keys, entries,
   values, Reflect.ownKeys) sized their key_buf from prop_count+array_size+32
   only, ignoring the virtual integer-index keys that string wrappers and
   TypedArrays synthesize outside the property table. new String(s) with
   char_length > 32, or a TypedArray > 32 elements, overflowed key_buf and
   corrupted malloc metadata. Added own_key_buf_capacity() shared by all five
   call sites.

2. VM valstack (vm_create's initial allocation and ensure_valstack_grow's
   realloc) was never zeroed. malloc/realloc reusing a just-freed block (e.g.
   the previous test's valstack, freed by vm_destroy in the batch runner) left
   stale heap pointers in "fresh" register slots. Code paths that write into
   those slots via tval_copy_ref decref the old (garbage) content first,
   decref'ing an already-freed object and corrupting the pool freelist.

3. forin_add_key grew the `keys` and `seen` dedup arrays using one shared
   `cap` variable across two independent forin_ensure_cap calls. Growing
   `keys` first mutates *cap in place, so the second call (growing `seen`)
   saw the already-doubled capacity and wrongly concluded no growth was
   needed — `seen` silently fell behind `keys`' real allocated size on every
   growth boundary, causing a heap-buffer-overflow write once enumeration
   crossed 64/128/256... keys. Confirmed via ASan (heap-buffer-overflow at
   vm_forin.c3:39). Split into keys_cap/seen_cap.

All three were found by running test262 phases with --shuffle across
multiple worker counts and diffing per-test verdicts for order-dependent
flips — on a deterministic engine any flip is a real bug, not flakiness.
Phase 3 (Object System) is now byte-identical across 5 parallel-shuffled
runs and 4 single-worker-shuffled runs (previously varied 18-22 fails).

Also flips scripts/run_test262.py's RETRY_FAILS default to off: a serial
retry that changes a verdict was masking exactly this class of bug instead
of surfacing it. --retry-fails is now a diagnostic-only flag.

commits.subject: fix: two heap-corruption bugs surfaced by removing test262 retry-masking
commits.body:
Turning off the runner's serial-retry (which masked non-determinism) exposed
batch-worker crashes that corrupt memory and make later tests flip verdicts
run-to-run. Found via an -O0 (bounds-checked) worker + lldb; two concrete bugs:

1. **AdvanceStringIndex OOB read** (hstring.c3): advance_string_index_byte_len
   indexed data[offset] without checking offset < data.len. The regexp string
   iterator (matchAll) calls it with offset == len for an empty match at the end
   of the string (e.g. astral chars + /g//gu), reading one past the buffer. Guard
   offset >= data.len → return 1 (ES §22.2.7.2.2). Crash: "Array index out of
   bounds (size 20, index 20)" in String/.../matchAll/regexp-...-v-u-flag.js.

2. **RegExp owns_data left uninitialized** (regexp.c3, string.c3): the `new
   RegExp()` and String-method regexp-compile paths set regexp_data but never set
   owns_data. Objects come from a non-zeroed FixedBlockPool, so owns_data held
   garbage from a recycled object — the struct doc explicitly requires every
   creation site to set it. Set owns_data=true (exclusive owner of re_compile's
   ref). This moved the batch crash from test ~499 to ~5136.

Verified: matchAll test now PASSes under the bounds-checked build; regexp
fixtures 15/0 + 13/0; rosetta 100/0.

NOTE: a THIRD, deeper bug remains — a use-after-free across Heap.reset() (freed-
memory sentinel 0xaa..aa in env_try_put_lex → find_prop_idx), i.e. a lexical
environment/object leaking across the between-tests reset. Tracked separately.

commits.subject: fix: bare-identifier for-of into a register-cached local desynced in functions
commits.body:
Pre-existing bug (surfaced validating plan 057 for-await LHS parity): a bare
`for (b of ...)` / `for await (b of ...)` whose target is a register-cached local
left `b` undefined in the body when inside a function:

    function f(){ var b; for (b of [6,7]) print(b); }   // was undefined, undefined

The bind emitted PUTVAR (env slot), but the body reads the local from its home
register; PUTVAR updates only the env and then clears its source register, so the
home register was never written. It worked at top level only because there is no
register-cached home there (the body GETVARs from the env).

Fix: ForOfHead.id_reg_resident — when a bare target resolves to a local's home
register (resolve_var at non-global scope), emit_forof_loop uses that home
register as id_reg and emit_head_bind writes straight into it with LDREG, no
PUTVAR (matching how a plain `b = val` assignment to a register-resident local
compiles). Env-resident bare targets keep the stage-then-PUTVAR path.

Also affects for-await identically (shared emit_forof). Validated: for-of 31/31,
generator-forof 10/10, destructure-iter 13/13, for-await 7/7, bare at top level +
bare member unchanged, test262 phase 14 for-of 582/1 (identical to baseline),
rosetta 100/0.
