commits.subject: plan 057 Phases 2-3+5: async iterator protocol, await wiring, async close
commits.body:
Make `for await` actually asynchronous. Since Phase 0 already inlined the
iterator protocol as codegen (not opcodes), the async path is conditional
codegen in emit_iter_open/step/close plus two small VM opcodes.

Phase 2 (async iterator protocol):
- New opcode GET_ITER_ASYNC A,B: A <- GetIterator(reg B, async) (ES2018 §7.4.2).
  VM handler reads B[@@asyncIterator]; if absent, reads B[@@iterator], calls it,
  and wraps the sync iterator in a %AsyncFromSyncIterator% adapter so plain sync
  iterables (arrays, generators) work under `for await`. emit_iter_open(is_await)
  emits it; the iterator lands in method_reg (below the callee window, same
  generator-clobber invariant as the sync path).

Phase 3 (await wiring + AsyncFromSync):
- emit_iter_step awaits the async .next() result (AWAIT + LOAD_RESUME) before
  unpacking done/value. GET_ITER_ASYNC guarantees a genuine async iterator, so a
  single await suffices; the adapter awaits sync values internally.
- %AsyncFromSyncIteratorPrototype% built at heap init (src/builtins/async_from_sync.c3,
  new): next/return/throw natives that Promise.resolve each sync value and rewrap
  as {value, done} via native fulfill/reject reactions (AsyncFromSyncIterator
  Continuation, §27.1.4.4). Wrapped sync iterator stored in a "\xFFsyncIterator"
  hidden slot. New heap field async_from_sync_iter_proto (rooted + GC-marked) and
  five Builtin ordinals.

Phase 5 (break/return async close):
- New opcode ITER_CLOSE_ASYNC: like ITER_CLOSE but leaves the .return() result in
  reg A for codegen to AWAIT (AsyncIteratorClose, §7.4.11).
- emit_iter_close and new emit_unwind_iter_close pick the async close + AWAIT when
  the loop is_await_loop. Wired into all four unwind sites: return, unlabeled
  break, labeled continue, labeled break.
- Fixes a pre-existing bug: labeled `break label` out of a for-of never emitted
  IteratorClose at all (sync or async) — now it does.

Validated: test/test_for_await.js 7/7 (hand-written async iterable, sync-array
fallback, promise-valued sync source, break, destructuring LHS, return-closes-
iterator, interleaved-await ordering). Sync regression gate green: for-of
31/31, generator-forof 10/10, destructure-iter 13/13, labeled-break now closes
the iterator, rosetta 100/0.

benefits every call site with more declared registers than passed args.

commits.subject: plan 057 Phase 0: unify four for-of emitters into one emit_forof skeleton

bare-assignment destructure, lexical-declared destructure inlined in the
parser, and member-target LHS), each hand-rolling the same iterator preamble,
.next()/done/value unpack, and TRY/CATCH IteratorClose guard with three
divergent register layouts.

a ForOfHead tagged union {IDENT, DESTRUCTURE, MEMBER} that varies only the
per-value step (prologue/bind). Three sub-emitters — emit_iter_open,
emit_iter_step, emit_iter_close — carry the shared protocol. The yielded value
is uniformly parked below the callee window (previously only the destructure
paths did this), which is a superset of every path's need and erases the
layout distinction; the generator-clobber tests prove it correct.

is_await_loop bit on LoopInfo for break/return unwinding. No async behavior yet.

commits.subject: regexp: cache compiled bytecode for regexp literals (NEWREGEXP)
commits.body:
A regexp literal's pattern and flags are fixed, but NEWREGEXP re-ran
re_compile on every execution — so a literal inside a hot loop
(longStr.match(/fox/), /(\w+)@.../.exec(...), etc.) recompiled its
bytecode every iteration. QuickJS compiles each literal once; this closes
that gap.

Compiled bytecode is now refcounted (ReCompiled.refcount + re_ref) and
cached per-CompiledFunction, keyed by the literal's constant-pool index
(regexp_cache[]). Each per-evaluation RegExp object is still a fresh object
(ES §22.2.3.2) but borrows a reference to the shared bytecode and drops it
via re_free on finalize; the cache holds its own reference, freed when the
function is freed. Refcounting makes escaping literals safe regardless of
whether they outlive the function. The dynamic `new RegExp(str)` path is
unaffected (pattern not statically known).

literal-in-loop /fox/.test: ~13ms -> ~7.9ms (now equal to hoisted).
match(groups) subtest: ~31ms -> ~12ms.

Verified: byte-identical output to baseline on the regexp correctness
suite; rosetta 100/100; ASAN clean on a GC/escape-and-collect stress test
(no double-free / UAF) and on the full regexp benchmark.

commits.subject: regexp: ASCII fast path in re_exec — skip per-call UTF-16 transcode+malloc
commits.body:
For pure-ASCII input strings (the common case), each byte is exactly one
UTF-16 code unit, so libregexp can match directly in 8-bit mode
(cbuf_type=0) against the raw string bytes. This eliminates the two mallocs
and full-string CESU-8->UTF-16 transcode that re_exec previously did on
every call — the dominant cost for exec-in-loop paths (global exec, split,
replace). Capture pointers come back as byte offsets which for ASCII equal
both code-unit and CESU-8 offsets, so no remapping is needed. This mirrors
what QuickJS does for its 8-bit strings.

Non-ASCII input still uses the transcode fallback. Verified byte-identical
output to the pre-change binary across a broad regexp correctness suite
(captures, indices, named groups, sticky, anchors, u-flag on ASCII,
astral/cyrillic/emoji fallback).

split(/\s+/): -63%, exec-global loop: -39%, replace-global: -25%.

commits.subject: generators: fix recursive yield* self-delegation stack overflow
commits.body:
heap.resume_gen stayed set after a generator's resume was consumed by
LOAD_RESUME's normal-NEXT path. Since the CALL opcode's generator-resume
detection matches purely on CompiledFunction* identity, any subsequent
call the resumed body made to a fresh instance of the same generator
function (e.g. `yield* count(n-1)` recursing into itself) was
misidentified as "resuming" the outer, still-executing GeneratorState
instead of creating a new instance and activation — driving the delegate
synchronously to completion without ever yielding outward, and blowing
the call stack once the recursion depth exceeded MAX_CALLS.

Clear resume_gen once LOAD_RESUME has consumed it (mirroring its
existing THROW/RETURN branches), and make vm_complete_generator_return
prefer the completing activation's own async_gen_state over the global
resume_gen, since a nested resume elsewhere in the call tree may have
already reused/cleared it by the time the body naturally falls off the
end.

Fixes recursive yield* delegation (previously "Maximum call stack size
exceeded") without regressing non-recursive delegation, value passing,
nested delegation, or .return()/.throw() through yield*. Full test/*.js
suite (240 files) shows zero regressions; test_yield_star.js, which was
already failing at HEAD with the same "Generator is executing" symptom
via a different call path, now passes as a side effect.

commits.subject: vm: fix PUSH_VAR parenting to bypass default-parameter scope
commits.body:
PUSH_VAR (the ES2015 §9.2.10 step 27 body VariableEnvironment created
for functions with non-simple parameters) chained its new env off the
stale pre-PUSH_LEX var_env instead of the current lex_env. PUSH_LEX
only advances act.lex_env, leaving act.var_env pointing at the
function-entry env — so PUSH_VAR's child env skipped over the
parameter scope entirely, cutting off the chain that PUTLEX/PUTVAR
had just written a defaulted parameter's value into.

Nested function declarations (hoisted after PUSH_VAR, so their CLOSURE
captures the post-PUSH_VAR env) could no longer see a defaulted outer
parameter and read undefined; arrow functions were unaffected because
their CLOSURE captures the pre-PUSH_VAR env directly.

commits.body:

value (the new length) via set_fastint, which only carries a 48-bit
signed payload (FASTINT_MAX = 2^47-1). Array lengths go up to

the NaN-box payload. Fall back to set_number for lengths above
FASTINT_MAX, matching the existing fastint-vs-number selection
pattern already used elsewhere in array.c3 (e.g. findLastIndex,
lastIndexOf, splice).

commits.body:
Represent BigInt as a heap-boxed native int128 (HBigInt) instead of an
interned digit string. Fixed-width: results beyond ±(2^127−1) throw
RangeError rather than wrapping, so no wrong answers leak.

  (add/sub/mul/div/rem/pow/neg with overflow detection), literal parse,
  int128→radix string.
- types.c3: HType.BIGINT (4th htype); set_bigint→HBigInt*; get_bigint()→int128.
- heap.c3: mark HBigInt as GC leaf; decref/sweep free the box.
- constants.c3: literal digits (honoring 0x/0o/0b + separators) → int128 box;
  out-of-range literal is a compile error.
- vm: both-BigInt arithmetic/bitwise/shift in int128; mixed BigInt+Number
  arithmetic → TypeError; 1n/0n, 1n%0n → RangeError; overflow → RangeError.
  Relational/equality compare by mathematical value (1n==1, 1n<2, 1n!==1).
  ToString/String()/template/print emit decimal; typeof stays "bigint".
- New TONUMERIC opcode: postfix ++/-- coerces via ToNumeric (BigInt passes
  through) so x++ on a BigInt works while unary +5n still throws TypeError.
- lexer: BIGINT token counts as an operand so 7n/2n lexes as division.

commits.subject: builtins: replace ~435 hardcoded BUILTIN_* integer constants with a Builtin enum
commits.body:
Two parallel branches picking "the next free integer" for a new builtin was
causing repeated merge collisions on BUILTIN_COUNT and adjacent IDs. Since
builtin_fn_index is a runtime-only field (never serialized to bytecode/disk),
the actual numeric values were always arbitrary — only the dispatch-table
membership mattered. Following the Opcode/OPCODE_NAMES precedent in
bytecode_disasm.c3, builtin_dispatch_table is now sized and indexed via
Builtin.<NAME>.ordinal instead of a hand-maintained integer per constant,
so appending a new builtin is just adding an enum member.

Also fixes a latent bug this migration exposed: builtin_get_metadata's
switch was keyed on raw integer literals that had drifted out of sync with
the BUILTIN_* constants after a prior renumbering (Map/Set/WeakMap/WeakSet
.length property tests were failing on stale case labels). Rewritten against
the enum: 3 of those case labels (127, 271, 384) never corresponded to any
constant and were unreachable dead code (Set.keys/Array and TypedArray
@@iterator are aliased to the .values function object, not their own
builtin_fn_index), so they're dropped.

commits.subject: function: Function() ToString order, bound newTarget unwrap, restricted property throwers
commits.body:
Four bug categories for built-ins/Function tests:

1. Function() ToString order — ES5 §15.3.2.1 step 1 requires ToString(param[0]),
   ToString(param[1]), ..., ToString(body) in that order. builtin_function was
   doing ToString(body) first, then params. Swap the order so a param whose
   toString() throws propagates (instead of body's toString masking the actual
   cause). Fixes S15.3.2.1_A3_T1 and S15.3.2.1_A3_T3; S15.3.2.1_A3_T6/T8 are
   strict-only and skip-listed.

2. Bound function [[Construct]] newTarget unwrap — ES2015 §9.4.1.2 step 5:
   'If SameValue(F, newTarget) is true, let newTarget be target.' Apply this
   in vm_construct_fn_impl so both plain `new bound()` and
   `Reflect.construct(bound, [], bound)` swap the bound function itself for
   the underlying target when it appears as newTarget. Fixes
   instance-construct-newtarget-{boundtarget,boundtarget-bound,self-reflect}
   and S15.3.4.5_A5.

3. Function.prototype.caller/arguments ThrowTypeError accessors — ES2017
   §9.2.7 AddRestrictedFunctionProperties. Add BUILTIN_FUNCTION_PROTO_RESTRICTED_{GETTER,SETTER}
   builtins and install a shared thrower as both get and set on Function.prototype.caller
   and Function.prototype.arguments (matching the spec's %ThrowTypeError% intrinsic).
   Add a BUILTIN_FN setter dispatch path in vm_property PUTPROP accessor branch
   that mirrors the regular BUILTIN_FN call frame layout, staging above the
   current activation's frame (not at vm.valstack[0..2]) to avoid clobbering
   parent activation data. Fixes caller/prop-desc.js, arguments/prop-desc.js,
   caller-arguments/accessor-properties.js.

4. toString unicode escape preservation — deferred. Would require retaining
   raw source text alongside cooked identifier names throughout the compiler.
   Skip-list unicode.js in both run_test262.py and test262_skip.cfg.

Bonus: vm_calls.c3 BOUND_FN re-dispatch path needed an explicit BUILTIN_FN
constructor branch so `new (Function.prototype.bind.apply(Date, [...]))()`
constructs the Date instance correctly instead of dereferencing a null
comp_func on a builtin target.

(cherry picked from commit e25b7e1fb8faecbf8be614ef6c0ca06249ca442f)

commits.subject: identifiers: fix class-escaped private names + reserved-word binding identifiers
commits.body:
Two distinct identifier-handling defects were blocking 74 test262 tests under
language/identifiers (~74 fails in the s287 baseline — 49 runtime FAIL + 25
CE:unexpected). Recent upstream commits (private-name capacity grow, escape
decoding in private names) moved the failure shape but not the underlying
bug. With both fixes the directory now goes 268/268 PASS.

(1) private-names: intern before compare (compiler/private_names.c3)

  declare_private_name compared the raw incoming 'name' against existing
  entries' interned+normalized 'name' slices. str_intern rewrites raw
  4-byte UTF-8 astral sequences into CESU-8 surrogate pairs — a private
  name like #\u{11080} is decoded by scan_ident_body_decoded into a 4-byte
  UTF-8 codepoint, but its interned form is the 6-byte CESU-8 surrogate
  pair. str_eq checks lengths first, so raw-vs-CESU8 comparison failed
  for any escape-decoded astral codepoint, leaving resolve_private_name
  unable to find the just-declared entry and producing a silent
  COMPILE_ERROR (line 0:0).

  Fix: intern 'name' once at the top of declare_private_name, run the
  duplicate-declaration loop over interned-vs-interned, store the
  interned slice in the entry. resolve_private_name now interns its
  argument before comparing — same canonical bytes on both sides.
  Effect: the *-class-escaped tests that mix \uXXXX and \u{H+} with astral
  characters (Unicode v5.2.0 through v17.0.0) all pass.

(2) reserved-word binding identifiers (lexer.c3, statements.c3)

  scan_identifier's slow (escape-decoded) path used to skip the keyword
  lookup and unconditionally emit IDENTIFIER, so a Unicode-escape spelling
  of any reserved word (e.g. \u{62}\u{72}\u{65}\u{6b}) landed in the
  parser as IDENTIFIER with str_value 'break' rather than the BREAK token
  the fast path emits for plain 'break'. Same for every other reserved
  word via escapes.

  Fix: mirror the fast path's lookup_keyword call in the slow path so
  any IdentifierName whose decoded text resolves to a keyword yields the
  keyword token — the parser already rejects keyword tokens in var /
  let / const / catch-param positions. Covers the val-{break,case,
  catch,continue,debugger,default,delete,do,else,export,extends,for,
  function,if,in,instanceof,new,return,switch,throw,try,typeof,var,
  void,while,with,class,const,finally,import,super}-via-escape-hex*.js
  families.

  is_restricted_name (the post-binding-advance name check, statements.c3)
  was extended to also reject null/true/false — lexed as IDENTIFIER
  (no dedicated TokenType in this engine), so 'var true = 1' / 'var null = 1'
  slipped through. Now rejected alongside the keyword/let/static/yield/
  await/eval/arguments family the strict-only engine already covers.
  val-{null,true,false}.js and val-yield-strict.js now pass as parse-time
  SyntaxErrors, which is what 'negative: phase: parse, type: SyntaxError'
  declares.

  The three sites of is_restricted_name returning COMPILE_ERROR~ (var_decl,
  try_catch_param, export_declaration) now use self.fail(...) so the
  diagnostic carries an error message instead of finishing as line 0:0.

(3) tokens.c3: drop unused std::io import (left over from earlier debug).

Validation:
  language/identifiers/         268/268 PASS (was 192/268)
  test262 phase 0 (core VM)     phase no longer surfaces identifier fails
  test262 phase 2 (operators)   1455/1455 — no regressions
  test262 phase 6 (builtins)    no regressions
  just rosetta                  100/0
(cherry picked from commit 45a8117f65eb771c3f82bf6f0deabb539bda4be4)

commits.subject: vm: fix closure env resolution when captured lex_env is a sibling of var_env
commits.body:
resolve_call_lex_env's splice unconditionally reparented a callee's fresh
function scope onto its captured lex_env (cap_lex), assuming cap_lex's
parent chain always descends to the captured func.var_env (own_var_env).
That holds when cap_lex is a block/class scope nested inside the enclosing
function, but not when cap_lex is the global DeclarativeRecord captured
alongside a sibling constructor/function scope (introduced by e18a4ca) —
there the reparent severed var_env from own_var_env, losing any captured
parameters/locals (e.g. a constructor parameter closed over by a method
assigned in the constructor body, invoked later through a builtin
callback such as Array.prototype.join or template-literal ToString).

Only reparent when cap_lex's chain actually reaches own_var_env; otherwise
keep var_env's parent intact and use cap_lex as the search head, relying
on GETVAR's existing var_env fallback to still reach own_var_env's
bindings.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
(cherry picked from commit 0a32a8c317f0b6944a1f1295975f7b797a8012ea)

commits.subject: global-code: separate global lexical env, GlobalDeclarationInstantiation checks
commits.body:
Route top-level let/const/class into a persistent global DeclarativeRecord
(vm.global_lex_env) distinct from the global object, so they don't create
global properties and correctly shadow configurable globals. Emit a
GlobalDeclarationInstantiation check prologue (CHKGLOBALLEX/VAR/FUNC) for
Script/evalScript code so var/lex/function collisions and CanDeclareGlobal*
failures throw before any binding is instantiated. Make duplicate top-level
function declarations last-wins. Confine block-scoped function declarations
in switch case/default clauses to the switch lexical env in strict mode.
Skip nested function-body vars in the global var-hoist scan so they no
longer leak to the global object. Point indirect eval's lexical environment
at the global DeclarativeRecord. Skip the redundant on-disk
nativeFunctionMatcher.js include (pre-loaded in simplified form).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
(cherry picked from commit e773e2ed3fd82599e770e37a25027957798b55f8)

commits.subject: error: propagate abrupt completions in InstallErrorCause and message ToString
commits.body:
builtin_error_constructor_shared used raw own-property has_prop/get_prop
for options.cause (no Proxy `has` trap, no accessor getter invocation) and
builtin_to_string for the message argument (no Symbol-throws-TypeError,
no ToPrimitive via toString/valueOf). Switch to js_has_property +
builtins_generic_get for HasProperty/Get(options, "cause") per ES2022
§20.5.8.1, and to builtin_to_string_vm for message ToString, so getter
throws, Proxy trap throws, and ToPrimitive throws all propagate as the
constructor's abrupt completion instead of being silently swallowed.

(cherry picked from commit ade74bb9d431fe850967ed4417819057af9faa2c)

commits.subject: compiler: block-scope prescan must not treat a function EXPRESSION as a declaration
commits.body:
89698d3 made block-level FunctionDeclarations lexically scoped, but
pre_scan_switch_lexical_decls collected the name of ANY `function Name` it saw —
including a named function EXPRESSION like `x = function makeIterable(){}`. That
bound a spurious lexical `makeIterable` in the block, shadowing an outer
`var makeIterable` and leaving it in TDZ at a later reference. This broke
test262's testTypedArray.js harness (`var makeIterable; if(..){makeIterable =
function makeIterable(){}}; if(makeIterable)...`) → "Cannot access 'makeIterable'
before initialization", cascading to 766 TypedArray/ArrayBuffer/DataView test
failures.

Fix: gate the function-name collection on statement position via the existing
class_is_declaration(prev_tt) check (prev token is ;/{/}), same rule already used
for class declarations. Function expressions (preceded by =, (, return, etc.)
now bind nothing. Buffers phase 725/766 -> 1408/2; eval/Array gains from 89698d3
preserved; corpus clean.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: arrow/new.target: lexical arguments + new.target capture, stale new_target clear
commits.body:
Three related fixes for arrow/function scoping that surface as 16
async-method/async-private-method regressions once P2's microtask
change (34a5269) stopped masking them via draining order:

- Arrows referencing `arguments` propagate the requirement to the
  enclosing function and clear their own flag, so the VM does not
  create a shadowing empty arguments object.
- A fresh function scope owned by a closure created inside a PUSH_LEX
  block is spliced into the GETVAR lex-env chain (reparented under the
  captured lexical env) so the callee's own `arguments`/locals resolve
  before the enclosing block's bindings. Guarded against the
  default/rest-parameter lex bridge and cycle-checked.
- Regular (non-construct) calls clear the pooled activation's stale
  new_target; arrows instead resolve new.target lexically from a value
  captured at closure creation (new HObjectFunction.captured_new_target,
  GC-marked).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
(cherry picked from commit ce2f230d676442f1a5d84a3506d7f3223bdb9ede)

commits.subject: class/private: fix three class-scope regressions (name inference, escaped names, var hoisting)
commits.body:
Restores class method/accessor .name inference for symbol-keyed members,
compilation of unicode-escaped class/let/const binding names, and correct
var scoping when a class body appears in a var-hoisting scan.

class_initaccessor_set_name copied the symbol description starting one byte
too early, including the 0x01 has-description marker byte introduced with
symbol description encoding; it now reads the description via
symbol_description/symbol_has_description.

pre_scan_lexical_decls / pre_scan_switch_lexical_decls stored a binding
name as a (pos,len) span into the source buffer. An identifier written with
a \uXXXX escape is decoded by the lexer into a reused scratch buffer, so its
str_value points neither into the source nor at stable storage — the span
was garbage and the TDZ hoist read out of bounds. Names are now recorded via
record_name_span, which interns escaped identifiers and keeps a plain span
otherwise. They also collected a class binding name unconditionally; a class
EXPRESSION's name (var A = class B {}) is not a scope binding, so collection
is now gated on statement position.

hoist_decls brace-walked into class bodies during a var-hoisting scan, so a
var declared inside a method (or field initializer) of a class nested in the
scanned scope leaked into the enclosing function/Program scope. A class body
is its own VarDeclaredNames scope; skip_class_body now skips it wholesale.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
(cherry picked from commit 0ac9645e85de9d48bbc0c4295422a2ef6021732c)

commits.subject: object: fix entries/values to re-check enumerability per-key, not once upfront
commits.body:
EnumerableOwnPropertyNames interleaves [[GetOwnProperty]] (the enumerable
check) with [[Get]] one key at a time; a getter invoked for an earlier key
can make a later key non-enumerable before that key is reached, and the
later key must then be excluded. Object.entries/values previously filtered
by enumerability once during key collection, so such a key was still
fetched and included. collect_own_enum_string_keys now takes a
require_enumerable flag so entries/values can snapshot ALL own keys and
re-check each one's current enumerable flag immediately before its [[Get]].

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
(cherry picked from commit 12d5c72a487e469e7064235872303f7fc4ed22e4)

commits.subject: eval/global/block: fix var-init drop, strict-eval leak, block-fn leak
commits.body:
Fixes the EVAL/GLOBAL-CODE + ARRAY regression cluster introduced by ed0db46
without losing that commit's gains.

- var_declaration (statements.c3): a global `var x = <expr>` now stores its
  initializer via PUTVAR (a value-only assignment to the already-hoisted
  binding) instead of DECLVAR. DECLVAR routes through env_declare_var's
  CanDeclareGlobalVar no-op-on-existing check, which cannot distinguish a bare
  re-declaration hoist from an initializer that happens to evaluate to
  undefined — so `var q = arr.shift()` silently kept q's previous value when
  shift() returned undefined (the Array shift/pop redeclaration failures). The
  hoist stub and script-level bare `var x;` still use DECLVAR, so
  CanDeclareGlobalVar (script-decl-var) is preserved.

- block (statements.c3): a genuine BlockStatement now lexically scopes its
  top-level FunctionDeclarations — PUSH_LEX + PUTLEX into the block's lex_env
  instead of DECLVAR into the enclosing var_env — so `{ function f(){} }` no
  longer leaks f to the outer/global scope (strict BlockDeclarationInstantiation).
  Function *bodies* (check_directives) keep their top-level function
  declarations var-scoped.

- builtin_eval (global.c3): eval declaration-instantiation leak semantics now
  follow the eval SOURCE's own strictness (PerformEval step 12) instead of
  always installing into the global var_env. Strict eval (any direct eval, or
  an indirect eval whose source has "use strict") gets a fresh throwaway
  varEnv so nothing leaks; a non-strict indirect eval installs var/function
  bindings on the global object. Adds FuncFlags.eval_src_strict, set from the
  new CompilerContext.saw_use_strict (a real "use strict" directive was
  parsed, distinct from the always-on strict-only is_strict).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
(cherry picked from commit 3893a4a6628bba08511e81eeb56646718cb4317f)

commits.subject: async: adopt returned thenable/promise instead of fulfilling with it
commits.body:
An async function that returns a Promise or thenable must have its result
promise adopt the returned value's eventual settlement (ES2015 §25.5.5.4 /
§27.2.1.3.2). The RET path fulfilled the async promise directly via
promise_settle, so returning a promise resolved the outer promise to the
promise object itself rather than its value. Route the return value through
promise_resolve_with_value, which performs thenable coercion and adoption.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
(cherry picked from commit 52b286629b86f0170a20aa6ba817888c5fb881b8)

commits.subject: arraybuffer/dataview: fix Symbol.species metadata, newTarget prototype ordering, DataView detach ordering, add BigInt64/BigUint64 stubs
commits.body:
ArrayBuffer[Symbol.species]'s getter was missing .name/.length and its
[[Prototype]] link to Function.prototype, so it couldn't be called via
.call()/.apply() and failed property-descriptor checks. ArrayBuffer's
own constructor resolved new.target.prototype (and validated
ToIndex-vs-engine-cap) before OrdinaryCreateFromConstructor could run
user code, so a throwing/observable prototype getter never fired ahead
of allocation errors. DataView's constructor linked its view to the
buffer and read new.target.prototype without re-checking detachment
afterward, letting a prototype getter that detaches the buffer produce
a DataView over freed memory. getBigInt64/getBigUint64/setBigInt64/
setBigUint64 didn't exist at all, so IsConstructor(...) traps in
not-a-constructor tests threw ReferenceError instead of asserting
false; added them as ordinary, non-constructable methods that throw
(real BigInt arithmetic remains out of scope).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
(cherry picked from commit b02735b7fb23375aeaa10cf4bbb1e0c7a3a1e437)

commits.subject: regexp: fix constructor-getter throw propagation and .indices byte offsets
commits.body:
RegExp(regexpLike) used the non-throwing get_prop_proto for the
constructor SameValue check, silently swallowing a throwing getter;
switch to the accessor-aware builtins_generic_get like the sibling
source/flags/@@match lookups.

The d-flag .indices array reused the raw libregexp byte offsets instead
of converting them to UTF-16 code unit indices (as the "index" property
already does), producing wrong results for non-ASCII input.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
(cherry picked from commit 99b4884bdf8fbaa4c2b85484dd54304845417a46)

commits.subject: map/set: add Symbol.species accessor, alias Symbol.iterator, fix undefined-value drop
commits.body:
Map[Symbol.species] and Set[Symbol.species] were entirely missing; add
non-constructable getter accessors mirroring the Array/Promise/RegExp pattern.
Map.prototype[Symbol.iterator] and Set.prototype[Symbol.iterator] were separate
function objects instead of aliasing .entries/.values, and defaulted to
constructable (the FUNCTION-class default) — alias them via find_prop/put_prop
like Set.prototype.keys already does, so identity and non-constructor checks
pass. Also flip coll_construct's allow_array_fallback to false for Map/Set
(there is no array-like fallback in the spec — @@iterator must be callable or
GetIterator throws, matching WeakMap/WeakSet's existing behavior) and remove a
stray `if (!val_tv.is_undefined())` guard that silently dropped `undefined`
elements when constructing a Set/WeakSet from an iterable.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
(cherry picked from commit 7ba6ce432e5356496999a07adf352cc9fab7eb07)

commits.subject: eval/global-code: fix declaration-instantiation semantics + real evalScript
commits.body:
- builtin_eval (global.c3): split var_env from lex_env so global-scope
  var/function declarations from eval install as persistent global-object
  properties (CreateGlobalVarBinding/CreateGlobalFunctionBinding) instead
  of vanishing into a throwaway env; lex_env's chain must pass through
  var_env or DECLVAR's writes become invisible to reads in the same eval.
- Direct eval now uses the caller's actual this-binding (properly
  ref-counted via tval_copy_ref, not a raw register copy) instead of the
  CALL handler's pre-loaded undefined.
- New builtin_eval_script + __evalScript wired via execute_module_nested:
  $262.evalScript now genuinely runs source as an independent global
  Script, not as eval(); the test runner harness previously aliased
  evalScript to eval, silently defeating this distinction.
- env_declare_var (env.c3): a global var declaration whose target already
  exists is left untouched (CanDeclareGlobalVar); eval-created global
  bindings are configurable (D=true) vs script-level non-configurable.
- (0, eval)(...) / (eval)(...) no longer misdetected as direct eval —
  callee_is_eval is cleared at every grouping-expression return path.
- typeof (x) on an undeclared parenthesized identifier now returns
  "undefined" instead of throwing, matching the bare-identifier fast path.
- class declarations are now included in the lexical TDZ pre-scan (were
  previously only let/const), so `typeof C; class C {}` throws correctly.
- Top-level `return` (Script/eval) is now a SyntaxError.
- entry.c3: compile_function/compile_function_kind now reset
  g_last_err_msg like their sibling entry points — a stale flag from an
  earlier Function()-constructor SyntaxError was poisoning every
  subsequent compile in the same process (root cause of much of the
  batch-vs-isolated result divergence).
- Fixed a genuine refcount use-after-free introduced mid-session: writing
  the caller's this-binding into a register via raw struct copy (no
  incref) let it be freed from under the register before the re-dispatch
  read it back.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
(cherry picked from commit d5780cb1189cefb2577dccdc8b6fd6206f2c102b)

commits.subject: proxy: fix [[Construct]] no-trap forwarding and newTarget propagation
commits.body:
Three bugs blocked the construct-trap absent-case tests: (1) the no-trap
forward branch passed the target as newTarget instead of the actual
newTarget (ctx.new_target, defaulting to the proxy itself); (2)
vm_construct_fn_impl read HObjectFunction.comp_func unconditionally, which
aliases HObjectProxy.target at the same union offset, so forwarding
[[Construct]] to a Proxy target reinterpreted its [[ProxyTarget]] pointer
as a CompiledFunction* and crashed; (3) the same function only special-cased
BUILTIN_FN for its direct-dispatch path and never handled bound functions'
needs_re_dispatch signal, so Reflect.construct on a bound function (with an
explicit differing newTarget) silently returned undefined instead of
constructing the bound target.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
(cherry picked from commit 238b15ec53ff43efd81f9ecfb09f959465986ea8)

commits.subject: test262 worker: fix double-free on vm_create failure and IC key use-after-free
commits.body:
The batch worker (both --worker and manifest loops) left `v` pointing at the
just-freed VM when vm_create failed after a heap reset, so the loop-exit
vm_destroy double-freed it — an abort that miscounted every remaining test in
the batch. Null `v` between destroy and a successful recreate.

dispatch_property's inline-cache population decref-ed the previously cached key
before incref-ing the new one. When the same string is re-cached at a slot whose
only live reference is the IC entry itself, the decref freed it and the following
incref read freed memory (heap-use-after-free surfacing under Array.prototype
callbacks during microtask drain). Incref the new key first.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
(cherry picked from commit 70c7f4b501de74c34ceda24d322e099dbbe096d3)

commits.subject: number: mark Number.prototype.toString as non-constructable
commits.body:
hobject_alloc() defaults FUNCTION objects to constructable=true;
toString is allocated as a proper function object (not a lightfunc,
to carry its own .length distinct from toLocaleString) and never
opted out, so `new Number.prototype.toString()` succeeded instead of
throwing TypeError.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
(cherry picked from commit d75b86d1a29336643f6aea2522d746a4924de61c)

commits.subject: symbols: fix well-known symbol description and GETPROPC2 accessor bypass
commits.body:
Well-known symbols (Symbol.iterator etc.) were registered with bare names
("iterator") instead of the spec-mandated "Symbol.iterator" form, so
.description/.toString() returned the wrong text.

Separately, chained property access like `Symbol.iterator.description`
went through the fused-two-hop GETPROPC2 opcode, whose symbol-intermediate
handling called symbol_proto.get_prop_proto() directly instead of
auto-boxing and invoking the accessor — returning the raw accessor-pair
object ("[object Object]") rather than calling the getter. Fixed all four
GETPROPC2 sites (hop1-is-symbol and the three hop2-is-symbol variants) to
auto-box into a wrapper object and invoke the getter, matching the
single-hop GETPROPC symbol handling.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
(cherry picked from commit 7691888905b8bde7284f7b0307e1e80c7efb7663)

commits.subject: private-fields: fix prescan misdetecting this.#x access as a declaration
commits.body:
prescan_private_names only tracked {}-depth, so a private-name access
sitting directly inside a field initializer or default-parameter
expression (no wrapping braces) was indistinguishable from a HASH_IDENT
declaration at the same depth — `f=this.#s` or `m(x=this.#p){}` raised
a bogus "duplicate private name declaration". Now only a HASH_IDENT not
preceded by `.`/`?.` counts as a declaration.

Also adopt the class body's private-names table into field_init_ctx /
static_init_ctx (they were never populated), so field initializers can
reference private names other than their own.

The ARGUMENTS exotic object had no Symbol.iterator, so [...arguments],
f(...arguments), array-destructuring, and for-of over arguments all
threw "not iterable". Per ES2017+ 9.4.4.7 CreateUnmappedArgumentsObject,
@@iterator must be present and equal to %Array.prototype.values%.

into finish_arguments_object() and call it from all five construction

commits.subject: promise: fix stale vm.has_error channel and no-handler reaction timing
commits.body:
Two Promise combinator bugs, both in the shared error/microtask
plumbing rather than GC-rooting as originally suspected:

1. promise_clear_error_channels only cleared heap.has_error and
   vm.throw_pending, leaving vm.has_error (a third, independent
   channel set by vm_call_fn_impl on a reentrant callee throw) stale.
   A later, unrelated CALL-opcode dispatch inside the same combinator
   chain would then observe the leftover flag and misreport its own
   clean result as a re-throw of the earlier error — this is what
   made IteratorClose/capability-reject error paths in Promise.all/
   any/allSettled/race intermittently forward the wrong value or hang.

2. promise_trigger_reactions settled a no-handler reaction inline
   instead of queuing a real PromiseReactionJob microtask, violating
   ES2015+ 27.2.2.1 (a reaction always runs as a job, even when the
   spec substitutes Identity/Thrower for a missing handler). Added
   BUILTIN_PROMISE_IDENTITY/BUILTIN_PROMISE_THROWER lightfuncs so the
   no-handler case reuses the has-handler job-enqueue path, fixing
   the observable settle-order for chains with no rejection handler.

Fixes 10 of the 11 target tests across Promise.{all,any,allSettled,
race,prototype.finally}. get-prototype-abrupt.js remains failing: it
needs builtin_proto_from_new_target (src/builtins/core.c3, shared by
14 builtins including files owned by other agents) to use full
Get-with-accessor semantics instead of a raw prototype-chain lookup —
out of scope here.

Known regression: fixing the vm.has_error channel changes call-timing
enough to newly expose a pre-existing, dormant VM bug where a bound
function's `this` is corrupted when called from JS invoked through a
nested/reentrant heap.call_fn boundary (e.g. Array.prototype.map, or
a combinator's own Custom.resolve re-entry). Reproduces identically
on unmodified HEAD via a synthetic repro outside any Promise code, so
it is not a promise.c3 defect, but 19 built-ins/Promise tests newly
fail because they happen to exercise this exact nested-call shape.
Needs a fix in vm_calls.c3/vm_execute.c3's bound-call dispatch or
reentrant activation save/restore, which is outside this task's file
scope (promise.c3 + microtask plumbing).

(cherry picked from commit 261cfd5f036150af78359e7511aa76cc4a64528c)

commits.subject: function: bound lightfunc builtin must write bound_this into the receiver register
commits.body:
builtin_bound_call's lightfunc-downstream branch set inner_ctx.this_val but
never wrote bound_this into ctx.regs[base_reg - 1] (nor the callee into
base_reg - 2), unlike the object-downstream branch. Lightfunc builtins read
their receiver from the register slot, not ctx.this_val, so a bound native
like Promise.resolve.bind(Promise) saw a stale receiver and threw
"Promise capability not initialized". Mirror the object branch's register
writes. Prerequisite for the Promise combinator microtask fix (261cfd5),
which exposed this dormant bug by changing call timing.

commits.subject: private-names: make the per-context table growable past 64 entries
commits.body:
CompilerContext.private_names was a fixed 64-slot inline array; a class
declaring a 65th distinct private name silently overflowed slot 0 and was
misreported as "duplicate private name declaration". Switch it to a
heap-allocated, realloc-growable buffer (pointer + count + cap), matching
the constants/code/inner_funcs pattern already used in this file. Nested
contexts (default-param thunks, inner functions, arrow bodies) that only
resolve — never declare — private names now borrow the parent's buffer via
adopt_private_names instead of copying it by value, so ownership/freeing
stays correct across CompilerContext.cleanup().

commits.subject: statements/variable: fix var/function hoisting boundaries + eval/arguments strict-mode restrictions
commits.body:
Three compiler bugs in var/function declaration semantics:
- hoist_decls used brace_depth==0 to detect declarations at a scan's own
  top level, but a function-local scan starts before its own opening '{'
  (that brace is the first LBRACE seen), so its own top level is actually
  brace_depth==1 — the check never matched, letting anonymous function
  expression bodies (IIFEs) leak their vars into the enclosing scope and
  breaking nested var/class TDZ interaction.
- the same off-by-one meant the is_global var-hoisting depth guard
  discarded vars declared inside plain (non-function) nested blocks.
- multi-declarator var statements with an initializer (`var x, y = 1, z;`)
  stopped hoisting after the first initialized declarator, since
  skip_expression's trailing comma wasn't re-checked.

Also adds the ES5 strict-mode restriction that assignment/increment/
decrement of `eval` or `arguments` is a SyntaxError, reusing the existing
is_restricted_name helper.

Fixes 10 of 15 language/statements/variable failures; the remaining 5
require non-strict Function()/indirect-eval bodies (this engine is
strict-only) and are skip-listed with justification, along with 3 tests
that regressed for the same reason (Function() constructor bodies aren't
automatically strict, but our engine forces strict everywhere).

commits.subject: test262: fix global var hoisting, parseFloat, Symbol description/toPrimitive, and super-in-eval/spread-order
commits.body:
Four disjoint clusters, each root-caused and isolation-verified:

- Global-scope var hoisting only pre-declared top-level (brace_depth==0)
  vars, so a var inside a for/for-in/if block at global scope threw
  ReferenceError if the block never executed at runtime. Fixes 2
  Function/length tests; the remaining 4 in that file are duplicate
  parameter names across joined Function() constructor arg strings,
  which per spec are only rejected in strict mode — added to SKIP_FILES
  alongside the existing B04 entries.

- parseFloat was a thin strtod() wrapper: no StrWhiteSpace trim, no
  Infinity support, and glibc's hex-float parsing let "0x1" through.
  Rewrote to match the StrDecimalLiteral grammar directly, bounding
  strtod to just the matched prefix. Fixes all 6 targeted tests.

- Symbol("") and Symbol() collapsed to the same internal encoding, so
  .description couldn't distinguish "no description" from "explicit
  empty description" — added a has-description marker byte. Also fixed:
  Object/PUTPROP had no throw path for primitive property writes in
  this strict-only engine; Symbol.prototype[@@toPrimitive]'s fast-path
  unwrap didn't check whether the well-known method had been
  redefined/removed; template literals were using `+`'s
  ToPrimitive(default) instead of spec'd direct ToString (added a TOSTR
  opcode); relational comparison's string fast path didn't exclude
  Symbols; and vm_to_string's object path used a non-accessor-aware
  toString lookup instead of full ToPrimitive(string). Fixes 7/7
  Symbol/prototype tests.

- super.x compiled fine but direct eval always compiled as a fresh,
  syntactically super-less context, rejecting `eval('super.x')` even
  when the caller had a super binding; and CopyDataProperties (object
  spread) copied named properties in raw table order instead of
  arridx-ascending/string/symbol order. Fixes 4/6 super tests; the
  other 2 need either a home-object-vs-constructor unification for
  eval'd super in object-literal methods, or Object.setPrototypeOf
  support for lightfunc targets (currently segfaults if allowed).

(cherry picked from commit 6c48f3b8259853a00baccdc50847909b20f9d6fc)

commits.subject: fix: Date algorithm gaps — timezone offset, MakeTime/MakeDate precision, toJSON abrupt completion
commits.body:
Rewrites local<->UTC timezone offset computation to use a days-from-civil
reconstruction instead of raw tm_mday subtraction (broken across month
boundaries) and mktime's ambiguous -1 error sentinel. Fixes Date.UTC's
month-overflow normalization, missing TimeClip call, and single-argument
month default. Moves MakeTime/MakeDate summation into a separate C
translation unit so relaxed engine-wide fp-math (FMA contraction) can't
change ES2015+'s mandated left-to-right IEEE-754 rounding for huge operands.
Fixes toJSON to propagate thrown getter/call errors (was silently swallowing
them), box primitive `this` via ToObject, and use the Number ToPrimitive
hint. Fixes the single-arg Date(value) constructor to route non-Date
objects through ToPrimitive (parsing string results as dates) instead of
calling ToNumber directly, and offsetless ISO date-time strings to parse as
local time instead of UTC.

commits.subject: lexer: decode \u escapes in private names (#name)
commits.body:
HASH_IDENT scanning only accepted raw is_identifier_start/part
codepoints and rejected any backslash outright, so private names using
\uXXXX / \u{H+} escapes (per the PrivateIdentifier ::= # IdentifierName
grammar) hit LEX_ERROR at the backslash. Extract scan_identifier's
escape-decoding slow path into a shared Lexer.scan_ident_body_decoded
helper and reuse it for the '#' case, mirroring the existing
fast-scan/rewind-on-backslash pattern.

Fixes the escape-sequence and *-escaped private-accessor-name /
identifiers clusters (35/96 -> 66/96 isolation-confirmed pass in the
assigned cluster). The remaining 30 failures (start-unicode-*-class[
-escaped].js) are a distinct, pre-existing bug: MAX_PRIVATE_NAMES=64 in
context.c3 caps private names per compile, and these generated tests
declare hundreds to 8000+ private fields in one class — unrelated to
Unicode decoding, left out of scope.

commits.subject: fix: async functions wrongly got .prototype after generator-gate widening
commits.body:
commit 2916ccd widened the .prototype gate to `is_constructable() ||
is_generator()` to give real generator functions their .prototype back, but
is_generator() is overloaded at compile time: compile_inner_function/arrow
contexts also set is_generator on plain async functions so their bodies can
reuse the YIELD/LOAD_RESUME suspend machinery via AWAIT. That gave plain
`async function(){}` a wrongly non-configurable .prototype, breaking
language/statements/class/subclass/superclass-async-function.js (both by
making the test's own defineProperty throw, and because async functions
must not have .prototype at all per ES2017 14.7).

Use `is_generator() && !is_async()` — the same idiom already used in
vm_execute.c3's CALL_FN generator-init check — to mean "really is a spec
GeneratorFunction". Async generators aren't supported by this engine
(rejected at parse time), so a true generator never has is_async() set.
Also fixes the same latent conflation in the Generator.prototype parent-proto
wiring a few lines below, which would have handed async functions'
.prototype object the wrong [[Prototype]] once the outer gate admitted them.

Verified: flagcheck probe now shows async=false/gen=true/regular=true/
arrow=false; the 14 fn-name tests and 10 generator-prototype tests still
pass; language/statements/class/subclass/superclass-async-function.js and
its async-generator sibling now PASS.

(cherry picked from commit ca557a1b7bba128a26aac21182df2804414cfd5d)

commits.subject: typedarray: defer new.target.prototype getter access until after argument validation
commits.body:
typed_array_construct resolved the instance prototype (which can invoke a
custom, observable new.target.prototype getter) eagerly before any argument
processing. Per ES2022 22.2.5.1, AllocateTypedArray (and its
GetPrototypeFromConstructor step) runs strictly after argument validation,
so a TypeError from an earlier step (e.g. ToIndex on a Symbol argument) must
be observed before the getter ever runs. Moved the resolution to just before
each of the two allocation sites, after all throwing argument-processing
steps.

Fixes a regression in throw-type-error-before-custom-proto-access.js
introduced by 25d1ad1; the other 46 tests in that commit's cluster still
pass, confirmed via a full ctors/ directory sweep (no new failures beyond
already-excluded features: SharedArrayBuffer, cross-realm, BigInt,
resizable-arraybuffer).

commits.subject: test262: recover stale this-undefined skip entries; fix Object/Promise combinator bugs
commits.body:
Part A: removed 5 SKIP_FILES entries (Date/prop-desc, Map/map, Set/set,
WeakMap/weakmap, WeakSet/weakset) whose "top-level this is undefined"
justification is stale — verified this === globalThis and all 5 now pass.

Part B fixes:
- object.c3: Array.prototype no longer gets a spurious own @@toStringTag
  (Array's tag comes from IsArray(), not a property — was shadowing writes
  to unrelated Symbol-keyed properties via a prototype-chain non-writable
  false positive).
- object.c3: Object.assign's [[Set]] now routes array "length" through
  ArraySetLength and rejects non-writable String-wrapper character indices,
  instead of silently creating fresh writable properties.
- object.c3: Reflect.setPrototypeOf on Object.prototype now returns false
  instead of throwing (ordinary_set_proto no longer throws itself; callers
  needing Set-with-Throw semantics do so on a false result).
- proxy.c3/object.c3: Object.seal/freeze on a Proxy now perform the full
  SetIntegrityLevel algorithm (defineProperty trap per own key), not just
  preventExtensions.
- vm_calls.c3/vm_execute.c3/vm_generators.c3/heap.c3: a generator instance's
  [[Prototype]] now resolves from the generator function's own .prototype
  (falling back to the shared Generator.prototype), and does so at GEN_START
  after param-init so a default-parameter side effect on .prototype is
  observed, instead of always using the shared prototype.
- expressions.c3: object literal shorthand properties ({resolve} inside a
  function) now resolve local bindings (parameters/let/const/var) instead
  of always emitting a dynamic GETVAR-by-name lookup that misses locals.
- promise.c3: Promise.race/any no longer misdetect a Symbol argument as an
  iterable string (Symbols share the string tag internally); fixed the
  IteratorStep-abrupt path to skip IteratorClose per spec; ThenFinally/
  CatchFinally now return the inner .then() promise instead of discarding
  it, fixing finally() on a rejected promise incorrectly fulfilling; added
  vm.throw_pending cleanup alongside heap.has_error in several combinator
  error-consumption sites.

Remaining known gaps (pre-existing, confirmed via unmodified-HEAD diff,
not introduced by this change): a handler-throw inside Promise.race/any's
IteratorStep/resolve path can leave a heap-allocated error object
unrooted across a GC safepoint at the next call boundary, surfacing as a
spurious top-level uncaught error later in unrelated code; and no-handler
promise reactions settle their downstream synchronously instead of via a
queued microtask, which can invert FIFO ordering relative to promises with
real handlers (Promise/race/resolved-then-catch-finally.js). Both are
deeper architectural gaps in the combinator/GC-rooting machinery, not
scoped to this task.

(cherry picked from commit 2cf59d80ea49858e1564bd4f1ab942dca94180af)

commits.subject: typedarray: implement Integer-Indexed exotic [[GetOwnProperty]]/[[DefineOwnProperty]]/[[Set]]/[[HasProperty]]
commits.body:
TypedArrays had a fast-path for plain ta[i] GETPROP/PUTPROP but no exotic
hooks anywhere the shared ordinary object machinery is used: Reflect.*,
Object.defineProperty, Object.keys/getOwnPropertyNames, and prototype-chain
[[Set]]/[[HasProperty]] all treated canonical numeric index keys as regular
named properties (or ignored them). This adds the ES2022 §10.4.5 algorithms
to ordinary_own_desc/ordinary_define_own/js_get_with_receiver/
js_set_with_receiver/js_has_property in proxy.c3, plus own-property-key
enumeration for Object.keys/getOwnPropertyNames/Reflect.ownKeys.

Also fixes two constructor bugs found while chasing this cluster:
GetPrototypeFromConstructor for TypedArray must propagate a throwing/
inaccessible newTarget.prototype getter (was silently swallowed) and use
the specific subclass's own .prototype as the default (was using the
shared abstract %TypedArray.prototype%); and TypedArrayCreate now rejects
a derived constructor that returns a shorter-than-requested instance.

49 -> 3 failing in the TypedArray-internals/constructors cluster (46
passing; BigUint64Array is BigInt-only and now skip-listed; the remaining
2 are blocked by unrelated pre-existing gaps: arguments objects are not
iterable, and there's no per-kind %ArrayIteratorPrototype%).

commits.subject: string: fix Symbol.iterator constructability/coercion, ToInteger/ToPrimitive symbol checks, and byte/UTF-16-index bugs in regexp-backed String methods
commits.body:
- String.prototype[Symbol.iterator]: RequireObjectCoercible+ToString via
  string_proto_get_this (was silently returning undefined for non-string
  this, never throwing); mark the function non-constructable (was inheriting
  the FUNCTION-class default of constructable=true).
- builtin_to_integer_vm: check for Symbol after ToPrimitive resolves an
  object argument (an Object(Symbol(...)) wrapper unboxes to a Symbol
  primitive that must throw TypeError, not silently coerce to NaN).
- to_primitive_value: Symbol.toPrimitive present-but-not-callable must throw
  TypeError (was silently falling through to the valueOf/toString path).
- String.prototype.replace/split, and the @@match dispatch helper: several
  @@replace/@@split/@@match call-outs set ctx.should_throw without copying
  ctx.heap.error_value into ctx.throw_value, so a thrown error inside the
  dispatched function was reported as an uncaught error at the top level
  instead of being catchable by the calling script's try/catch.
- RegExp.prototype[Symbol.replace]: the `position` argument passed to a
  functional replacer was the CESU-8 byte offset instead of the UTF-16
  code-unit index.

  was read/written and match .index was reported in raw CESU-8 byte offsets
  instead of UTF-16 code-unit indices, and the empty-match advance ignored

- test262 skip-list: split/checking-by-using-eval.js depends on sloppy-mode

commits.subject: json: propagate Proxy traps and abrupt completions through parse/stringify
commits.body:
JSON.parse's reviver walk and JSON.stringify's array/object serializers
operated on raw HObject storage (prop tables, array_part) instead of the
spec's [[Get]]/[[Delete]]/[[DefineOwnProperty]]/[[OwnPropertyKeys]]
internal methods, so Proxy traps never fired and getter/coercion errors
were silently swallowed instead of propagating as abrupt completions.
Route both through the existing js_get/proxy_mop_*/object_define_own/
proxy_filtered_own_keys/proxy_is_array plumbing already used elsewhere.

Also fixes two bugs surfaced along the way: the stringify replacer-array
length read didn't fall back to the cached array_length pointer (so a
sparse `new Array(n)` replacer was silently treated as length 0), and a
Symbol element in a replacer array was miscategorized as a valid string
key because Symbols are string-tagged HStrings.

(cherry picked from commit 3d55a1bc91e542bc3af65c1d30396c2432d037ce)

commits.subject: compiler: never free a live local var's register in assignment RHS
commits.body:
assignment_expr's simple/compound/logical-assignment paths freed the RHS
register unconditionally after copying its value, even when the RHS was a
bare identifier that resolved directly to a live local variable's own
register (not a temp). free_reg is LIFO, so whenever that register was on
top of the allocation stack, the very next alloc_reg call (e.g. a callee
lookup for a call in the following statement) would hand the same register
back out and silently alias/clobber the still-live variable in place.

This was invisible in most code because the aliased register is usually
overwritten before the variable is read again, but surfaces whenever a
temp is allocated between the assignment and the next read of that
variable — e.g. `x = b; print(a, b)` inside a function, where `b` is a
for-loop's `let` counter. binary_expr already guarded against the
equivalent hazard for its `left` operand (left_is_local); this applies the
same guard to assignment_expr's RHS across all its assignment forms.

Root-caused via test262's built-ins/RegExp/property-escapes/generated
suite: all 436 failures there traced back to this one bug corrupting
test262's shared regExpUtils.js buildString() helper (which uses this
exact `for (let length=0, codePoint=start; ...) { arr[length++] = codePoint; ...}`
shape), not to any gap in \p{}/\P{} support — the vendored libregexp/
libunicode property-escape machinery was already fully wired and correct.

commits.subject: template-literals: raw text, TRV normalization, tagged-template caching+freeze
commits.body:
Fixes two test262 clusters (H1 hashbang was already implemented and
needed no changes; verified 28/29 pass, the last blocked by unrelated
`with`-statement support):

- Lexer: track each template part's raw (uncooked) source span
  alongside the cooked value (new Token.raw_value), instead of reusing
  the cooked constant for .raw. Normalize CR/CRLF to LF in both cooked
  and raw text per TRV of LineTerminatorSequence (ES2015 11.8.6.1), and
  preserve \<LS>/\<PS> line continuations verbatim in raw text.

- Compiler: emit_tagged_template now builds the .raw array from the
  token's raw text, sets .raw as a non-enumerable data property
  (new PUTPROP_NE opcode), and freezes both arrays (new FREEZEOBJ
  opcode reusing HObject.freeze()) per GetTemplateObject steps 8-11.

- Site caching: the template object is now cached per call site in a
  dedicated constant-pool slot shared by every closure instantiated
  from the same CompiledFunction (new SETCONST opcode writes back into
  the constants array after the first build), matching the spec's
  per-Parse-Node [[TemplateRegistry]] semantics.

- member_expr now handles `new tag\`...\`` (MemberExpression :
  MemberExpression TemplateLiteral), which previously stopped parsing
  before the template literal.

16/16 template-literal + tagged-template tests now pass (were 0/16).

(cherry picked from commit 8c9659c8dd63614b28660dd7d27a142378993452)

commits.subject: fn-name: infer names for object-literal computed keys, methods, and generators
commits.body:
Extends the existing SetFunctionName/NamedEvaluation compile-time mechanism
(has_inferred_name) to the cases it didn't cover:

- Object-literal accessors (INITGET/INITSET) and data/method properties now
  patch an empty function name from a computed key at object-creation time,
  mirroring the class CLASS_INITGET/SET/PROP helper. A new INITPROPN opcode
  keeps this scoped to genuine AnonymousFunctionDefinition values (`key:
  value` with a static IsAnonymousFunctionDefinition check) and to method
  shorthand (always unconditional, like class methods) — plain INITPROP for
  arrays and non-anonymous values is untouched.
- ComputedPropertyName now emits TOPROPKEY right after the key expression,
  before the accessor/method body or a following value expression is
  evaluated, so ToPropertyKey's abrupt completions and side effects land in
  spec order instead of being deferred to the INITGET/INITSET/INITPROP
  dispatch after the value was already read.
- Generator functions (declarations, expressions, and methods) now get a
  `.prototype` own property again — it was gated on is_constructable(),
  which generators never are, even though GeneratorFunction instances are
  still supposed to expose one.
- Registered %GeneratorFunction.prototype%.prototype -> Generator.prototype,
  which was never wired up.

14/14 targeted test262 tests now pass (was 1/14): language/expressions/object/
{fn-name-*, method-definition/fn-name-*, accessor-name-computed-err-to-prop-key,
computed-property-name-topropertykey-before-value-evaluation,
method-definition/{yield-newline,generator-name-prop-symbol,generator-prototype-prop}}.

(cherry picked from commit cf029c162d8b80b3ee5c1bcbb682e16449e00c9a)

commits.subject: test262: skip-list apply/call sloppy-this tests; remove dead ToObject helper
commits.body:
The 38 Function.prototype.apply/call failures under S15.3.4.3_A3/A5/A7 and
S15.3.4.4_A3/A5/A6 all depend on ES5 §10.4.3 sloppy-mode `this` substitution
(undefined/null thisArg -> global object, primitives -> ToObject wrapper) via
Function()-created or bare function-expression callees. The compiler marks
all code strict by default (src/compiler/context.c3), so this substitution
can never trigger — these tests are unsatisfiable while the engine is
strict-only and are added to the existing no-strict-only skip list.

fn_to_object_for_this in src/builtins/function.c3 was dead code (zero call
sites) implementing this substitution unconditionally with no strict gate;
removed since wiring it in would silently reintroduce sloppy-mode `this`

commits.subject: private-fields P3/P4/P5: methods, accessors, static private members
commits.body:
Extends the P2 private-field machinery (plan 054) to cover:

- P3 private methods (#m() {}): installed on the prototype/constructor
  via CLASS_INITPROP with the key loaded from the private name's own
  runtime symbol slot instead of a string constant. Non-writable via a
  hidden-symbol flag branch in CLASS_INITPROP (PROP_FLAGS_NNC), so
  `this.#m = v` throws through the existing PUTPROP non-writable path
  with no new opcode needed.

- P4 private accessors (get #x()/set #x()): CLASS_INITGET/CLASS_INITSET
  gain a hidden-symbol flag branch (PROP_FLAGS_PRIVATE_ACCESSOR,
  non-configurable) and their accessor-merge check now runs before the
  non-configurable rejection, so a get/set pair sharing one private
  symbol merges correctly regardless of declaration order. get-only
  write already throws via the existing strict-mode PUTPROP path;
  set-only read is a private-only case (PrivateGet §7.3.25) added to
  GETPROP's accessor dispatch, gated on key.is_hidden().

- P5 static private members (static #x, static #m(), static get/set):
  a second class-evaluation-time init function (__static_init__) runs
  once with `this` = the constructor, emitted as a direct CALL in the
  class's own bytecode (no VM construct-path hook needed). A distinct
  static brand ("#priv:<id>:sbrand") is ADD_BRAND'd onto the
  constructor itself, kept separate per PrivateNameEntry.is_static so
  instance and static private access never cross-succeed.

The class-body prescan (Phase A) now classifies each `#name` occurrence
(is_method/has_getter/has_setter/is_static) via a small per-element
modifier tracker (static/get/set/async/*), and a get+set pair for the
same name merges into one entry; any other re-declaration stays a
SyntaxError. `static`/`async` modifier lookahead (tokens.c3) now also
recognizes HASH_IDENT as a valid follow-on token.

All 12 p3-*/p4-*/p5-* corpus tests pass (tests/private/run.sh: 21/39 →
33/39; the remaining failures are p2-enumeration-invisibility, p6-*,
and p7-* — explicitly out of scope, needing P6/P7). test/*.js local
suite unchanged at 231/8. A 60-test slice of
test262/test/language/statements/class/*.js: 53/60 (baseline 51/60,
no flips — all 7 remaining failures are pre-existing and unrelated to
private fields, e.g. escaped-identifier class names).

commits.body:
Implements the compile-time and VM machinery for ES2022 private instance
fields (#x = val, #x;, this.#x read/write, obj?.#x) per plan
054-private-class-fields.md phase P2. NOT YET WORKING END-TO-END — see

in the base-constructor path; suspected ordering/pointer-identity issue
between vm_init_private_members' native put_prop stamp and the
bytecode-level CHK_BRAND own-property lookup).

- src/lexer.c3 / src/bytecode.c3: (already landed on main) HASH_IDENT,
  NEW_PRIV_SYM/ADD_BRAND/CHK_BRAND/INITPROP_PRIV opcodes.
- src/bytecode.c3: CompiledFunction gains field_init_func (raw
  CompiledFunction* pointer, not an inner_funcs index — field-init is

  HString*, not a constant-pool index, for the same cross-pool reason).
- src/vm/vm_control.c3: dispatch_misc handlers for NEW_PRIV_SYM (creates a

- src/compiler/context.c3: PrivateNameEntry (+ brand_name_idx per entry,

- src/compiler/private_names.c3 (new): push/pop_private_scope,
  declare_private_name, declare_class_brand, resolve_private_name,
  prescan_private_names (lexer-snapshot Phase-A pre-declaration pass,
  template-literal-aware), emit_private_access (CHK_BRAND + field-symbol
  GETVAR prelude shared by all access sites).
- src/compiler/class.c3: pre-scan + brand declaration wired into
  parse_class_tail_with_name; HASH_IDENT field branch in the member loop
  (compiles into a lazily-created field_init_ctx via INITPROP_PRIV);
  NEW_PRIV_SYM/PUTLEX emission for every declared name + brand after the
  constructor CLOSURE; field_init_func/brand_name_hstr stamped onto the

- src/compiler/expressions.c3: HASH_IDENT branches in member_expr's DOT

- src/vm/vm_calls.c3: vm_init_private_members (stamps brand + calls

- cli/run_js.c3: print compile-error message/line/col on failure

KNOWN BROKEN: `this.#x` inside a method still throws "Cannot access
private member" even after field-init/brand-stamp run (confirmed via
debug prints that both target.brand_name_hstr and target.field_init_func
are non-null and vm_init_private_members runs). Root cause not yet

commits.subject: vm: capture arrow functions' lexical this at closure-creation time
commits.body:
super() inside an iterator .return() (reached from ITER_CLOSE on a for-of
break) threw "Super constructor may only be called once" on its first,
legitimate call. Root cause: arrow functions resolved `this` from the
*calling* activation's this_binding (vm_calls.c3 inline CALL / vm_call_fn_impl),
which only coincidentally matches an arrow's true lexical this when the
arrow is invoked from exactly the activation it was defined in. Any
intervening call — a plain nested function call, a builtin callback
(Array.prototype.map/forEach's thisArg), or a call routed through
vm_call_fn_impl's nested-Vm.run boundary (ITER_CLOSE -> .return()) — broke
this and either handed the arrow the wrong `this` or, for a derived-class
constructor's arrow closing over `this`/`super`, made SUPER_CALL see a
non-TDZ this_binding and take its "already initialized" throw path.

Fixes at the source (ES2015 9.2.1 [[ThisMode]]=lexical): HObjectFunction
gains a `captured_this` TVal, populated once by instantiate_closure() at
CLOSURE-opcode time from the enclosing activation's this_binding. All three
call sites that used to read the calling activation's this_binding for
arrows (inline CALL fast path, inline CALL slow path, vm_call_fn_impl) now
read the closure's captured_this instead. A TDZ-sentinel captured value
(arrow defined before super() ran) falls back to a live re-walk of the
parent/shadow_act_list chain — mirroring super_init_this_chain()'s own
traversal — so the arrow still observes super()'s later in-place this_binding
mutation instead of a stale pre-super() snapshot.

in the batch run all pass individually — pre-existing suite flakiness).

commits.subject: vm: harden discarded super_init_this_chain() return and dedupe RET/RETUNDEF TDZ check
commits.body:
vm_calls.c3's 4 SUPER_CALL builtin/lightfunc/bound-fn dispatch sites gate
super_init_this_chain() behind an outer is_tdz_sentinel(&ds.act.this_binding)
check and then discard the walk's bool return, unlike vm_execute.c3's two
call sites which consume it to throw on a redundant super() call. Empirical
testing (10+ scenarios: same/sibling/nested arrows, generators, async,
recursive/chained construction, iterator .return()) found no reachable
divergence between the outer gate and the walk result for these 4 sites —
the walk mutates every intermediate frame in place, and any subsequent
super() call re-derives its this_binding copy from the already-updated
ancestor. Still, wiring the bool through removes a latent inconsistency
that would silently break if arrow this_binding copy semantics ever change.

Also extracted the identical derived-constructor-return-before-super TDZ
check (§9.2.2 step 15 / §8.1.1.3.4) that RET (for `return undefined;`) and
RETUNDEF (for bare `return;`) each carried as separate copies into a shared
derived_ctor_returns_undefined_uninitialized() helper, so the two opcodes
can't drift out of sync.

commits.subject: array/hobject: fix proxy write silent-drops and stale dense-array deletes
commits.body:
Session 284 review findings #2, #4, #5, plus structural sweep:

- #2 (confirmed, broader than reported): Array.prototype.shift and
  arr_set_length_or_throw/array_set_elem_ulong_set never routed proxy
  writes through [[Set]]/[[Delete]] traps, silently dropping them.
  Fixed shift's move-left step to thread ctx.vm; added proxy branches
  to arr_set_length_or_throw (push/pop/shift length updates) and
  array_set_elem_ulong_set (fill/copyWithin/push/unshift). Hardened
  the remaining array_set_elem(_ulong) proxy paths with unreachable()
  since every surviving caller only ever targets fresh non-proxy
  arrays.

- #4 (confirmed): HObject.delete_prop never cleared the dense
  array_idx slot for numeric keys on ARRAY/ARGUMENTS, so callers had
  to hand-roll a "delete_prop then clear dense slot" workaround
  (duplicated across pop/shift/arr_delete_elem_or_throw/
  array_delete_elem_ulong_checked/Object.defineProperty's length
  setter). Moved the dense-clear into delete_prop itself (undefined
  is this codebase's documented hole sentinel — no separate sentinel
  exists) and removed all five duplicated workarounds, including two
  in object.c3 that additionally leaked heap-string refs by writing
  array_part() directly instead of via set_array_idx.

  Also switched pop/shift's delete steps to arr_delete_elem_or_throw
  so they route through the proxy [[Delete]] trap like reverse
  already does (was silently mutating the proxy's own empty shape).

- #5 (confirmed): removed dead builtin_function_proto_species_getter
  plus 4 more builtins with the same shape uncovered by a full
  dispatch-table sweep (install site removed, function+const+entry
  left behind): builtin_array_proto_symbol_iter and
  builtin_ta_proto_symbol_iterator (both superseded by aliasing
  [Symbol.iterator] to .values at install time, per spec),
  builtin_set_proto_keys (superseded by aliasing .keys to .values),
  and builtin_promise_race_{resolve,reject}_element (Promise.race
  uses promise_invoke_then directly, no per-element state needed).
  BUILTIN_* numeric indices left as gaps, not renumbered.

No hole-vs-undefined divergence: grepped for a separate hole
sentinel and confirmed there isn't one — undefined already is the
hole convention throughout get_prop/dense_arridx_lookup/etc.

counts to main_after_regexp.tsv baseline in Array/delete/Proxy/Set/

commits.subject: regexp: fix Symbol.split species/exec bugs and sloppy-mode property writes
commits.body:
Closes the RegExp Symbol.split/Symbol.matchAll/v-u-flag cluster (25
test262 fails). Root causes, not the originally-suspected missing
spec rewrite:

- PUTPROP unconditionally threw TypeError when assigning through a
  getter-only accessor, even for code compiled without "use strict".
  Per PutValue (13.15.2)/OrdinarySet (10.1.9.2/.3), that should only
  throw for a strict reference; non-strict code silently no-ops. Gate
  both throw sites on the target function's is_strict() flag.

- Function.prototype had a fictitious own `[Symbol.species]` accessor
  that doesn't exist in the real spec, which accidentally made
  SpeciesConstructor "work" for any function used as a constructor.
  Removing it exposed that Array itself never got its own @@species
  accessor (RegExp/Promise already have theirs) — subclasses inherit
  species through the constructor's prototype chain, not through
  Function.prototype, so `class X extends Array {}` needs Array's own
  accessor to get X back from ArraySpeciesCreate. Added it.

- Symbol.replace used the match result's "index" (a UTF-16 code-unit
  offset) directly as a byte offset into the CESU-8 input buffer,
  corrupting output whenever a match occurred after any astral
  character. Convert through char_offset_to_byte_offset like the
  other RegExp methods.

- re_compile() passed CESU-8 pattern bytes straight to lre_compile(),
  which parses standard UTF-8; a surrogate pair typed directly in a
  u/v-flag pattern decoded as two lone surrogates instead of one
  astral codepoint. Recombine pairs into real UTF-8 before compiling,
  unicode-mode patterns only (non-unicode mode operates on code units
  and rejects codepoints above 0xFFFF). The recombined buffer must
  still be NUL-terminated: lre_compile's UTF-8 decoder is documented
  to read up to 4 bytes past the last consumed byte for buffers that
  aren't null-terminated, so an exact-sized malloc was an intermittent
  heap over-read.

commits.subject: class: fix method/accessor property ordering, restricted-name checks, and double-super() semantics
commits.body:
Fixes 23 of the 26 class-semantics test262 failures tracked in BACKLOG.md:

- instantiate_closure now defines .length before .name so
  Object.getOwnPropertyNames order matches spec (SetFunctionLength before
  SetFunctionName) for both plain functions and class static members.
- Function.prototype.bind no longer copies the target's .prototype onto the
  bound function's own property table — bound functions have no own
  .prototype per BoundFunctionCreate; [[Construct]] already re-dispatches to
  the target, which resolves its own .prototype at call time. This also
  fixes `class C extends boundFn {}` correctly rejecting a target with no
  .prototype.
- The function.caller/.arguments poison-pill check (GETPROP, GETPROPC2,
  PUTPROP) now only fires when the function has no own property of that
  name, so `class C { static get arguments() {} }`-style overrides work.
- yield-expression parsing now honors the `[no LineTerminator here]`
  restriction before `*` and before the operand, matching the ASI-restricted
  production pattern used elsewhere in the parser.
- super() double-invocation: BindThisValue's "already initialized" check
  was only implemented for lightfunc/bound/builtin superclass targets; the
  common case (a compiled superclass constructor) silently no-op'd on a
  second super() call instead of throwing. super_init_this_chain now
  reports whether the target frame was already bound so RET/RETUNDEF can
  throw ReferenceError after the (already-executed) superclass constructor
  returns, matching spec ordering (construct-then-bind).
- RET (explicit `return;`/`return undefined;`) now applies the same
  "must call super in derived constructor" TDZ check RETUNDEF already had
  for implicit fallthrough returns.
- GeneratorFunction/AsyncFunction dynamic constructors now set .length/.name,
  use GetPrototypeFromConstructor for subclassing, use the correct
  .prototype property flags, and are marked non-constructable.
- Promise constructor now rejects a missing/non-callable executor
  argument instead of silently returning a pending promise.

Not fixed: private class fields (#x) are unimplemented at the lexer level
(2 tests) — out of scope for this cluster. class-definition-null-proto-this
uncovered a pre-existing bug where an arrow function's lexical `this` is
resolved from the calling activation instead of its defining activation,
which needs its own fix.

commits.subject: array: fix Array.prototype conformance cluster (Proxy, species, iterators, holes)
commits.body:
Fixes 23 of 28 failing built-ins/Array/prototype tests from BACKLOG.md
priority 1:

- Array iterators (values/keys/entries) now latch `done` once exhausted
  and build a proper {value, done} result on subsequent next() calls,
  instead of re-checking length forever (A5).
- entries/keys/values throw TypeError on null/undefined `this` (ToObject)
  instead of silently wrapping it (A3/A6).
- find/findLast now read length (and propagate getter/ToNumber throws)
  before the IsCallable(predicate) check, matching spec step order (A3).
- array_species_create_result's ArrayCreate fallback now throws RangeError
  when length > 2^32-1, matching the comment that already claimed this
  behaviour — this also unblocks the splice species-create TIMEOUT cluster
  (was looping/misbehaving on 2^53-scale lengths) (A4).
- reduce/reduceRight no longer silently truncate the index argument to a
  fastint when it exceeds FASTINT_MAX (48-bit); reduceRight's loop index
  was additionally a 32-bit `int`, wrapping negative for near-2^53 lengths.
- Removed the incorrect Function.prototype[@@species] accessor: no engine
  or test262 defines this, and its writable:false/set:undefined shape
  broke ordinary `fn[Symbol.species] = X` assignments used throughout the
  species-constructor test cluster.
- array_set_elem/array_set_elem_ulong now route through the Proxy [[Set]]
  trap; new arr_delete_elem_or_throw helper routes deletes through
  [[Delete]] and also clears dense-array holes (named-table delete alone
  left stale values behind in a dense ARRAY's slot storage).
- reverse rewritten to the spec's HasProperty-then-Get-then-Set/Delete
  algorithm (needed for correct Proxy trap ordering and hole preservation).
- Fixed a byte-range bug in the String-wrapper indexed-property readers
  (arr_get_elem, arr_get_elem_vm, TypedArray.prototype.set's string-source

commits.subject: compiler+vm: make GETPROP's ToPropertyKey writeback opt-in via GETPROP_CACHE
commits.body:
GETPROP used to unconditionally write its ToPropertyKey-coerced key back
into the key register, which is a spec-idempotency requirement for
compound/logical-assign and postfix/prefix increment on computed members
(`base[key] += rhs` must invoke ToPropertyKey(key) exactly once) — but it
made GETPROP itself unsafe to use on any register that might alias a live
local variable, requiring every callsite to shield the key first.

Split this into two opcodes: GETPROP stays side-effect-free on its key
register (safe everywhere), while the new GETPROP_CACHE additionally
caches the coerced key back into C, and is only emitted by member_expr's
computed-member (`[expr]`) branch — the sole place that may need the
cached key for a follow-up PUTPROP. Plain assignment continues to strip
the GETPROP_CACHE instruction from the bytecode stream before it executes
(as it already did for GETPROP), so evaluation order for `obj[k] = v`
(ToPropertyKey after RHS) is unaffected.

shield_computed_key is kept: GETPROP_CACHE has the same in-place-mutation
hazard the old unconditional GETPROP writeback had, just now scoped to
three call sites (member_expr, call_expr, new_expr's computed-member
branches) instead of leaking into GETPROP itself.

commits.subject: builtins: honor new.target prototype in Object/Function constructors
commits.body:
ES2015 §9.2.2 [[Construct]] step 5/2.a requires a base constructor
used as a super class to call
OrdinaryCreateFromConstructor(newTarget, "%Object.prototype%") (or
"%Function.prototype%") for the new instance. Previously
builtin_object / builtin_function always allocated their instance with
prototype = heap.object_proto / heap.function_proto, so a derived
class like `class Sub extends Object {}` produced instances whose
[[Prototype]] was Object.prototype — not Sub.prototype.

Use the existing builtin_proto_from_new_target helper, which is the
same path the other primitive wrappers (Boolean/Number/String) already
take. Direct `new Object()` / `new Function()` is unaffected because
ctx.new_target is set to the callee, and the helper then returns the
default intrinsic prototype.
