commits.subject: compiler: destructuring assignment defers RHS-independent side effects
commits.body:
Object/array destructuring assignment (`{[k()]: t.p} = src()`) eagerly
emitted code for computed keys and member-expression targets at
pattern-parse time, before the RHS was even parsed. Spec §12.15 says
the RHS runs first, then each computed key, then each target, then the
per-property [[Get]]/[[Set]] — so we produced the wrong observable
order (log showed sourceKey/target/targetKey before source).

Extended the deferred member-target mechanism (session 280 lexer-
snapshot-and-reparse) to (a) object-pattern computed keys and (b)
`{key: target}` member targets. Added a TOPROPKEY opcode because
ToPropertyKey coercion runs as its own step before the deferred
target evaluates — folding it into GETPROP wouldn't give the right
side-effect ordering.

Also fixes 3 nested-pattern compile errors (`[[x[yield]]] = v`):
collect_arr_param_binds/collect_obj_param_binds only accepted
identifier leaves, so nested sub-patterns of an assignment couldn't
contain member-expression targets. Added parent_idx propagation
through the assign-bind collectors so member targets are accepted
and deferred at any depth.

Register-clobber fix: pre-allocated bind_reg for member-target leaves
sat below persistent member_obj_reg/member_prop_reg/computed_key_reg,
which the accessor-getter call frame (placed at GETPROP's result
register) would silently corrupt. Allocated lazily inside
emit_destruct_bindings, after persistent regs are known.

Also fixed a latent .done/.value ordering bug in the shared iterator-
step emitter — read .value before .done, violating IteratorStep/
IteratorValue spec ordering when .value is an accessor.

commits.subject: compiler: computed member key copies live locals before GETPROP writeback
commits.body:
GETPROP writes the ToPropertyKey-coerced string back into its key
register so a follow-up PUTPROP on the same register (compound
assignment's read-op-write sequence) doesn't re-invoke ToPrimitive.
When the key expression resolved directly to a live local var register
(e.g. `arr[idx]` where idx is a local), the writeback mutated the
local — turning `idx` from number 0 into string "0" mid-callback and
breaking every `!==` comparison against 0. Manifested as ~20 Array
prototype callback regressions (every/filter/forEach/map/reduce/some).

Fix: at compile time in the 4 computed-member parse sites (member_expr,
call_expr's [], new_expr's [], optional-chain a?.[]), if the index
expression resolved to a local-var register, copy it to a fresh temp
before GETPROP. Temps are safe to overwrite; locals no longer are.

Idempotency (T4) preserved for real compound-assignment keys, which
always resolve to a computed expression temp, not a local reg.

commits.subject: vm: super property assign evaluates RHS before null-proto TypeError
commits.body:
Per spec, MakeSuperPropertyReference (§13.3.7.1) computes the super
base eagerly at LHS-evaluation time but never throws (GetSuperBase
just returns null for a null-prototype HomeObject); the actual
ToObject(base) TypeError only happens inside PutValue, after the RHS
has been fully evaluated (§6.2.5.6). The compiler was instead emitting
an eager GETPROP_SUPER read of the LHS before parsing the assignment
operator, throwing immediately and skipping RHS evaluation.

assignment_expr now strips that eager GETPROP_SUPER (and its paired
LDTHIS this-binding probe) the same way it already strips a plain
GETPROP for member assignment targets, deferring the null-base throw
to PUTPROP_SUPER's own runtime check, which runs after the RHS.

Fixing this exposed a second, unrelated bug blocking the same two
tests: static methods' `super.x` was resolving HomeObject against the
class prototype (__super__) instead of the constructor itself, so
`Object.setPrototypeOf(C, null)` on a static method's class never
affected its super lookup. Added a separate __static_super__ binding
(bound to the constructor) and a super_is_static_method compile flag,
threaded through all inner-function propagation sites, so static
methods resolve super against the constructor per §13.3.7.1.

Fixes test262 language/expressions/assignment/target-super-computed-reference-null.js
and target-super-identifier-reference-null.js. Also fixes
language/statements/class/super/in-static-methods.js, in-static-getter.js,
in-static-setter.js (phase 15: 0 regressions, 4 fixes; phase 2: 0
regressions after accounting for known batch-runner flakiness).

commits.subject: compiler: compound-assignment evaluates ToPropertyKey before RHS
commits.body:
GETPROP/PUTPROP/GETPROP_SUPER/PUTPROP_SUPER silently swallowed a
ToPropertyKey failure from get_prop_key (e.g. prop.toString() throwing):
the key==null case fell through without checking vm.throw_pending, so
the pending error was discarded and execution continued into the RHS
of a compound assignment instead of propagating. Fixed all four
opcodes to check vm.throw_pending and route through vm_throw_value.

GETPROP also now writes the resolved key back into its key register so
a follow-up PUTPROP on the same register (compound assignment's
read-op-write sequence) is idempotent — ToPropertyKey is only supposed
to run once per `base[prop] op= rhs`.

Plain `super[prop] = expr()` doesn't evaluate ToPropertyKey until after
both operands are evaluated (§13.15.2 defers the read). The compiler's
existing peephole that strips the LHS's read-instruction for plain
member assignment only recognized GETPROP; extended it to also strip
GETPROP_SUPER, sliding the LDTHIS staged for super-call this-binding
down over the removed slot.

Fixes 11 failing test262 compound-assignment tests
(S11.13.2_A7.1_T3..A7.11_T3) plus 11 latent T4 idempotency failures
and one super-assignment ordering test; zero regressions against the
phase 2 baseline (two flaky dstr tests reproduce independently of this
change).

commits.subject: compiler: SetFunctionName on plain assignment `x = anonymous fn`
commits.body:
Per ES2015 §12.15.4, `x = function(){}` must name the RHS "x" when the
LHS is a simple IdentifierReference (not a member expression or a
parenthesized identifier). assignment_expr now tracks the LHS
identifier's raw text (getvar/local-var paths) and sets the existing
has_inferred_name/inferred_name_buf mechanism before parsing the RHS,
mirroring the `var x = fn` case already handled in statements.c3.

Two supporting fixes were needed: object/array literals must clear any
pending inferred name on entry (it doesn't apply to them and was
leaking into unrelated later function expressions, e.g. `var o = {};
o.attr = function(){}` was wrongly naming the anonymous function "o");
and a parenthesized identifier LHS (`(fn) = function(){}`) is not an
IdentifierRef per the static semantics, so the saved LHS name is
cleared when returning from a grouping expression.

commits.subject: compiler: don't force regex-after-} for function-expression/method bodies
commits.body:
Lexer.note_block_close() marks a following `/` as the start of a
RegularExpressionLiteral rather than division, but CompilerContext.block()
called it unconditionally — including when the block being closed is a
function-expression or method body used in *expression* position (e.g.
`function(){return 1} / x`). Since the whole function is itself an operand
there, the following `/` must be division. Threaded an is_expr flag through
block()/compile_inner_function()/parse_function_body() so only statement-
position block closes (declarations, standalone blocks) set the regex hint.

(and 5 other tests) when run with the assert.js/sta.js test262 harness.

commits.subject: vm: fix ToInt32, exponentiation ±1**±Inf, relational compare on objects
commits.body:
Cluster E of phase-2 test262 sweep — 11 tests fixed, 0 regressions.

- ToInt32: fast-path (int)d truncates toward zero, wrong for negative
  values with a fractional part after mod. Spec is floor(abs(d))*sign
  then mod 2^32; fixed the slow path accordingly (also handles NaN/Inf
  up-front). Fixes S11.7.{1,2,3}_A5.1_T1 (left/right/unsigned shift).

- EXP opcode: C99 pow(±1, ±Inf)=1 but ES2016 §12.6.4 says NaN. Guard
  abs(base)==1 && !isFinite(exp) → NaN before math::pow. Fixes
  applying-the-exp-operator_A7/A8.

- LT/LE/GT/GE + 8 fused JMP_* variants: object operands took the
  vm_to_number fallback directly, skipping the string-string re-check
  after ToPrimitive("number") — so `fn > {}` compared numerically as
  NaN>NaN instead of "function(){...}" > "[object Object]". New
  vm_relational_compare helper does the spec §7.2.14 dance in one
  place; the 12 near-identical dispatch blocks collapse into 2 shared
  bodies. Fixes greater-than/less-than/…-or-equal A3.2_T1.2.

commits.body:

commits.subject: vm: fix builtin [[Construct]] semantics and builtin result ownership
commits.body:
Two latent VM bugs surfaced by the tighter register allocation (both
depended on which stale values happened to sit in reused register slots):

1. NEW_OBJ on builtin function objects. Every FUNCTION HObject defaults
   flags.constructable=true, so `new String.prototype.charAt` dispatched
   the builtin as a constructor with `this` read from the callee_reg+1
   slot — which the compiler never writes for `new`. The old register
   layout happened to leave an object there (the method's receiver check
   threw, passing tests by accident); the new layout left a string and
   `new charAt` silently succeeded. NEW_OBJ builtin paths now pass an
   undefined `this` and gate dispatch on builtin_fn_is_constructor
   (lightfunc constructor table + typed arrays, ArrayBuffer, DataView,
   Proxy, callable-proxy trampoline, %AsyncFunction%), throwing
   "not a constructor" per ES §10.3. Fixes the S15.5.4.*_A7 family.

2. Builtin results written directly into register slots are borrowed
   references — pass-through builtins (e.g. Promise.resolve(p) reached
   through .bind's re-dispatch) return an existing object without
   increfing. decref_callee_regs sweeps every slot up to max_heap_reg
   assuming owned references, so a borrowed slot below the high-water
   mark was over-decrefed and the live object freed back to the pool
   (ASan use-after-poison; crashed the Promise invoke-resolve tests).
   The remaining direct-register dispatch sites in the CALL family now
   use the local-result + tval_copy_ref + track_heap_store pattern the
   main HObject path already used, which also removes their stale
   ctx.result pointer hazard across valstack reallocs.

bench-fast at baseline.

commits.subject: compiler: reclaim statement temporaries; pin params; register overflow is a compile error
commits.body:
Three related register-allocator fixes:

- statement() now records the allocator watermark and reclaims every
  register above it (except scope-tracked local slots) after each
  statement. Member calls strand ~2 registers per statement — the 'this'
  object register sits below the call window it outlives, so its LIFO
  free_reg is an out-of-order no-op. 306 assert.sameValue() statements
  were enough to exhaust all 512 registers (the bigint-arithmetic.js
  worker abort).

- free_reg/free_regs_to never release registers below reserved_regs,
  pinned after parameter/hoist allocation at each body-compile site.
  An expression statement whose result register was a parameter could
  previously free it, letting the next temp clobber the parameter
  (pre-existing; masked by the leaks the reclaim removes — a wrapper
  calling f(err) would pass f itself once GETVAR reused the slot).

- alloc_reg/alloc_regs no longer abort() on register exhaustion: they
  set reg_overflow and clamp, and finish() reports a COMPILE_ERROR. A
  pathological source now fails its own compile instead of killing the
  host process (and every queued test behind it in a batch worker).

commits.subject: compiler: re-parse deferred destructuring member targets instead of replaying captured bytecode
commits.body:
The deferred member-target mechanism (targets like [...obj['a'+'b']] whose
lref must be evaluated after GetIterator, inside the IteratorClose guard)
captured the collection-time bytecode, NOP'd it, and re-emitted it verbatim
at the guard. The captured instructions carried absolute register numbers
from the collection watermark, so replaying them at the emission watermark
clobbered live state — in array-rest-lref.js the key-eval scratch LDCONST
landed on the rest array's NEWARR register, appending a phantom element. The
scheme also capped targets at 16 instructions and could not survive a CALL
frame overlay inside the target expression.

collect_assign_target now parses the target once at collection purely to
advance past it — the emitted code and registers are discarded — and stores
a heap-allocated lexer snapshot in the bind. emit_destruct_bindings re-parses
the target at the point of use via emit_deferred_target, so its registers are
allocated at the live watermark, then copies the evaluated object/key down
into a persistent pair pre-allocated below every iterator/push callee window
so they survive the protocol CALLs up to the final PUTPROP. The two collect
sites and two replay sites now share these single helpers.

Fixes both array-rest-lref regressions and 9 more assignment/dstr
iterator-close tests (thrw-close family); phases 12-14/21 and the
destructuring suites show no regressions.

commits.subject: vm: propagate return/throw completions through yield in destructuring thunks
commits.body:
The remaining for-of/dstr IteratorClose failures all had a `yield` (or
side-effecting expression) inside a destructuring default value or computed
target key in a for-of head, resumed via generator .return()/.throw(). Two
gaps let those abrupt completions leak:

1. When a generator suspends at a yield nested inside a non-generator thunk
   (default-expr / computed-key thunk), the CALL-site resume path always placed
   the resume value and continued normally — so a .return()/.throw() resumed as
   if it were .next(), swallowing the completion (the body ran, "unreachable"
   executed, and `{} = yield` saw undefined). The resume path now detects a
   thunk-yield resume with resume_kind RETURN/THROW and injects the completion
   into the restored generator frame: THROW routes via vm_throw_value, RETURN
   routes through the nearest enclosing finally (else completes the generator) —
   mirroring LOAD_RESUME's own THROW/RETURN handling.

2. The destructuring IteratorClose finally hard-coded ITER_CLOSE B=1 (suppress
   .return() errors), which is only correct for a throw completion. A new B=2
   "auto" mode inspects the in-finally catcher's pending state: it suppresses
   only when the pending completion is a throw, and propagates a throwing or
   non-object .return() for return/break/continue/normal completions
   (§7.4.6 steps 6/8). The destructuring finally now emits B=2.

Fixes the 8 remaining for-of/dstr rtrn-close / rtrn-close-err / rtrn-close-null
tests; also improves the parallel assignment/dstr close tests. Zero regressions
across for-of, for-in, generators, yield, try, and destructuring suites.

commits.subject: compiler: correct IteratorClose for rest destructuring targets
commits.body:
Two fixes to the array-rest destructuring emitter so IteratorClose matches
ES2022 §13.15.5.3 / §7.4.6-7.4.8:

- Latch [[done]] across the rest-collection .next()/.done/.value reads (both the
  synthetic-rest and leaf-rest loops): park the iterator in save_reg and clear
  method_reg before each step, restoring only after a successful not-done step.
  A throw from .next() now leaves the iterator [[done]], so the enclosing finally
  does NOT call .return() on it (was calling it, e.g. array-rest-iter-thrw-close-skip).

- Defer the rest member-target lref evaluation: capture and NOP the target's
  bytecode at collection time and re-emit it inside emit_destruct_bindings AFTER
  the iterator is opened. A throw from a side-effecting rest target such as
  `[...{}[thrower()]]` now runs IteratorClose on the open iterator (was evaluating
  the target before GetIterator, so .return() was never called).

commits.subject: compiler: close destructuring iterators via finally, not catch-only
commits.body:
emit_destruct_bindings guarded its array-iterator IteratorClose with a
catch-only TRY, so the close ran on a throw completion but NOT on a return /
break / continue completion (e.g. a generator .return() resuming a `yield`
inside the destructuring). Per ES2022 §13.15.5.3 IteratorClose must run on
every abrupt completion.

The guard is now lowered as try/FINALLY: the finally runs ITER_CLOSE for each
active iterator and ENDFINALLY re-dispatches the pending completion. The finally
also runs on normal completion, which subsumes the previous separate
normal-path IteratorClose (covering §13.15.5.3's not-done close of a
partially-consumed iterator). No regressions across the for-of, assignment, and
variable destructuring suites.

commits.subject: compiler: heal callee window each iteration in for-of head destructuring
commits.body:
`for (let [x] of gen)` / `for ([...] of gen)` where the source is a generator
crashed on the second iteration ("Cannot read properties of undefined") because
the outer loop loaded its .next callee/this registers once before the loop and
kept the yielded value in registers inside the .next() call frame. When the
nested (head) destructuring resumed the generator, its frame overlaid that
window and clobbered callee_reg/next value, so the next iteration called the
generator function (fresh GEN_START) instead of .next.

Both head-destructuring emitters (the let/const inline path and the bare
assignment-target emit_bare_forof_destruct_loop) now:
  - copy the yielded value into a holder allocated BELOW the callee window,
    free the above-callee protocol temps, then destructure the holder; and
  - reload callee/callee_this from the below-window next_reg/method_reg at the
    top of every iteration (matching the plain for-of loop).

Fixes the {let,const,var}-ary-ptrn-elem-id-iter-val-array-prototype for-of/dstr
tests (custom Array.prototype[Symbol.iterator] generator). No regressions across
the for-of suite.

commits.subject: vm: construct_fn handles derived classes and rest params (Promise subclassing)
commits.body:
The internal Construct path (Heap.construct_fn, used by NewPromiseCapability
for Promise.all/allSettled/race/any/resolve/reject with a subclass `this`)
did not support derived class constructors:

- It always pre-allocated a plain object as `this` and never set
  ACT_FLAG_DERIVED, so for `class Custom extends Promise {}` the activation's
  this_binding was not the TDZ sentinel and super() never rebound it. The
  constructed instance was lost and the capability read back uninitialized
  ("Promise capability not initialized by constructor").

- It copied arguments positionally, ignoring a rest parameter, so the implicit
  derived constructor `constructor(...args){ super(...args); }` saw the raw
  first arg in its rest slot instead of an array. `super(...args)` then
  forwarded nothing and the base Promise constructor's executor never ran, so
  resolve/reject were never captured.

construct_fn now: starts a derived target with a TDZ-sentinel this_binding and
ACT_FLAG_DERIVED, reads the super-initialized instance back from the
activation's this_binding on return, and builds the rest array in the rest slot
(mirroring the normal call path). Fixes Promise.{all,allSettled,race,any,resolve}
subclassing tests (e.g. invoke-resolve-on-promises-every-iteration-of-custom,
capability-resolve-throws-reject).

commits.subject: compiler: don't clobber a live local when compiling `typeof local.prop`
commits.body:
`typeof d.value` where `d` is a local variable corrupted `d`: the typeof
member branch reused last_member_obj_reg as the TYPEOF result destination,
but for a bare-local base that register IS the live variable, so it was
overwritten with the result string. A subsequent read of `d.value` then saw
a string and threw "in requires an object" / "cannot read property".

(last_member_obj_is_local); when it is, the typeof branch writes the result
in place into the GETPROP result temp (the only owned temp on top of the
stack in RHS mode) instead of into the base register, leaving the variable
intact. The non-local case is unchanged.

var t=typeof d.value; return 'x' in d.value;}` — previously threw, now works.

commits.subject: module: instantiate exported function declarations at link time (16.2.1.5.5)
commits.body:
A cyclic import that read an exported `function` binding before the owning
module's body had run observed `undefined` instead of the hoisted function,
and even in the non-cyclic case the export's identity changed once the body
ran. Per ECMA-262 16.2.1.5.5 (InitializeEnvironment) step 17, a module's
top-level function declarations are instantiated during LINKING — before any
module body executes — so their closures exist and are identity-stable from
the moment linking completes.

Implementation:

- New ModuleDef.func_decls list (name + inner_funcs index), mirrored by the
  compiler-side CompModuleDef/CompFuncDeclEntry (layout must match, since the
  compiler writes into the runtime ModuleDef via current_module).

- The compiler records every top-level module `function` declaration into
  func_decls and no longer emits body-level CLOSURE+DECLVAR for them:
  hoist_global_fn_decls handles plain/non-exported declarations; the
  `export function` and `export default function` sites handle exported ones.
  Scripts (non-module) keep in-body instantiation unchanged.

- link_module instantiates each func_decl once, binding the module env as both
  var and lex environment, before pre-declaring the remaining (var/let/const)
  exports. The CLOSURE-opcode body was factored into vm::instantiate_closure so
  the linker and the VM share one closure-construction path.

- Fixed a latent GC bug surfaced by this: link_module creates mod.env first, so
  execute_module's env-creation branch (which registered the env bindings as a
  GC root) was skipped in the normal pipeline, leaving module bindings unrooted
  between link and evaluation. link_module now roots the env bindings itself.

test_vm gains a `--module <path>` flag driving the full resolve→link→evaluate
pipeline, used to reproduce and verify the fix.

commits.subject: module: TDZ semantics for cross-module let/const/class exports
commits.body:
An import (or namespace property read) of an exported let/const/class
binding that hasn't run its initializer yet returned undefined instead of
throwing ReferenceError (ECMA-262 10.4.6.8 / 16.2.1.5.5). link_module now
pre-declares lexical local exports as the TDZ sentinel (reusing
env::tdz_sentinel) instead of plain undefined, so a cyclically-importing
module's live-binding accessor observes TDZ before the owning module's
body runs its own INITTZ/PUTLEX. ExportEntry/CompExportEntry gained an

commits.subject: module: live module namespace bindings (plan 053 follow-up)
commits.body:
Module namespace exports and named imports were snapshotted by value at
link/execute time, so a later mutation of an exported binding in the
source module was invisible to importers and to `import * as ns`

(ECMA-262 SS10.4.6 / SS16.2).

(module::install_live_binding / build_namespace_object), resolving one
level of re-export indirection via resolve_export_binding_source and
guarding against self-referential accessors that would otherwise recurse
forever on unresolved self-imports.

commits.subject: compiler: fix register leak in typeof applied to a member access
commits.body:
typeof on a member-access operand (e.g. `typeof Date.parse`) leaked
two registers per occurrence: member_expr keeps the obj/prop registers
of a member access live (for a possible assignment target), and the
typeof fallback path allocated its result register on top of them
before freeing anything, which made free_reg on the lower registers a
silent no-op (free_reg only pops the top of the LIFO register stack).
After ~130 occurrences this exhausted the register file and aborted
compilation.

Fix: reuse the operand's own register (or the member's obj register,
freeing prop/op_typeof first) to hold the TYPEOF result instead of
allocating a new one on top, restoring correct LIFO order.

commits.subject: compiler: reject import(x) and other non-simple targets in update/assignment
commits.body:
ImportCall produces a value, not a Reference (ES2024 §13.3.10), so it is
not a SimpleAssignmentTarget. The compiler previously compiled
`import(x)++`, `++import(x)`, and `import(x) = v` successfully instead of
raising an early SyntaxError, and the same was true for CallExpressions
(`f()++`, `f() = v`) — the assignment/update-target validation the engine
already has for member/getvar targets simply had no "reject" branch, it
only ever chose how to emit the store.

Fix: in assignment_expr/postfix_expr/unary_expr's prefix INC/DEC, reject
with COMPILE_ERROR when the parsed operand is neither a member expression
(last_was_member), an environment variable (last_was_getvar), nor a
register-resident local variable (last_was_local_var) — the same flags the
compiler already tracks to decide how to emit PUTPROP/PUTVAR_ASSIGN
stores. import(...) now clears last_was_member/last_was_getvar after
emitting DYN_IMPORT, exactly like a CallExpression clears them after
emit_call, so both are rejected via one shared mechanism (no duplicated
target-detection logic).

While bisecting a startup regression this surfaced a latent bug in
binary_expr: last_was_local_var was unconditionally cleared on every loop
iteration (including before checking operator precedence), so it never
survived back to the caller even when no binary operator followed the
operand. That silently defeated the local-var check for any bare
identifier target went through binary_expr (essentially all of them),
which is fixed by restoring self.last_was_local_var from the loop's
left_is_local before returning.

Validated: all 17 test262 dynamic-import assignment/update-target
negative-parse tests now report COMPILE_ERROR (were FAIL); a 400+ file
regression sample across assignment/postfix-increment/postfix-decrement/
prefix-increment/prefix-decrement shows zero PASS regressions, only
additional correct FAIL->COMPILE_ERROR fixes for other non-simple-target
cases (this++, new.target++, target-number, etc.) already covered by the
same fix.

commits.subject: promise: fix derived promise never settling for non-thenable results
commits.body:
promise_coerce_thenable() signals "not a thenable" by returning a plain
null HObject* (not a fault) — it never actually errors for non-thenable
inputs. The caller in promise_microtask_after used `if (catch err = ...)`
to distinguish "not a thenable" from "adopted by thenable", but since no
fault is ever raised, the catch branch was dead code and every call fell
into the else branch, which unconditionally returned without settling
the downstream promise.

This meant a .then()/.catch() handler returning ANY plain value (not
just undefined, though that's the most visible case) left the derived
promise stuck pending forever, breaking chains like
`.then(h).then(k)` whenever h returned undefined, a number, a string, a
thrown-adopted rejection was unaffected, but plain fulfillment values
and undefined were both swallowed.

Fix: check `coerced != null` directly instead of relying on `catch`,
since promise_coerce_thenable's success value (null vs non-null) is the
actual signal, not its fault channel.

Validated: Promise/then+catch test262 subdir 52->75 pass (0 regressions,
23 newly passing); full built-ins/Promise suite 432->557 pass, 271->146
fail (0 regressions); both target dynamic-import tests now PASS without
hanging.

commits.subject: fix: use zero_regs_undefined() for async function register init in slow call path
commits.body:
The slow call path (used by async/generator functions) used libc::memset(0)
to zero remaining registers after copying arguments. But memset(0) sets raw
bytes to 0, which for NaN-boxed TVals produces the number 0, not undefined.

This caused async functions with default parameters to receive 0 instead of
undefined for missing arguments, breaking the param !== undefined check that
triggers default value application.

The fast call path (used by sync functions) correctly uses zero_regs_undefined()
which calls set_undefined() on each register. The generator initial call path
also uses zero_regs_undefined(). Only the slow path (async initial call
fallthrough at line 1035+) used memset.

Changed the slow path to use zero_regs_undefined() for consistency with the
fast and generator paths.

Fixes methods-async-super-call-param and the default parameter evaluation
for all async functions (standalone and class methods).

commits.subject: Fix 6 class subclass tests in test262 phase 15
commits.body:
- Add CHK_PROT opcode to validate that superclass.prototype is Object or
  Null (ES2015 section 14.5.14 step 5.g.ii-iv). Fixes class P extends Proxy {}
  which should throw TypeError because Proxy.prototype is undefined.

- Add FWD_ARGS opcode that forwards rest arguments directly to super()
  without calling @@iterator. The default derived constructor now forwards
  args via array index access rather than spread/iterator protocol.
  Fixes default-constructor-spread-override test.

- Fix ENDFINALLY return handling for derived constructors: when a return
  is intercepted by a finally block, the constructor return logic
  (section 9.2.2 step 13) now correctly uses this_binding for non-object returns
  (e.g. super() in finally after return in try). Fixes all 4
  derived-class-return-override tests.

commits.subject: fix: use number constant for class accessor numeric literal names
commits.body:
When a class getter/setter uses a numeric literal name (e.g. `get 0x10()`),
the compiler was storing the raw token text (0x10) as the property key
string, causing it to be installed under the wrong key. Per the JS spec,
numeric property names should be coerced to strings via ToString(), so
0x10 should become 16.

Added name_is_number and name_num_value fields to ClassMethod to track
when the method name came from a NUMBER token. When building the key
constant, use add_number_constant() for NUMBER tokens (matching object
literal semantics) so the runtime get_prop_key() converts the number to
its proper string representation.

Fixes 24 test262 accessor-name failures in phase 15 (12 instance + 12
static, across expressions/statements class forms, covering hex, binary,
octal, exponent, leading decimal, and non-canonical numeric literals).

commits.subject: fix: IteratorClose in for-of destructuring LHS error paths
commits.body:
Fix three interrelated issues causing ~53 test262 phase 14 failures:

1. Outer iterator close (TRY/CATCH in emit_bare_forof_destruct_loop and
   let/const/var [a,b] of arr path): wrap destructuring + body in
   TRY/CATCH that calls ITER_CLOSE on the for-of iterator (B=1) on
   abrupt completion, matching emit_forof_loop and emit_forof_loop_member.

2. Deferred member-target evaluation (DestructBind.deferred_code): for
   patterns like [{}[thrower()]], the target evaluation bytecode was
   emitted during collect_arr_assign_binds — BEFORE the inner iterator
   was opened by emit_destruct_bindings. Now the bytecode is saved in
   DestructBind.deferred_code, NOPped out during collection, and
   re-emitted inside emit_destruct_bindings AFTER the inner iterator
   setup but BEFORE IteratorStep, matching ES2022 §13.15.5.6.

3. Exhaustion ITER_CLOSE on the normal exit path: emit ITER_CLOSE
   (B=0) when the iterator reports done:true, so the outer iterator
   is properly closed.

Results: phase 14 FAIL drops from 75 → 22. Rosetta 99/100 (no regression).

commits.subject: fix: destructuring assignment result register clobbering
commits.body:
array_destructure_assign() and object_destructure_assign() returned
rhs_reg directly, which was the same register holding a live variable
(e.g. vals). When the outer assignment
called free_reg(right), it freed the variable's register. The next
statement's register allocator reused it, corrupting the variable.

Fix: copy rhs_reg to a fresh temp before returning, so the outer
assignment's free_reg(right) targets only the temp, not the variable's
register.

Verified: rosetta 99/100 (pre-existing strict_mode failure only),
test262 phases 2/14 unchanged.

commits.subject: fix: separate body var_env from parameter scope when hasParameterExpressions
commits.body:
When a function has default parameter expressions, ES2015 section 9.2.10
step 27 requires a separate VariableEnvironment for the function body.
Without this, closures created by default parameter expressions could see
var declarations from the function body.

The fix emits PUSH_VAR/POP_VAR around the function body when
inner_has_func_lex is true. PUSH_VAR creates a new var_env and lex_env
for the body, so DECLVAR for body vars targets the new body var_env and
closures in default parameter expressions do not see body var declarations.

Fixes 18 class scope tests plus 2 function scope tests.
Phase 15: 2035 to 2053 pass, 168 to 150 fail, 0 regressions.

commits.subject: compiler: async flag never inherits from the enclosing body
commits.body:
function_expr and the arrow parsers read ctx.is_async — which is also the
enclosing body's flag — to decide whether the compiled function is async.
Inside a TLA module body (is_async stays true through statement parsing)
every plain function expression and arrow was therefore compiled async:
calling one returned a Promise instead of its value (broke module tests
like instn-local-bndng-const once hoisting stopped clobbering the flag).

- function_expr takes the expression's async-ness as a parameter (set by
  the 'async function' expression caller) and restores the enclosing flag
  after compiling.
- Arrow async-ness comes from pending_async_arrow_src — set exactly when
  primary_expr consumed 'async' in front of the arrow — instead of the
  ambient flag; the async-arrow entry no longer latches/clears is_async.

commits.subject: module: statement-level import(), self-import guard, async-flag clobber fixes
commits.body:
- Statement dispatch peeks IMPORT before consuming, so import(...) as an
  expression statement was routed to import_declaration and rejected;
  consume the token, check for LPAREN, and push back to pick the right path.
- link_module early-outs on EVALUATING: a dynamic self-import mid-body was
  re-linking the module, replacing its live env and downgrading the status
  so the body re-executed (SIGSEGV).
- The hoist passes and function_declaration conflated 'this declaration is
  async' with the enclosing function's is_async flag: inside an async
  function (or TLA module) body, a plain nested function declaration was
  compiled as async AND the enclosing function lost its async flag — so the
  VM never allocated its evaluation promise, and an awaited rejection then
  restarted the frame at its stale entry pc forever (the 6 dynamic-import
  namespace await-ns-* timeouts; reproducible with plain Promise.reject).
  Hoist passes now save/clear/restore the enclosing flag; the declaration's
  async-ness is an explicit function_declaration parameter.
- AWAIT of a rejected promise in a frame with no async promise now surfaces
  an uncaught error instead of restarting the frame (infinite-loop guard).

commits.subject: fix: allow yield in destructuring default expressions inside generators
commits.body:
When a yield expression appears as a destructuring default value inside a
generator (e.g. [x = yield] = []), the parser now accepts it and the VM
correctly suspends the enclosing generator.

Changes:
- compiler/functions.c3: propagate is_generator to compile_default_expr
  so yield is parsed inside default thunks, then clear is_generator on
  the compiled thunk (it must not be a generator itself)
- heap.c3: add pending_resume_reg to GeneratorState for yield-through
  thunk support
- vm/vm_generators.c3: when yield fires inside a non-generator inner
  function, walk up the activation chain to find the enclosing generator,
  pop intervening activations, save the generator's state from the
  correct activation, and record the call result register
- vm/vm_calls.c3: on generator resume, if pending_resume_reg is set,
  place the resume value into the call result register so the code after
  the CALL instruction sees the correct value
- vm/vm_execute.c3: initialize pending_resume_reg to 0xFFFF on
  GeneratorState allocation

Rosetta: 99/100 (same pre-existing strict_mode.js failure only)

commits.subject: fix: treat yield as identifier outside generators, propagate is_generator/is_async in compile_key_expr
commits.body:
- expressions.c3: When yield appears outside a generator, treat it as
  an identifier (same pattern as await outside async). This fixes
  [yield] as a computed property name in non-generator class bodies.

- functions.c3: propagate is_generator and is_async from the enclosing
  context into compile_key_expr's key_ctx, so non-inline key
  expressions lex yield/await correctly in generator/async contexts.

commits.subject: fix: compile computed property keys inline in generator/async contexts
commits.body:
When a class body appears inside a generator or async function, computed
property names like [yield] or [await expr] must be evaluated inline in
the enclosing function so they interact with the enclosing generator/async.

Previously, all computed keys were compiled as separate inner functions
(via compile_key_expr + CLOSURE + CALL). This broke yield/await inside
computed keys because the inner function is not a generator/async, so
YIELD/AWAIT opcodes inside it would fail at runtime.

Fix: when is_generator or is_async is set, compile the key expression
inline via assignment_expr() and store the result register. During method
installation, use that register directly instead of CLOSURE + CALL.

Also propagates is_generator/is_async through compile_key_expr so that
non-inline key expressions in generator/async contexts lex correctly.

Verified: 8 of 12 target tests now pass (the 4 remaining CE tests are
module/async tests with top-level-await, pre-existing and unrelated).
No rosetta regressions (99/100 pass).

commits.subject: fix: for-of IteratorClose on throw/error paths, .next() result type check
commits.body:
- ITER_CLOSE VM handler: use get_with_accessors to properly invoke accessor
  getters on the .return property (fixes tests where .return is a getter)
- ITER_CLOSE: add completion-type flag via B field (B=0 non-throw, B=1 throw)
  - Non-throw (break/return/exhaustion): propagate errors from .return access
    (TypeError if non-callable) and from .return() call
  - Throw (body threw): suppress all errors from .return access/call per
    ES2022 §7.4.6 steps 6,8 — the original throw takes precedence
- NEW opcode CHKOBJ: throws TypeError if register is not an Object
  (ES2022 §14.7.5.6 step 3.b — validate .next() result)
- emit_forof_loop: wrap assignment + body in TRY/CATCH so that any abrupt
  completion (throw, assignment error, etc.) calls IteratorClose before
  propagating
- emit_forof_loop_member: same TRY/CATCH wrapper + CHKOBJ for member-expr LHS
- functions.c3 destructuring catch block: use B=1 (throw completion) for
  ITER_CLOSE so errors from .return are suppressed during destructuring

commits.subject: promise: adopt a native promise returned from a .then handler
commits.body:
When a .then/await fulfillment handler returned a native Promise (e.g.
```.then(() => Promise.reject(e))```), the downstream promise was
FULFILLED with the promise object as its value instead of ADOPTING that
promise's state. promise_coerce_thenable deliberately returns null for native
promises, and promise_microtask_after then fell through to the
"settle-fulfilled-with-result" path — so a returned rejected promise never
propagated its rejection, and `await` of such a chain never settled.

Per the Promise Resolution Procedure (§27.2.1.3.2), a returned native promise
must be adopted. Add promise_adopt_native: if the returned promise is settled,
settle the downstream with the same state/result now; if pending, attach a
handler-less pass-through reaction so the downstream settles when the source
does. Call it from promise_microtask_after before the (non-native) thenable
coercion.

Fixes:
- `Promise.resolve().then(() => Promise.reject(e))` now rejects (was: no
  settlement).
- `await` of that chain propagates the rejection.
- top-level-await/module-import-rejection-tick now PASSes (3 of 4 TLA targets;
  only await-dynamic-import-rejection remains, needing real import()).

Verified no regressions: 361 built-ins/Promise tests (prototype/resolve/reject/
all/race) identical vs main (121 PASS/240 FAIL, 0 crash/hang); 200 async/await
tests identical; module + non-module sanity unaffected. Fulfillment adoption
(handler returns a resolved promise -> value chains, not the object) and
pending-then-reject adoption both verified.

commits.subject: module: top-level await evaluation (plan 053 Phase 2, partial)
commits.body:
Modules with top-level `await` (ES2022) now evaluate asynchronously and a
rejected top-level await surfaces as the module's uncaught error.

- compile_module marks the module body async (ctx.is_async = true), so
  top-level `await` emits AWAIT/LOAD_RESUME and suspends the module
  activation via the same machinery as async functions. Non-await modules
  simply never emit AWAIT.
- Add Vm.execute_module_async: allocates the module's evaluation Promise,
  runs the body as an ACT_FLAG_ASYNC activation, then drives the microtask
  queue until the promise settles. A REJECTED promise leaves its reason in
  heap.error_value; execute_module returns false so run_module_file reports a
  runtime throw with the correct type.
- Fix a latent VM crash on the dispatch restart loop: when the top-level
  async/module frame unwinds (uncaught throw in a top-level async body),
  vm_throw_value settles the promise, pops to activation_count 0, and requests
  a restart to "resume the caller" — but there is no caller. The restart loop
  then indexed vm.activations[-1]. Now it halts cleanly at count 0. This path
  was unreachable before top-level await (async functions always have a
  caller frame).

commits.subject: fix: switch CaseBlock lexical scoping (let/const/class/function leak)
commits.body:
ES2015 §14.12 gives a switch statement's CaseBlock its own lexical scope
via BlockDeclarationInstantiation. Declarations made directly in any
case/default clause (let, const, class, and function/generator/async-function
declarations) were leaking into the enclosing scope instead of being
confined to the switch, so referencing the name after the switch silently
succeeded instead of throwing ReferenceError.

Reuses block()'s existing PUSH_LEX/POP_LEX + INITTZ scoping mechanism,
widening the pre-scan to additionally collect class and (hoisted)
function-declaration names — block() only needed let/const because
function/class scoping wasn't previously exercised the same way inside
a CaseBlock. Two bugs found along the way:

- The CaseBlock's POP_LEX was emitted after end_addr was computed, so
  every case/default body's fall-through jump (and the "no match, no
  default" path) landed past it and skipped it entirely. Fixed by making
  end_addr point at the POP_LEX itself, with `break` jumps patched to
  land just after it instead (break already unwinds the CaseBlock's lex
  scope on its own via push_loop's saved_lex_depth).
- function_declaration() always binds via DECLVAR into the function-scoped
  var_env. Added a force_lexical_fn_decl flag, set while compiling a
  switch's case/default bodies, so a function/generator/async-function
  declared directly in a clause binds via PUTLEX into the CaseBlock's own
  lex_env instead, and disappears when POP_LEX runs.

commits.subject: fix: restricted-global let/const collision and unparseable postfix ASI
commits.body:
Two independent SyntaxError fixes:

- `let undefined;` (and NaN/Infinity) at Script/eval top level must throw a
  runtime SyntaxError per GlobalDeclarationInstantiation
  (HasRestrictedGlobalProperty). Added a THROW_SYNTAX opcode (mirrors the
  existing THROW_REF pattern) so the collision, detected during the
  existing top-level lexical pre-scan, surfaces as a runtime throw rather
  than a compile-time failure — matching the spec's `negative: phase:
  runtime` expectation. Module top-level bindings are exempt since they
  live in the Module Environment Record, not the Global one.

- Postfix `++`/`--` incorrectly ignored the ES5 §7.9.1 restricted-production
  rule that a LineTerminator before the operator forces ASI, so
  `eval("x = 1; x\n++")` silently parsed `x++` instead of failing on the
  now-dangling `++`. Fixed postfix_expr to check `seen_line_term`. This
  alone didn't surface a throw because `literal_keyword`'s default case
  silently emitted `undefined` for any unparseable token (e.g. a lone `++`
  or `+` with no operand) instead of raising a compile error — fixed to
  call `self.fail`, which lets `eval`'s existing SyntaxError-on-compile-fail
  path (builtin_eval) work as intended.

commits.subject: fix: implement AnnexB HTML-like comments (<!-- and -->) in lexer
commits.body:
Adds SingleLineHTMLOpenComment (<!--, comment to end of line, anywhere)
and SingleLineHTMLCloseComment (-->, comment to end of line, only at
start of a line) per AnnexB B.1.3. Tracks a persistent `at_line_start`
flag on the Lexer struct across skip_whitespace_and_comments calls so
mid-line `-->` (e.g. `x --> y`, a decrement+comparison) is still parsed
correctly, while `-->` following only whitespace/comments since the
last line terminator (or start of source, or a block comment spanning
a line terminator) is treated as a comment.

No module/script flag is reachable from the lexer, so this is applied
unconditionally; module code's `<!--`/`-->` syntax errors are not
enforced (see task report — this is a documented limitation, not a
regression since module comment handling wasn't implemented before).

commits.subject: test: enforce error-type + phase matching for negative tests
commits.body:

thrown exception's constructor name matches the declared `type` AND the error

which let a throw of the *wrong* type pass (e.g. the annexB HTML-comment tests
expect Test262Error but the engine throws ReferenceError because <!-- isn't
handled — that was scoring PASS).

- thrown_type_matches() reads the thrown value from heap.error_value (the
  uncaught-error unwind clears vm.throw_value), matches builtin errors by
  walking the prototype chain against the heap error protos, and matches
  everything else (Test262Error, custom errors) by thrown.constructor.name.
- run_one_test enforces throw + type match for negative:phase:runtime.

with wrong-type throws now correctly failing (verified: comment-single-lf
throws Test262Error -> PASS; single-line-html-open throws ReferenceError -> FAIL).

commits.subject: fix(unicode): workstream C — identifier registers, full case mapping, normalize, \x escapes
commits.body:
Four fixes in one commit (all verified pass individually and quick.sh 283/0):

1. hoist_decls / hoist_global_fn_decls: free var/fn registers after DECLVAR at
   global scope. Each `var` in a 6000-declaration test was permanently consuming
   a register slot; at >512 vars the compiler aborted with "register limit exceeded".
   Non-global function hoisting is unchanged (those registers are actual locals).
   Fixes all 24 language/identifiers/start-unicode-*.js tests.

2. Unicode case mapping (toLowerCase/toUpperCase/toLocale*): replace the
   ASCII-only 256-byte-buffer implementations with a full Unicode conversion
   using lre_case_conv from QuickJS libunicode. Handles multi-codepoint
   expansions (ß→SS, İ→i+0307), astral codepoints via CESU-8 surrogate pair
   reassembly, and Final_Sigma context-sensitive lowercase (Σ→ς vs Σ→σ).
   New unicode_case_conv / unicode_is_cased / unicode_is_case_ignorable wrappers
   in unicode_wrapper.c.  Fixes all 6 toLowerCase/toUpperCase test262 fails.

3. String.prototype.normalize: replace per-code-unit decode (which split astral
   chars into lone-surrogate "codepoints") with cesu8_to_codepoints (reassembles
   surrogate pairs before feeding libunicode). Re-encode back to CESU-8.
   Fixes 3 normalize test262 tests.

4. Lexer \xHH escape: stored raw byte (e.g. 0xC5) instead of UTF-8-encoding
   the Unicode codepoint U+00HH. Values >= 0x80 produced invalid CESU-8,
   causing str_intern to emit U+FFFD replacement characters. Fixed in both
   regular string literals and template literals.

commits.subject: fix: this_binding refcount underflow in nested vm_call_fn_impl
commits.body:
Root cause: repeated forEach/map callbacks via vm_call_fn_impl would
decrement the outer frames' this_binding refcount to zero (crashing)
because inline CALL's tval_copy_ref was writing new this_binding values
into activation slots that still held the outer activations' stale data
(after memcpy-save but before being zeroed).

Three-part fix:
1. tval_copy_ref: incref incoming value BEFORE decref of old, guarding
   same-object premature-free when src==dst points to the same object.
2. ACT_FLAG_THIS_OWNED (1<<5): set on every inline CALL/getter activation
   that uses tval_copy_ref for this_binding; handle_return decref's
   this_binding only when this flag is set, balancing the incref.
3. vm_call_fn_impl / vm_construct_fn_impl: after memcpy-saving outer
   activations to saved_acts, zero out vm.activations[1..N-1] so that
   the inner run's inline CALLs decref undefined (no-op) rather than
   stale global-object bits left by the saved outer activation data.

commits.subject: fix: MemberExpression targets in destructuring assignment + strict unresolvable ReferenceError
commits.body:
Problem 1: Array/object destructuring assignment patterns failed to parse when
an element target was a MemberExpression starting with an object or array
literal, e.g. `[{}.x] = arr` or `({key: {}.y} = obj)`. The compiler mistook
the leading `{`/`[` as the start of a nested sub-pattern.

Fix: Added `primary_is_member_target()` in destructuring.c3 — a speculative
scan that copies the lexer state, advances past the balanced bracket, and checks
if the next token is `.`, `[`, or `(`. When true, the element is routed through
`parse_assign_target_lhs` (full LHS expression) instead of the nested-pattern
collector. Applied at both the element level and the rest element level in
`collect_arr_assign_binds`, and at the property-value level in
`collect_obj_assign_binds`.

Problem 2: Assigning to an undeclared identifier in strict mode via a
destructuring assignment did not throw ReferenceError (e.g. `[undeclared] = []`
in strict mode silently created the global).

Fix: In `PUTVAR_ASSIGN` (vm_execute.c3), when `env_try_put_lex` returns 0 (not
found in lex env) and the function is strict and the identifier is absent from
the var env chain, throw ReferenceError per ES5 §11.13.1 / ES2015 §12.15.4.

commits.body:
Three root causes fixed across 9 test262 tests:

1. src/builtins/function.c3: Function.prototype.toString called on a callable
   Proxy exotic object was reading extra_ptr().func fields which overlap with
   proxy data. Now detects exotic_proxyobj and returns "function () { [native code] }"
   directly, as required by ES2019 §19.2.3.5.

2. src/vm/vm_coerce.c3: vm_to_string on a LIGHTFUNC (built-in function) was
   returning the literal "[function]" string instead of invoking
   Function.prototype.toString. This caused `"" + fn.apply` (where fn is a Proxy)
   to fail the NativeFunction syntax check. Now calls Function.prototype.toString
   via heap.call_fn so the correct "function name() { [native code] }" form is produced.

3. src/builtins/proxy.c3: Proxy [[Construct]] with no construct trap forwarded
   directly to construct_fn(target), losing the original proxy as new.target.
   For a base constructor, GetPrototypeFromConstructor(newTarget) must call
   Get(newTarget, "prototype"), which triggers the proxy's get trap. If that trap
   revokes the proxy, the subsequent GetFunctionRealm(newTarget) must throw TypeError
   (§7.3.22 step 4a). Now simulates this Get before forwarding so the revocation is
   detected and a TypeError is thrown.

holding the TDZ sentinel — so `({x}={x:5})` before `let x` did not throw. Plain
`x=5` only threw by accident via a spurious preceding GETVAR. env_try_put_lex
now returns -2 when the target binding is the TDZ sentinel, and PUTVAR throws
'Cannot access X before initialization'. Initialization uses PUTLEX/PUTLEX_C
(not PUTVAR), so this only rejects genuine before-declaration assignments.

Fixes TDZ-assignment for function- and block-scoped lets (incl. destructuring
assignment targets). Global-scope lets remain a separate gap (not TDZ-hoisted).
Zero regressions.

commits.subject: fix: uncaught throw in an async body rejects its Promise
commits.body:
An async function that threw an uncaught exception (before or after any await)
surfaced as a VM_ERROR instead of returning a rejected Promise — only the
resume-point throw path (LOAD_RESUME/AWAIT) rejected, not synchronous throws
from the body or a sync callee.

Fixed at the single chokepoint: vm_throw_value now recognizes the async-function
boundary the same way it recognizes catchers. When the catcher walk reaches an
async frame (ACT_FLAG_ASYNC) with no handler, the throw does not propagate to
the caller — it rejects the frame's Promise (which the caller already holds in
its result register), unwinds the async frame like a normal return, and resumes
the caller. Every opcode that can throw now settles the async Promise
correctly, unifying with the existing resume-point reject path.

Covers: sync throw, throw after await, throw from a sync helper called by the
async fn, nested async, non-Error throw values; inner try/catch still handles
locally without rejecting. +20 pass, 93.3% → 93.4%, zero regressions.

own throw path.

commits.subject: fix: Function.prototype.toString source retention for object method shorthand
commits.body:
Object-literal method shorthand (`{ m(){} }`, `{ get g(){} }`, `{ async m(){} }`)
retained source text that dropped the method name / prefix, so
`({m(){}}).m.toString()` returned "(){}" instead of "m(){}".

Root cause: match_async_method_prefix() consumes then pushes back the first
token via the compiler-context pushback stack; that pushback makes
refresh_token_start() early-return, leaving the lexer's token_start pointing
past the key for identifier keys. The method path then captured key_src_start
at the `(` rather than the key.

Fix: capture prop_src_start at the property's first token BEFORE any
async/star prefix is consumed, and use it as the source-retention origin for
all method forms (async/star prefixes, get/set, identifier/string/number/
computed keys). Since the span now already includes a leading `async `, the
async-prefix synthesis in compile_inner_function is suppressed when the
captured text already starts with "async " (still prepended for
`async function` declarations, which capture from `function`).

forms already worked and are unaffected. Remaining failures are comment/
whitespace-in-prefix edge cases and a missing harness helper.

commits.subject: fix: spec-compliant parseInt (ES2015 §18.2.5)
commits.body:
Rewrote builtin_parse_int, which delegated to libc strtol and inherited
several non-conformances:
- strtol with radix 0 applied C octal, so parseInt("010") returned 8 (spec: 10)
- whitespace-only input returned 0 instead of NaN
- only ASCII whitespace was stripped (spec strips Unicode StrWhiteSpace)
- radix argument was read raw instead of ToInt32-coerced
- large exact integers were truncated to the 48-bit fastint payload

New implementation strips full StrWhiteSpace (ASCII + the Unicode space /
BOM code points via UTF-8), handles sign, 0x/0X hex detection under radix
0/16, validates radix 2..36 (NaN otherwise), accumulates digits in a double
for arbitrary magnitude, and emits a fastint only within FASTINT range,
falling back to set_number for larger values.

parseInt cluster 23 fail -> ~1 (only an unrelated getOwnPropertyNames case
remains). Phase 8 ES5 Built-ins +20.

commits.subject: fix: for-of array/object destructuring RequireObjectCoercible + IteratorClose
commits.body:
Two ES2015 §13.3.3.6 conformance gaps in for-of binding destructuring:

1. Object patterns skipped RequireObjectCoercible. `for (var {} of [null])`
   silently bound nothing instead of throwing TypeError — the extraction
   loop is empty for `{}` and nothing checked the source. Emit REQUIRE_OBJ
   on the iterated value before the property-extraction loop (covers empty
   and non-empty object patterns alike).

2. Array patterns never closed the inner iterator. `for (let [x] of [iter])`
   left iter open when the pattern didn't exhaust it, so its return() was
   never invoked (step 4: IteratorClose when [[done]] is false). Track the
   most recent `done` value in a register across holes/simple bindings and,
   when the pattern has no rest element, conditionally emit ITER_CLOSE.

Phase 14 for-of 419 -> 434 (+15); Phase 3 +3. No regressions in phases 3/12/15.

commits.subject: fix: incref bound args in bound_call re-dispatch to prevent premature free
commits.body:
builtin_bound_call's compiled/BUILTIN_FN re-dispatch path copied the
prepended bound args into the callee's argument register window with raw
TVal assignment. The callee frame takes ownership of those slots and
decrefs them on overwrite/unwind, but the bound args were read out of the
stored bound-args array via get_prop_proto() without an incref. The result
was a net over-decref: a heap value passed as a bound argument (e.g. a
TypedArray constructor via `factory.bind(undefined, Float64Array)`) was
freed while still live. Its pool block was then recycled into the next
bound function, whose `.name = "bound <target>"` write corrupted the
original object — so `Float64Array.name` returned "bound makeArrayLike".

This corrupted nearly every test using testWithTypedArrayConstructors /
testWithAllTypedArrayConstructors (they .bind() each constructor as a
factory arg), plus any bound-function-with-heap-args pattern.

Root-caused with a hardware watchpoint: the victim object's memory was
never written through its own slot; instead its whole pool block was
freed at refcount 0 during a routine LDREG decref, then handed back out.

Fix: incref heap-ref bound args (indices < bound_argc) before writing them
into the callee register window. Appended call args (>= bound_argc) are
moved out of the caller's own registers and need no extra incref.

Phase 22 Buffers 857 -> 1119 (+262). Full suite 91.2% -> 92.1% (+258 pass),
no regressions.

commits.subject: fix: Promise.all/any/race/allSettled spec-conformant combinator semantics
commits.body:
Rewrote the Promise combinators to follow ES2021 §27.2.4: read C from `this`,
NewPromiseCapability(C), read C.resolve once (TypeError if not callable), and

handlers). Abrupt completions during iteration close the iterator
(IteratorClose, tolerant of null/undefined/non-callable return) and reject the
capability. allSettled builds the settled records correctly.

in phases 6/21.

commits.subject: fix: INITPROP opcode for class static data methods to override auto-set name
commits.body:
Class static methods like `class Foo { static name() {} }` need to override
the constructor's auto-set .name property. The runtime sets .name on every
function object at CLOSURE time (NWC: non-writable, non-enum, configurable),
and PUTPROP uses [[Set]] semantics which reject writes to non-writable
properties. Per ES2015 §14.5.13 class method installation uses
DefinePropertyOrThrow, which allows replacement when the existing
property is configurable.

Add a new INITPROP opcode with DefinePropertyOrThrow semantics and emit
it for static data methods. For data methods without a pre-existing
property, INITPROP and PUTPROP are equivalent, so use INITPROP only for
static methods (instance methods target the freshly-created prototype,
which has no pre-existing properties).

Object.defineProperty's existing-property paths were using own-prop checks
on the descriptor object to decide which fields were "present" — but per
ES5 §8.10.5 ToPropertyDescriptor, a field is present when [[Get]] returns
a value (even undefined), so inherited accessors that yield undefined
count as present. Restructure to_property_descriptor to return a struct
of has_* flags, then use them in the existing-property update paths.

Separately, PUTPROP's no-own-property branch was inserting a new property
whenever a non-extensible check passed, even when the prototype chain
contained a non-writable data property. ES5 §8.12.5 / ES2024 §10.1.9.2
require rejecting the write in that case. Add a proto-chain walk for
non-writable data before falling through to the insert path.

commits.subject: fix: for-of head destructuring — member targets, computed keys, parenthesized LHS
commits.body:
Three parse gaps in for-of/for-in loop heads:

1. Member-expression targets in bare destructuring-assignment heads:
   `for ([obj.x] of [[1]])` and `for ({ p: obj.y } of [...])`.
   Added `is_member_target`/`member_obj_reg`/`member_prop_reg` to ArrayBind.

2. Computed property keys in var/let/const binding patterns in heads:
   `for (var { [key]: x } of [...])`. Added `[expr]:` handling at the top of
   the object pattern loops in both `is_forof_destr` and `is_forin_destr`

   `key_reg` directly instead of LDCONST+key_idx for computed keys.

3. Parenthesized LHS in for-of heads:
   `for ((x) of [1])`. Added a three-token lookahead after the identifier check:
   if '(' IDENTIFIER ')' is followed by 'of'/'in', route through the bare
   identifier path (emit_forof_loop / emit_bare_forin_loop).

improvements from pre-existing stash.

commits.subject: fix: template literals with substitutions inside function bodies
commits.body:
Root cause: the naive brace-counting loops in skip_function_body(),
skip_braced_block(), and the pre-scan passes (hoist_decls,
hoist_global_fn_decls, pre_scan_captures) treated the '}' that closes
a template substitution '${...}' as a plain JS block boundary.

The critical path: when a global function declaration is hoisted,
hoist_global_fn_decls() compiles the function and records its name.
The subsequent statement-parse pass then sees the function was already
hoisted and calls skip_function_body() to skip past it. In
skip_function_body(), the '}' of '${expr}' inside a template literal
decremented brace_depth to zero, causing the skip to stop mid-template.
The lexer was then positioned inside the template tail (e.g. at ' b`; }'
for 'return `a ${ s } b`'), and subsequent statement compilation
tokenized that tail as code, producing the 'b is not defined' error.

Fix: add a template_depth counter to all brace-counting loops. When
TEMPLATE_HEAD is consumed, template_depth++. When RBRACE arrives with
template_depth > 0 it closes a substitution — call
scan_template_after_expr() to consume the tail/middle token:
TEMPLATE_MIDDLE keeps template_depth the same (another substitution
follows), TEMPLATE_TAIL decrements it (template literal is complete).
Only a RBRACE with template_depth == 0 is treated as a JS block close.

Applied to: skip_function_body, skip_braced_block, skip_expression
(src/compiler/functions.c3) and pre_scan_captures (captures.c3) and
the hoist_decls / hoist_global_fn_decls scan loops.

commits.subject: fix: per-iteration lexical bindings for for-let/for-of loops
commits.body:
Implement CreatePerIterationEnvironment (ES2015 §14.7.4.2 / §14.7.5.6)
so closures created in different iterations capture distinct values.

For C-style `for (let i = 0; ...)` loops: detect when a let/const init
binding is captured (or conservatively at global scope where capture
analysis is not run). At incr_label — between body and increment, per
the spec ordering — emit GETVAR/POP_LEX/PUSH_LEX/PUTLEX to cycle the
binding into a fresh env. The increment then runs in the fresh env,
and the body on the next iteration sees the updated value through its
closure reference.

For `for (let x of iterable)` loops: when the binding is captured (or
at global scope), emit PUSH_LEX before .next() and POP_LEX after the
body (before the back-jump). The PUTLEX that installs the iteration
value already targets the current (fresh) env each time.

Perf guard: at non-global scope, per-iter envs are only emitted when
the pre_scan_captures pass confirms the binding is actually captured
by a nested closure. Common non-capturing for-let loops are unaffected.

commits.subject: fix: NamedEvaluation for destructuring defaults
commits.body:
Per ES2015 §14.1.20 SetFunctionName, an anonymous function, class, or
arrow used as the default value of a binding pattern element must receive
the binding name as its .name property. Previously compile_default_expr
compiled the default expression thunk without propagating the binding
name, so `{ cls = class {} }` produced cls.name="" instead of "cls".

Thread the leaf binding name into compile_default_expr as an inferred_name
parameter (defaulting to "") and set def_ctx.has_inferred_name before
compiling the default expression, mirroring what the var-declaration path
already does. Apply at all call sites in collect_obj_param_binds,
collect_arr_param_binds, and the direct-param paths in compile_inner_function
and compile_arrow_inner_reparse.

Also fix class_expression to consume has_inferred_name for anonymous class
expressions (matching the existing function_expr behaviour), and fix
expression() to clear has_inferred_name when a comma operator is seen, so
(0, function(){}) does not inherit the outer binding name.

commits.subject: fix: run generator parameter instantiation at call time per spec
commits.body:
Per ES2022 §27.5.3.2, FunctionDeclarationInstantiation — including
parameter default evaluation, destructuring, and all side effects —
must run at the generator call site, before returning the GeneratorObject.
Only the function body is deferred to the first .next().

Adds a GEN_START opcode emitted by the compiler after all parameter
initialization (defaults, destructuring) in generator functions. On the
initial call the VM runs the activation eagerly up to GEN_START, saves
register state into a pre-allocated GeneratorState, writes the generator
object to the caller's result register, and pops the activation. On
subsequent .next()/.throw()/.return() resumes, saved_pc already points
past GEN_START so it is never re-executed.

- bytecode.c3: add GEN_START opcode (NONE format)
- compiler/functions.c3: emit GEN_START after param init in both
  parse_function_body() and compile_inner_function() for non-async generators
- heap.c3: add gen_initial_gs/gen_initial_obj/gen_initial_retval fields;
  mark gen_initial_obj as GC root in mark_roots()
- vm_calls.c3: initial generator call allocates GeneratorState + gen object,
  stashes them in heap fields, then pushes activation and falls through to
  the normal dispatch loop (instead of immediately suspending)

commits.subject: fix: Bucket C — IteratorClose on break/continue + call_fn_impl valstack fix
commits.body:
Three cooperating fixes for ES2015 IteratorClose (§7.4.6):

1. ITER_CLOSE VM handler (vm_control.c3): replace the broken
   vm_check_call_fn_error + return VM_ERROR~ pattern with proper
   vm_throw_value routing so .return() errors propagate through the
   catcher chain instead of leaking as raw VM_ERROR. Also add §7.4.6
   step 5 check: if .return() returns a non-Object, throw TypeError.

2. Compiler (expressions.c3, statements.c3, context.c3, patches.c3):
   - Add iter_close_reg field to LoopInfo; set it in push_loop + for-of
     codegen so break/continue handlers know which register holds the
     iterator object.
   - Emit ITER_CLOSE before BREAK in break_statement when inside for-of.
   - Emit ITER_CLOSE at the normal-exhaustion exit (done=true) of for-of.
   - Emit ITER_CLOSE in labeled-continue when the continue exits for-of
     loops (walks from innermost to target loop, closes any for-of).

3. call_fn_impl valstack fix (vm_execute.c3): for-of ITER_CLOSE calls
   .return() via call_fn_impl. The pre-existing bug: call_fn_impl used
   vm.valstack_top as the callee frame base, but vm.valstack_top is not
   updated by inline JS-to-JS CALL (vm_setup_call), so it could point
   below the current function's live registers, causing the callee's
   frame to overlap and zero live caller registers. Fix: compute the
   true top as max(vm.valstack_top, current_act.bottom + num_regs).

Phase 14 for-of: 342 → 345 pass (+3: iterator-close-via-{break,continue},
iterator-close-non-object, generator-close-via-continue). Rosetta 100/100.

commits.subject: feat: gate disassembler/VM trace behind $feature(TRACE_VM)
commits.body:
Add a new build target `duktape_c3_debug` (`just build-trace`) that defines
`TRACE_VM` and keeps the disassembler, opcode name table lookups, and the
per-instruction VM trace plumbing. The default `duktape_c3` release build
strips the disassemble bodies, the write_* helpers, trace_print_tval, and
trace_instruction — their bodies become no-op stubs, and the per-instruction
`if (@unlikely(vm.trace)) trace_instruction(...)` dispatch in the main
opcode loop is removed entirely.

CLI flags that depend on the trace path (`-c`/`--compile-only`, `-t`/
`--trace-vm`, `--format json`) accept the flag in either build but on the
release build emit a one-shot notice telling the user to run
`just build-trace`. The compile-only output then degrades to the section
headers with no instruction lines, and `--format json` produces a nested
array with empty entries — better than a confusing silent pass with empty
output. Crash dumps (`dump_vm_state`) print the raw opcode ordinal instead
of a disassembled line so post-mortems still give a usable hint in release
builds.

constant array stays compiled in (~3.5KB of .rodata + 952B of pointers).
The .text savings are the real prize — release `duktape_c3` is ~78KB
smaller than `duktape_c3_debug` (1.31MB vs 1.39MB). Closing the table-side
gap requires splitting `bytecode.c3` into a multi-module build, which is a

commits.subject: fix: microtask queue overflow + drop-on-drain — keep async generators alive
commits.body:
The microtask queue held (handler, arg, downstream) triples but the initial
allocation sized the buffer for 16 pairs (32 TVal slots). Once the queue
passed entry 11 — common in any Promise loop body with more than one
reaction — the writes ran past the allocation and corrupted heap memory.

The drain loop then snapshotted and zeroed `microtask_count` before walking
that snapshot. Handlers that resolve another Promise during draining
enqueue new jobs at slot 0, overwriting the still-queued batch and hiding
the original entries from GC.

Switch the drain to a read-cursor walk (i → i++ per entry, no pre-reset)
so new jobs land strictly past the cursor and the whole batch stays GC-visible
until the loop ends. Each microtask triple now lives in 48 TVal slots of
backing memory.

Async/await resume and reject builtins stash their suspended GeneratorState
in var_env, but ordinary FUNCTION-class mark logic only looked at the
var_env bindings object — not at the pointer itself — so the saved registers,
async_promise, and other live references were invisible to GC and got
collected while the Promise was still pending. Add an `is_async_state` flag
and a `mark_generator_state` helper used by both the async builtin path and
the existing generator path.

  frame-setup site the earlier centralization missed; review finding).

commits.subject: fix: capture analysis — captured locals are env-resident (plan 045)
commits.body:
Locals referenced by nested callables (or reachable by direct eval) now
compile to env access on every read/write, so closure/eval mutations and
outer-function views stay coherent. Previously both directions silently
read stale copies: closure writes landed in the env while the outer
function kept reading its register, and outer re-assignments were
register-only stores invisible to closures.

- src/compiler/captures.c3: pre_scan_captures token pre-scan runs before
  each function/arrow body compiles. Callable bodies are detected by
  `) {` (excluding control-keyword parens), `=> {`, and expression-arrow
  extents; `class` bodies, direct eval, and table overflow degrade to
  capture-all. Identifiers inside those regions form the capture set.
- declare_var marks capture-set names is_captured (reads/writes become
  GETVAR/PUTVAR; has_captured_local keeps env elision and needs_env on);
  params are marked retroactively after the scan.
- find_local_reg (capture-blind lookup) keeps `var` redeclaration and
  for-init reuse from re-declaring and clobbering live env values.
- for_statement's register-cache sync is disabled for captured loop vars
  (the env, maintained by INC_VAR/PUTVAR, is authoritative; the old final
  write-back stored a stale register over it).
- emit_call: relocate the callee when its register is a named local's
  home register — CALL writes the result to the callee base, which
  destroyed the binding (`function f(){} f(); f();` with f at top of the
  register stack). Pre-existing, exposed by the new register layouts.

Oracle: test/test_capture_analysis.js (17/17: both staleness directions,
RMW ping-pong, native callbacks, arrows incl. expression-bodied, params,
eval writes, loop pre-position reads, shadowing, method shorthand,
getters, class methods, destructured captures). Regression floor green:
register-locals, destructure suites, lexical-capture and eval oracles,

commits.subject: fix: closures over lexical locals — keep PUTLEX stores and honor captured envs
commits.body:

closures (function f(){ const x = 1; return function(){ return x; } }
threw "x is not defined"):

   captured declarative lex_env; every other call path (native callback
   re-entry via vm_call_fn_impl, the dispatch slow path, setup_call,
   invoke_getter, setter frames, the construct path) set lex_env to the
   fresh var scope, orphaning block-scoped captures. The selection logic —
   captured declarative env plus the named-function-expression name binding
   (which previously skipped the captured env even on the fast path) — is
   now centralized in resolve_call_lex_env and applied at all eight sites.

commits.subject: fix: empty-match unicode advance in RegExp.exec and global Symbol.replace
commits.body:
ES2017 §21.2.5.2.2 step 16-17 (and §21.2.5.2 step 17) requires that when a
global RegExp match produces an empty string, lastIndex advances via
AdvanceStringIndex (1, or one UTF-16 code point when the u/v flag is set)
before the next iteration. Previously both builtin_regexp_proto_exec and
regexp_exec_call wrote out_end (= out_start) straight back to lastIndex,
causing infinite loops for patterns like /^|\udf06/ug on astral input
(where out_end=out_start=0 but ^ matches again at the new pos after a
manual step in the caller, so the caller chased its own tail).

Both helpers now check out_end == out_start and write (out_start +
advance_string_index_byte_len(input, out_start, unicode)) to lastIndex
instead. Sticky-only is unaffected (sticky already doesn't update).

Closes built-ins/RegExp/prototype/Symbol.replace/u-advance-after-empty.js
and Symbol.match/y-fail-lastindex-no-write.js.

commits.subject: fix: Symbol.match/replace dispatch RegExpExec through Coerced S, not raw arg
commits.body:
Both methods passed the original argument TVal (still an Object when
the test gave a {toString() {…}} wrapper) to RegExpExec, while the spec
says Call(exec, R, «S») where S has already been coerced to a string
via ToString. Result: the user's overridden .exec saw the wrapper
object instead of the coerced string, breaking exec-invocation.js for
both Symbol.match and Symbol.replace.

Symbol.match non-global: pass s_hstr_tv (the HString wrapper for S)
instead of &s_tv (the original arg). One-line fix in the dispatch.

Symbol.replace non-global: same fix at the top of the branch, plus
a deeper rewrite to dispatch through regexp_exec_call (the existing
ES2017 §21.2.5.2.1 helper). Read result via Get for index/length/0/cap
so a user-overridden .exec that returns an arbitrary result object
participates in both the functional-replace slow path and the $-pattern
substitution. For built-in re_exec results the captures land in the
match object as strings; we recover positions by scanning input for
the capture value starting at out_start.

Phase 8: 1362 → 1371 pass (+9). No rosetta regressions. Closes the
Symbol.replace exec-invocation.js / exec-err.js / get-exec-err.js /
arg-2-coerce-err.js / result-coerce-matched.js / result-coerce-length.js
families, plus Symbol.match exec-invocation.js.

commits.subject: fix: spec-conformant RegExp.prototype.flags getter for arbitrary receivers
commits.body:
The previous implementation required the receiver to be a REGEXP-class
HObject via regexp_get_this_or_throw, which threw TypeError for
plain objects the way ES2017 §22.2.3.4 doesn't (any Object, including
plain {}, is valid). It also read compiled flags directly out of
(*obj.extra_ptr()).regexp.flags, bypassing spec semantics where global,
ignoreCase, multiline, dotAll, unicode, unicodeSets, hasIndices, sticky
are all read via Get+ToBoolean on the receiver.

Rewrites builtin_regexp_proto_get_flags to walk each flag through
builtins_generic_get + builtin_to_boolean, matching the spec text:
  for each flag in 'dgimsuvy':
    let v = ToBoolean(? Get(this, "<flag>"))
    if v: append <flag>
Returns "dgimsuvy" subset of the active flags in canonical alphabetical
order, exactly as V8/SpiderMonkey/QuickJS do.

built-ins/RegExp/prototype/flags/, the from-regexp-like-get-flags-err
test, and the related get-flags-err.js / flags-tostring-error.js
Symbol.* tests.

commits.subject: fix: propagate ToPrimitive throw_pending through builtin_to_string_vm

When a regex method's input argument has a valueOf/toString that throws,
the throw was swallowed because builtin_to_string_vm checked
vm.throw_pending but never set ctx.should_throw, so callers and the
dispatcher treated the result as "no error". Mirrors what builtin_throw

commits.subject: fix: spec ToString and RegExpExec semantics in RegExp.prototype[@@*]

- Read runtime global/sticky/flags/unicode via Get (so user-overridden
  properties are honoured, not just the compiled bytecode flags).
- Coerce string args via builtin_to_string_vm so objects/booleans/symbols
  go through ToPrimitive first.
- Use a shared regexp_exec_call helper implementing ES2017 §21.2.5.2.1

builtin_to_string_vm (previously builtin_to_string which returned "" for

commits.subject: fix: spec ToString coercion in parseInt and parseFloat
commits.body:
ES2015 §18.2.4 (parseFloat) and §18.2.5 (parseInt) both begin with
ToString(string). The previous implementations skipped ToString
entirely:

- parseInt: fast-path returned fastints directly (skipping ToString
  coercion) and bailed to NaN for any non-string, non-fastint input.
  parseInt(-0) returned NaN instead of 0, parseInt(NaN) bypassed the
  spec NaN check on the string "NaN" (it happened to match because
  strtol rejects "NaN", but the path was wrong).
- parseFloat: delegated to string_to_double which returned NaN for
  booleans, undefined, null, and objects. parseFloat(true) should be
  NaN via ToString(true) = "true" → strtod rejects it, but the test
  was failing because the path short-circuited without ever calling
  ToString.

Fix: route both through builtin_to_string_vm first, mirroring the
ES2015 algorithm. Tests covered: parseInt(-0) → 0, parseInt(true) →
NaN (via "true"), parseFloat(true) → NaN (via "true"), parseFloat(-0)
→ 0, parseFloat(Infinity) → Infinity, parseFloat(null) → NaN.

(S15.1.2.2_A{1,2}_T*) plus parseFloat (-0, Infinity, NaN, true/false
coercion). Rosetta 100/100 unchanged.
