commits.subject: fix: infer Function name from assignment target (ES2015 §14.1.20)
commits.body:
Anonymous function expressions assigned to a variable, used as an object
property value, or written as a method shorthand now inherit the name of
their assignment target — so `var f = function(){}` gives f.name === "f"
instead of the previous empty string.

The fix threads an inferred-name buffer through the parser:
* var_declaration sets `inferred_name` to the declared name before parsing
  the initializer (unconditionally — overwriting stale values from prior
  declarators in the same var statement).
* function_expr / function_expr_body consume the buffer when no explicit
  function name is given. Always clear after consumption so explicit
  names (`var x = function bar(){}`) don't leave a stale inferred name
  for the next declarator.
* object_literal sets the buffer from the property key. Computed keys
  `[expr]` clear it (per spec the inferred name is empty for computed).
  Getter/setter prefixes are added (`"get " + key` / `"set " + key`).
* parse_arrow_function / parse_arrow_function_reparse apply the inferred
  name to arrow function CompiledFunction structs.
* class.c3 prefixes getter/setter method names with `"get "` / `"set "`
  matching object literal semantics.

`compile_inner_function` now heap-allocates the function name (instead
of storing a pointer into the caller's inferred_name_buf), so multiple
sequentially-compiled functions each keep their own stable name. Arrows
get the same treatment via explicit copy in parse_arrow_function*.

Added test/test_name_inference.js covering var/let/const inference,
named-expr override, object literal values / method shorthand /
getter+setter, computed key (no inference), class methods, IIFE,
arrow functions, and name-binding scope (only explicit named exprs
create a lexical binding inside the body).

commits.subject: fix: String.prototype.match sets .index/.input and handles missing args
commits.body:
Three bugs found and fixed in builtin_string_proto_match:

(1) The non-RegExp arg path created the result array but never set
    .index or .input. Per ES5 §15.5.4.10 step 11 these are required
    on the match result, so `__string.match(3).index` and
    `__string.match(3).input` were undefined for number/string args.

(2) The non-RegExp arg path used builtin_to_string which does not
    call ToPrimitive, so objects with custom valueOf/toString were
    coerced via their identity rather than their string hint.
    Switched to builtin_to_string_vm which calls ToPrimitive(hint="string").

(3) When called with no args, undefined, or null, the function
    returned null per ES5.1 step 3. ES2015 §21.1.3.10 step 4
    instead constructs a new RegExp from ToString of the arg (empty
    string for missing/undefined, "null" for null) and calls its
    @@match. Tests for sputnik-style ES5 match behaviour expect this
    shape, e.g. `"".match()` and `"undefined".match(undefined)` should
    produce non-null arrays matching the equivalent RegExp(...).exec.

Added test/test_match_fixes.js covering number/string/object coercion
with .index/.input, no-match returns null, and RegExp arg path still
working. Rosetta 44/44 unchanged.

commits.subject: fix: Array methods work on non-array objects with .length (arguments, plain objects)
commits.body:
ES5 §15.4 Array.prototype methods (map, filter, slice, etc.) are defined
on any object with a `length` property, not just real arrays. Two real
bugs surfaced when exercising them on the arguments object:

1. arr_has_prop and arr_get_elem_vm only consulted the dense array_part
   for ARRAY-class objects. The arguments object stores its indexed
   values in array_part but its class is ARGUMENTS, so map/filter/slice
   on arguments always returned empty results. The fast path now also
   matches ARGUMENTS class.

2. Array.prototype.map on a sparse source like {0:'a', 2:'c', length:3}
   returned a 2-element array (['a', 'c']) because the implementation
   skipped holes and didn't advance the result index. ES5 §15.4.4.19
   step 8.c requires the callback to be invoked for every k in [0,len)
   with undefined for holes. The loop now always invokes the callback
   and writes the result at the next sequential index.

A second bug was uncovered while testing JSON.stringify of array results:

3. json_serialize_array read the length from the named `length` property
   only. Some arrays (e.g. result of Array.prototype.slice on the
   arguments object) have their length stored in the cached
   array_length pointer only, with no named prop — JSON.stringify of
   such arrays returned "[]". Now falls back to *arr.array_len_ptr()
   for ARRAY class when the named prop is missing.

Added test/test_array_generic.js covering: plain object, arguments,
sparse, empty, and JSON.stringify of arrays derived from non-array
sources. Rosetta 44/44 unchanged.

commits.subject: fix: JSON.stringify outputs integer-indexed keys first, sorted numerically
commits.body:
ES5 §15.12.3 step 4.b.ii requires the serialization to emit integer-indexed
keys first in ascending numeric order, followed by all other string keys in
their original insertion order. The previous implementation iterated the
shape chain directly with prop_key_at(i), which produced reverse insertion
order for non-integer keys (e.g. {"p1":"a","p2":"b","add":"add"} for
{add, p2, p1}) and treated integer keys like any other string.

Snapshot the property keys via prop_key_at(i) for i in 0..prop_count-1 (which
already walks the chain in insertion order — that's what Object.keys uses),
then split into integer vs string keys, numerically sort the integer keys
with insertion sort, and concatenate integer-first / strings-after.

This change matches the spec for tests that don't involve delete+re-add
(e.g. {p1:'a',p2:'b',add:getter,0:'0',1:'1',2:'2'} now serializes to
{"0":"0","1":"1","2":"2","p1":"a","p2":"b","add":"add"}).

The test262 property-order test still fails because of an underlying
shape/prop_values bug that scrambles values after delete+re-add
(o.p1 returns "2", o[0] returns "p3", etc.) — this is a separate
issue outside JSON.stringify's scope. After fixing that, this ordering
fix should let property-order and several other ordering-sensitive
JSON.stringify tests pass.

commits.subject: fix: Object.prototype.toString.call returns correct tags for primitives and TypedArrays
commits.body:
Object.prototype.toString.call(x) for a primitive x was returning
"[object Object]" because the builtin only handled the object branch and
fell through to a generic Object message. ES6 §19.1.3.6 step 2 derives
the class from the value type: Undefined/Null/Boolean/Number/String/
Symbol. The implementation now branches on TVal.is_undefined/is_null/
is_boolean/is_number/is_fastint/is_string and is_symbol_val before the
object path. The Arguments ObjClass was also missing from the class-name
switch, so Object.prototype.toString.call(arguments) returned
"[object Object]".

Each TypedArray constructor (Uint8Array, Int16Array, ...) had a single
shared %TypedArray%.prototype as its .prototype, and that shared
prototype carried @@toStringTag = "TypedArray", so every typed-array
instance's toString tag was "TypedArray" rather than the constructor
name. Per ES6 §22.2, each ctor gets its own .prototype that inherits
from the shared one with its own @@toStringTag. register_ta_ctor now
allocates a per-ctor proto and sets the @@toStringTag accordingly.

The per-ctor proto is found via the constructor's own .prototype
property, which requires the builtin dispatcher to expose the callee
HObject. The NEW_OBJ[_S] path and super-call path now set
ctx.callee_obj = hobj so builtins (currently TypedArray constructors)
can introspect their own prototype.

commits.subject: fix: bridge block-scope lex_env so closures see enclosing let/const
commits.body:
When a closure is created inside a function body, the callee's `lex_env`
was previously always set to the freshly-allocated `fast_var_env`. That
means a closure referencing a let/const declared in a `{` block of the
parent body would fail to resolve the binding — the fresh function scope
has no record of it.

Use the closure's captured `lex_env` when it is a declarative block
scope (created by PUSH_LEX), falling back to `fast_var_env` for the
ordinary function-scope or global cases. The captured lex_env points to
the body's binding scope, so closures can see let/const bindings
declared in the enclosing body.

commits.subject: fix: allocate fresh env for functions with simple parameters
commits.body:
A function with parameters but no body locals would previously reuse the
parent's variable environment. Its DECLVAR instructions for each parameter
name then wrote into the shared env, silently clobbering an outer binding
when the parameter name matched one in the calling scope. The classic
reproducer:

    function isSameValue(a, b) { return a === b; }
    function base() {}
    var b = new base();
    b.x = 1;
    isSameValue(b.x, 1);  // outer `b` is now 1 instead of the object

Give any such function a fresh function-scope env on entry, the same as
the existing path for `needs_env=true`. The `needs_lex_bridge` exception
preserves the params-vs-body split for default-valued parameters, which
already allocates its own env through the bridge mechanism.

Both call paths (fast HObject call and the generic dispatch loop) need
the check.

commits.subject: fix: hoist function expressions correctly and document default-param env
commits.body:
Global function-declaration hoisting treated every `function` token at
brace depth 0 as a declaration, double-compiling expressions like
`var x = function f() { ... }` and `arr.map(function() { ... })`. Track
the previous top-level token and only hoist `function` keywords in
statement position (start-of-file, after `;`, `{`, or `}`). Other
function keywords have their body skipped and are left for the regular
statement parser.

Also fix hoist_decls to push back the name token when the function is
anonymous, so skip_function_body sees the full `(...) { ... }` form.

commits.subject: fix: Math.imul, Math.clz32, Math.hypot, and math_arg valueOf propagation
commits.body:
Four latent bugs in Math methods surfaced under test262:

- Math.imul and Math.clz32 used `(uint)x` to coerce doubles, which is
  undefined behavior for negative inputs because `(uint)(-1.0)` overflows.
  Math.imul(-1, 8) returned 0. Rewrite with a 64-bit multiply and an
  explicit int32 reinterpret; Math.clz32 special-cases NaN, Infinity, and
  zero (which all return 32 per ToUint32) before the bit-count.

- Math.hypot(NaN, Infinity) returned NaN, but ES6 §20.2.2.18 says
  Infinity propagates over NaN. Track Infinity and NaN separately and
  pick the result by precedence.

- math_arg used builtin_to_number, which doesn't call valueOf on plain
  objects. Use vm_to_number for object args so valueOf/toString are
  invoked and any exception they throw propagates correctly.

commits.subject: feat: support spread arguments in calls and `new` expressions
commits.body:
Calls and `new` expressions with spread (`f(...args, x)` and `new C(...args)`)
previously failed because the compiler couldn't lay out arguments whose
position depends on a runtime count. Add two opcodes:

- PUTARG: write a value into the call-argument area at a slot computed
  from a runtime count register; increments the count.
- NEW_OBJ_S: same as NEW_OBJ but reads the argument count from a register.

The compiler now emits these when a spread appears in the argument list.
Also move the constructor register to a fresh slot before evaluating
arguments, since per ES2023 §13.3.1.1 GetValue(constructor) must happen
before argument evaluation and an argument assignment could otherwise
clobber the constructor.

commits.subject: fix: bind name in lexical environment for named function expressions
commits.body:
Per ES2015 §14.1.20 NamedEvaluation, the BindingIdentifier of a named
function expression (e.g. `function foo() {}`) must be bound as an
immutable lexical binding inside the function's own scope, so the
body can refer to itself by name and reassignment throws TypeError.

Implementation:
- Plumb an `is_named_expr` flag through `compile_inner_function` and
  set `CompiledFunction.flags.is_namebinding` (which was already
  reserved but unused).
- At call time, when the function is entered, allocate a fresh
  declarative lexical env with the name bound to the function object
  using non-writable flags (PROP_FLAGS_EC). The lex_env's parent is
  the function's var_env so other lookups still walk the normal chain.
- Arrow functions now use their captured `lex_env` instead of
  `var_env` for the new activation, so named bindings inside an
  enclosing named function expression are visible to nested arrows.

Clears `named-strict-error-reassign-fn-name-in-body` and its
`-in-arrow` variant (2 of 3 test262 failures fixed). The `-in-eval`
variant still fails — it requires a real `eval` implementation that
this codebase doesn't have.

No regressions: rosetta 44/44, test262 Phase 1 155/74 (was 154/75).

commits.subject: fix: bind `arguments` correctly when the target has a rest parameter
commits.body:

ran AFTER the rest-parameter handling, by which time new_regs[0] had
already been overwritten with the rest array. For constructors with

sliding-window slot before any overwrite.

commits.subject: fix: preserve local-var slot register across expression statements
commits.body:
A standalone assignment statement like `ok = true` returns the LHS
register as its expression value. expression_statement then freed
that register via free_reg, decrementing next_reg past the var's
slot. The next alloc_reg returned the freed slot, letting the next
property lookup (`x.hasOwnProperty("a")`) overwrite the var's
value with the property-name string. This is the bug that caused
tinycolor's `c._ok` to come back as the string "hasOwnProperty"
instead of the boolean true.

The fix: skip the free_reg when the result register is the slot
of a live local variable AND is the top of the register stack
(so free_reg would actually decrement). The top-of-stack guard
keeps register reuse for temp results that happen to alias a
var slot but aren't themselves live bindings.

Added is_local_var_reg(reg) in src/compiler/scope.c3, a focused
regression test in test/test_regalloc_no_clobber.js, and a
tinycolor smoke test under test/modules/t12_tinycolor.

Also fixed the IF_TRUE/IF_FALSE liveness check in the LDREG-dead
peephole in context.c3:finish — IF_TRUE/IF_FALSE use field A as
a read of the condition register, not a write, and the read-check
must run before the ABC-format dispatch.

commits.subject: refactor: replace fixed-size compiler arrays with growable heap buffers
commits.body:
The CompilerContext previously used fixed-size inline arrays for code,
constants, inner_funcs, and const_hash — hardcoded limits that silently
capped or broke compilation of large modules (e.g. tinycolor with 37
top-level functions).

Replace them with heap-allocated pointers + capacity that double on
overflow, following the same realloc pattern used throughout the runtime.
The hash table grows proportionally and rehashes on constant pool growth.

Also centralizes the 14 inner_funcs write sites into a single
add_inner_func() helper that handles growth, replacing scattered
if (count < MAX_INNER_FUNCS) { ... } blocks.

commits.subject: fix: compiler hoisting and capacity limits for large modules
commits.body:
Fix four interrelated bugs that caused corruption in modules with many
top-level declarations (e.g. tinycolor.esm.js with 37 functions):

- hoisted_fn_names overflowed at 16 entries; functions beyond the limit
  were compiled twice (hoist + main pass), corrupting register and inner
  function indices. Increased array from 16 to 64.
- hoist_decls(true) re-processed function declarations that
  hoist_global_fn_decls already handled, causing triple compilation.
  Now skips function bodies at global/module scope.
- hoist_decls(true) leaked var declarations from inside function bodies
  to the module scope, allocating registers for variables that belong to
  inner functions. Now skips vars at brace_depth > 0 when is_global.
- MAX_INNER_FUNCS (64) was too small for modules with many function
  expressions; overflow silently aliased closures to inner_funcs[0].
  Increased to 256.
- brace_depth could underflow (uint wraparound) when an extra RBRACE
  was encountered. Added a > 0 guard before decrement.

commits.subject: fix: for(var X=init) inside functions binds the hoisted var
commits.body:
A C-style `for (var X = init; cond; incr)` inside a function declared a
fresh register for X instead of reusing the one X was hoisted to, so the
init value and body mutations landed in a register the function body never
read — `return X` after the loop saw undefined.

- Reuse the hoisted register via resolve_var (mirroring var_statement) for
  both the first and subsequent (comma) for-init declarators.
- Restore next_reg to the loop's high-water mark before compiling the
  increment and the condition, so their temporaries allocate above live
  locals rather than into the (low, hoisted) for-var register — fixes
  wrong results when an early return precedes the loop or when the
  condition reads a property of the for-var (e.g. `e.length < 3`).
- Reload the for-var register via GETVAR after the end-of-loop PUTVAR,
  whose handler clears the source register.

commits.subject: fix: strict eval scope isolation — create fresh declarative env
commits.body:
builtin_eval at src/builtins/global.c3 was assigning the eval'd
function's var_env = lex_env = caller_act.lex_env (direct eval) or
ctx.global_env (indirect). The eval'd code's DECLVAR then wrote into
the SHARED env, mutating the caller's bindings — 'let x = 10;
eval("var x = 99");' printed 99, leaking across the eval boundary.

Per ES5 §10.4.2 (strict) and ES6 §18.2.1, strict eval must create a
fresh declarative env. The engine is strict-only (AGENTS.md), so this
is the correct behavior in all cases.

Fix: call env::env_create_declarative(ctx.heap, env_for_eval) to
create a child env, then assign that to func.var_env/func.lex_env.
compile_eval's func.flags.needs_env = false stays — we don't want the
per-call env_create_function_scope alloc, the env is created
explicitly in builtin_eval. env_create_declarative already exists
and is used at vm.c3:5217 for the needs_lex_bridge path.

Verified:
  let x = 10; eval('var x = 99');  → after: 10 (outer unchanged)
  function f() { let y = 5; eval('var y = 99'); } → inside f: 5

Added vm_uncaught_error(vm, &err_val) helper at vm.c3:269 that mirrors
the THROW opcode's recording (vm.has_error, vm.heap.has_error,
vm.heap.error_value, vm.return_val). Dispatched an agent to replace
45+ return VM_ERROR~ sites after failed vm_throw_value calls with
return vm_uncaught_error(vm, &VARNAME), preserving indentation and
handling multi-line, single-line, and braced variants.

Updated the CLI to print 'Uncaught <Name>: <message>' by walking the
error's shape chain to find .name and .message properties (the
prop_hash may not be populated for small freshly-created errors, so
find_prop_idx's hash path misses — the shape chain walk is the
reliable lookup).

Verified:

  throw new Error('boom');   → Uncaught Error: boom
  null.foo;                  → Uncaught Error: Cannot read properties of null
  undefined.x;               → Uncaught Error: Cannot read properties of undefined
  undefined();               → Uncaught Error: undefined is not a function

commits.subject: fix: don't cache inherited property lookups in IC
commits.body:
The IC (ICEntry, MegamorphicEntry) cached inherited property lookups
with proto=owner and prop_value_ptr=owner.prop_values()[idx]. When an
intermediate object in the proto chain was modified (e.g.
B.prototype.foo = ... when b.foo was previously resolved via
A.prototype), the IC returned a stale value because it only checked
the OWNER's prop_alloc, not the intermediates'.

This matches the QuickJS design: QuickJS encodes the proto in the
shape itself and always walks the current chain for lookups. The
shape's prop field is never stale because shapes are never mutated
in place — they're always transitioned (unlinked + re-linked, or
cloned) on property changes.

Fix: gate IC populate on owner == hobj (own properties only) at all
four property-read sites and the megamorphic cache. Inherited lookups
always walk the chain via get_prop_or_accessor_proto — O(depth) with
O(1) per level via the property hash table. For depth 1-3 (the common
case), this is fast.

commits.subject: fix: handle lightfunc intermediates in GETPROPC2 hop 2
commits.body:
When the intermediate result of hop 1 is a lightfunc (e.g. Math.min after
Math['min']), the GETPROPC2 handler at vm.c3:4131 took the
'mid_val.is_object()' branch and set ra2 to undefined. This broke
chained property access on builtins like 'Math.max.apply',
'Array.prototype.concat.apply', 'Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call',
etc. — all of which go Math.X.apply / .call / .bind.

The single GETPROPC opcode has explicit lightfunc handling at
vm.c3:3968-4021 that walks Function.prototype for .call/.apply/.bind
and resolves .name/.length from builtin metadata. Added an equivalent
branch to GETPROPC2 hop 2.

This bug was previously masked by the LDCONST+GETPROP peephole
over-conservatism (commit 95aaf55): when the LDCONST+GETPROP fusion
didn't fire, the trailing GETPROPC handled .apply correctly. With the
fusion fixed, the trailing instruction became a GETPROPC2 data slot
which had no lightfunc handling — exposing the latent bug.

Verified: apply_call.js now passes all 12 assertions. Rosetta: 44/45.
prototypes.js still fails — separate bug in prototype property
writeback/inheritance visibility.

commits.subject: fix: make LDCONST+GETPROP peephole scan format-aware
commits.body:
The scan at context.c3:363-379 treated b/c fields of every instruction as
register references. For A_BC opcodes (LDCONST, LDINT, GETVAR, PUTVAR,
DECLVAR, SETALEN, CLOSURE, etc.), b/c are the low/high bytes of a 16-bit
immediate value, NOT register operands. LDINT r11, +4 has c=4 (high byte
of BC=4), which the scan misread as a reference to register r4 — blocking
the LDCONST fusion whenever an LDINT immediate coincidentally matched the
key register.

After the fix, the LDCONST+GETPROP fusion fires more often, and the
downstream GETPROPC2 chain fusion (jit.c3) can then fuse consecutive
GETPROPC pairs. Verified: in apply_call.js, both apply sites now produce
GETPROPC2 + GETPROPC instead of LDCONST + GETPROP + GETPROPC for the
first and GETPROPC2 + GETPROPC for the second.

apply_call.js still crashes but in a different place — see next commit.
The root cause is in the GETPROPC2 handler or its IC integration, not in
the LDCONST fusion. Prototypes.js unchanged (different bug).

commits.subject: opt: GETPROPC2 chain-fusion superinstruction for chained property access
commits.body:
jit_scan detects consecutive GETPROPC pairs where the output of the first
feeds the input of the second (e.g. obj.a.b), rewrites the first to
GETPROPC2, and repurposes the second slot as a data slot holding dst2/key2.
The handler executes both hops with a single dispatch, populating ICs for
both sites on miss.

Technique from VMIL 2024 superinstruction synthesis work.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: opt: GETPROPC_CACHED specializing adaptive opcode (PEP 659 style)
commits.body:
After the per-site IC is first populated for a GETPROPC site, the opcode is
rewritten in-place to GETPROPC_CACHED. The specialized handler skips the
ic_base null check and key pointer comparison, only validating shape_id and
prop_alloc. On shape change it downgrades back to GETPROPC and re-executes.

Technique from CPython PEP 659 (3.11, 2022): in-place bytecode specialization
after warmup.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: opt: megamorphic global property cache for polymorphic call sites
commits.body:
512-entry (shape_id, key) → (owner, prop_idx, value_ptr) hash table shared
across all GETPROP/GETPROPC call sites. When the per-site IC misses (shape
changed or IC cold), the global cache is probed before the full prototype
chain walk. On IC population the entry is also stored in the global cache.

Technique from SpiderMonkey/V8 (2022-2023). Separate heap allocation keeps
the hot Heap struct compact.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: feat(async/await): implement async/await with resumable execution
commits.body:
Implement full async/await support using resumable execution (same
approach as QuickJS/V8). Async functions return Promises, await
suspends on pending Promises and resumes via microtask callbacks.

Key changes:
- AWAIT opcode: checks settled Promises (extract value), suspends on
  pending (saves state to GeneratorState, creates resume/reject
  callbacks, adds reaction, pops activation)
- CALL opcode: async initial call creates Promise, enters body,
  writes Promise to result register for suspension case
- vm_call_fn_impl: detects resume_gen for async resume, restores
  saved PC and registers
- Compiler: async functions get is_generator=true for state save/
  restore; await emits AWAIT+LOAD_RESUME; async hoisting detects
  `async function` pattern
- Builtin async resume/reject callbacks drive the resumption cycle
- Fix pre-existing skip_function_body bug (paren/brace depth)
- Remove dead hoisting.js rosetta test (zero assertions ran)
- 23 async tests + 43 rosetta tests pass

Async generators (async function*) will not be implemented.

commits.subject: feat(compiler): parse async function declarations and expressions
commits.body:
Add lexer/parser support for `async function` syntax in both declaration
and expression positions. The result is a normal CompiledFunction whose
`is_async` flag is set; the VM does not yet honour the flag, so calling
an async function still returns the raw return value rather than a
Promise.

Changes:
- tokens.c3: add match_async_function() helper that peeks ahead and
  consumes the `async` keyword only when followed by `function` (so
  arrow function parameters and other uses of `async` as an identifier
  remain unaffected).
- statements.c3: in statement() default case, detect
  IDENTIFIER(="async") + FUNCTION and dispatch to function_declaration
  with is_async set. Save/restore the flag for nested declarations.
- expressions.c3: in primary_expr IDENTIFIER case, intercept
  `async function` and dispatch to function_expr.
- functions.c3: propagate is_async to inner CompilerContext in
  compile_inner_function; save/restore in function_expr.
- context.c3: copy is_async to func.flags.is_async in finish().

Parser is syntax-only; semantics (Promise wrapping, await lowering) are
tracked under plan 034.

commits.subject: refactor(promise): move state out of array_part into HObjectExtra
commits.body:
Promise internal state (state, result, reaction list) previously lived in
the user-visible array_part[0..N], which was corruptible by:
  - user assigns to numeric indices (p[0] = ...)
  - Object.keys(), Object.defineProperty(p, "0", ...)
  - Array.prototype operations inherited via the prototype chain

The new design uses a dedicated HObjectPromise struct in HObjectExtra,
keyed by flags.obj_class == PROMISE. Reactions are now a linked list of
HObjects (linked via a hidden \xFFpromise_reaction_next property) rather
than array slots, so they cannot collide with user-visible indices.

Changes:
- hobject.c3: add HObjectPromise { state, result, reactions_head,
  reactions_tail } to HObjectExtra union. Decref string result on free.
- heap.c3: GC mark case for ObjClass.PROMISE that walks the reaction
  linked list and marks the result TVal.
- promise.c3: rewrite state helpers (promise_init/settle/get_state/...)
  to use the extra slot. promise_trigger_reactions walks the linked list
  and unlinks each reaction before invoking. promise_add_reaction does
  O(1) append via tail pointer. All promise_set_result callers now pass
  the heap for refcounting.
- plans/index.md: register plan 034.

Existing Promise rosetta/promise tests pass. No regressions in rosetta
suite (43/43) or test/test/*.js (123/124 — one pre-existing failure
unrelated to this change).

commits.subject: fix: stage PUTPROP setter call frames above caller's live registers
commits.body:
The accessor-setter paths in PUTPROP staged the callee/this/arg at
registers A+1..A+3 and wrote the setter's return value over register A.
That convention is only safe for GETPROP, where A is a fresh expression
temp at the top of the live range; PUTPROP's A/B/C are arbitrary live
locals, so invoking any JS setter from inside a function silently
corrupted caller variables (test262 propertyHelper verifyWritable broke
on every accessor property).

Stage the frame at caller num_regs instead (valstack_top is not
reliable here — builtin calls can leave it lowered), use raw stores for
the scratch slots (tval_copy_ref would decref stale garbage above the
initialized frame), and discard the setter return value (retval=null).

commits.subject: fix: arguments[i] and Object.keys([]) — register zeroing & array key filtering
commits.body:
Two bugs exposed by new Rosetta Code tests:

1. VM register init clobbers arguments object: When a function has zero
   formal parameters but is called with arguments (e.g. `function f() {
   print(arguments[0]); } f(42)`), the sliding-window model places args
   at new_regs[0..nargs-1]. But the register zeroing code started at
   undef_limit=0 (since formals=0), overwriting all argument values with
   zero. Fix: start the memset at max(undef_limit, nargs).

2. Object.keys on arrays includes "length": The named-properties loop in
   Object.keys didn't skip "length" on array objects (only on string
   exotics), and numeric-index named properties duplicated the dense
   array loop. Fix: skip "length" and numeric-index named properties
   when the object is an array exotic.

commits.subject: fix: clear callee registers after decref to prevent double-decref via overlapping frames
commits.body:
Callee frames overlap the caller's register window (sliding-window
calls). decref_callee_regs released refs but left the stale TVal bits
in place; the caller's own return then decref'd the same slots again
(its max_heap_reg covers the overlap from arg/this stores), underflowing
refcounts. In rosetta/quicksort this freed the global Math object while
still bound, recycling its memory as a closure (Math became callable)
and double-freeing at heap teardown.

commits.subject: fix: allow compare+branch fusion when rA aliases a source operand
commits.body:
When a comparison writes its result to the same register as one of the
source operands (e.g., `LE r3, r3, r0` in a loop condition), the fusion
pass's liveness analysis incorrectly prevented fusion because the
aliased register appeared live at the branch target. After fusion, the
JMP_LE/JMP_LT/etc. instruction does not write to any register, so the
aliased register retains its pre-compare source value — exactly what
the branch target expects. Skip the branch-path liveness check when
rA == rB or rA == rC.

Fixes the collatz loop that previously hung due to its loop counter
being clobbered by the unfused compare.

commits.subject: Fix property hash table corruption on growth and delete
commits.body:
Three bugs in the per-object property hash table:

- Growing the table during put_prop rebuilt it from the old table's
  entries, dropping the newly appended key (which was only in the
  shape). The property became permanently unfindable — on the global
  object this surfaced as "X is not defined" for whichever global
  triggered the resize.
- delete_prop compacted prop_values without updating the hash table,
  leaving stale indexes for every property after the deleted slot.
- The direct-insert fast path never synced hash_prop_count, so the
  staleness check in ensure_prop_hash was ineffective.

ensure_prop_hash now always rebuilds from the shape chain, delete_prop
rebuilds the table after compaction, and direct inserts sync the count.

Fixes 6 failing bench_fast benchmarks (bench_object died with "nested
is not defined") and takes test262 quick.sh from 0/283 to 258/25.

commits.subject: Fix var_ic_base missing in inline CALL dispatch (GC corruption on deep recursion)
commits.body:
The inline CALL dispatch paths (both fast and slow) set ic_base to the
callee's IC entry array but forgot to update var_ic_base — the analogous
pointer for VarICEntry (the inline cache for GETVAR/SETVAR/DECLVAR).

When a callee executed a GETVAR instruction, it wrote into
var_ic_base[callee_pc_offset] — but var_ic_base still pointed at the
caller's VarICEntry array. The callee's PC offsets indexed into the wrong
array, scribbling garbage over the caller's VarIC slots. The corrupted
vic.key fields held NaN-boxed fastint values that the GC mark_tval scan
interpreted as heap pointers, causing heap corruption on deep recursive
calls with string/object values.

Fixes the non-deterministic segfault in bench_valstack_copy (string
recursion now passes 100/100).

commits.subject: Fix GC corruption on deep recursive calls with local variables
commits.body:
Defer vm.activation_count++ to after all activation fields (var_env,
lex_env, this_binding) are fully initialized. The previous code
incremented activation_count before env_create_function_scope, making
the activation visible to vm_mark_activations while var_env/lex_env
still held stale pointers from the reused activation slot. This caused
GC to follow garbage EnvRecord->bindings pointers during heap
allocation.

Also clear the 'this' slot (regs_base[callee_reg+1]) before env
creation to prevent the GC valstack scan from following stale
NaN-boxed object pointers left over from the previous call in the
sliding-window register model.

Fixes the deterministic VM_ERROR on bench_valstack_copy. A residual
non-deterministic crash (~40% at N=22) remains from stale values in
the temp register area overlapping the caller's frame; this requires
a more comprehensive GC-root validation fix.

commits.body:

constructor and sets needs_restart=true, but never saved curr_pc
back to act.curr_pc. When the super constructor returned via

was the only one missing it.

commits.body:
Add the foundational reference-counting machinery needed for deterministic
heap-object freeing.  Strings are NOT refcounted (M&S-managed); only objects
and buffers participate.  The refcount field is placed after `flags` in
HeapHeader/HObject/HString to fill alignment padding (struct size unchanged).

- `refcount` field in HeapHeader, HObject, HString (strings stay at refcount 0)
- `HeapHeader.incref()` / `refcount = 1` in `init()` for all new allocations
- `Heap.decref()` — unlinks from heap_allocated, frees on count 0 (skips strings)
- `Heap.decref_tval()` — dispatches on TVal tag to decref objects/buffers
- `set_object`/`set_buffer`/`make_object`/`make_buffer` auto-incref the target
- `set_string`/`make_string` do NOT incref (strings are M&S-managed)

VM-side activation (RET/RETUNDEF decref of callee registers, per-opcode decref
for LDREG/LDCONST/LDINT etc.) is deferred — it requires every raw TVal
assignment in the codebase to be converted to refcount-aware copies first.

commits.subject: Fix comparison aliasing bug and reduce memory overhead
commits.body:
LT/LE/GT/GE opcodes wrote the result to ra before reading rb/rc.
When ra aliases rb (e.g. LE r1 = r1, r2), set_boolean(false) clobbered
the source operand before the comparison, always yielding false. This
broke all for-loops and any comparison where the result register matched
an input register.

CompiledFunction (incref/decref were defined but never called), and
reduced initial capacities: GRAY_STACK_INITIAL_CAP 1024→64,
GC_MAX_ROOTS 128→16, INITIAL_VALSTACK 1024→256.

commits.body:
All arithmetic (+, -, *, /, %, **) and bitwise (&, |, ^, ~, <<, >>, >>>)
operators produced NaN or garbage when operands were BOOLEAN, OBJECT
(wrapper), NULL, or UNDEFINED. Root cause: `num_val` macro and ADD
handler called `get_number()` on non-numeric TVal types, reading raw tag
bits as doubles.

commits.subject: Fix compound assignment/prefix-postfix bugs (arithmetic opcode ra-tag ordering + PUTVAR write-back)
commits.body:
Bug 1 (VM): All arithmetic and bitwise opcodes (SUB, MUL, DIV, MOD, EXP, ADD,
BAND, BOR, BXOR, SHL, SHR, USHR, UNP, UNM) set ra.tag = NUMBER before reading
rb and rc. When ra == rb (compound assignment x -= 1, prefix ++/--), num_val(rb)
returns garbage because the tag was already changed to NUMBER. Fix by capturing
num_val results into local doubles before modifying ra.

Bug 2 (compiler): postfix_expr and unary_expr for ++/-- at global scope never
emitted PUTVAR after modifying the operand register, so increment/decrement
effects were lost. This caused infinite loops in for-loops using i++ as the
update expression. Fix by tracking last_was_getvar and emitting PUTVAR after
the operation, matching the pattern used by assignment_expr.

Also fix bash script issues in test262_runner/quick.sh (local keyword usage).

commits.subject: Implement try/catch/throw VM with catcher chain
commits.body:
Phase 4 of the port is now complete. Key changes:

- Added Catcher struct with linked-list chain (CATCH_ENABLED, FINALLY_ENABLED)
- vm_throw_value() walks catchers across activation boundaries, unwinding
  intermediate activations when a catcher is found in a parent
- TRY opcode: pushes catcher with catch/finally handler PCs from bytecode
  jump slot (NOP word after TRY encoding finally_offset)
- ENDTRY: pops catcher (normal exit)
- THROW: walks catcher chain, jumps to handler
- CATCH: reads thrown value from catcher; pops catcher if no finally
- FINALLY: no-op marker
- ENDFINALLY: re-throws pending exception if finally was entered via throw
- Compiler modified: TRY encodes flags (bit0=catch, bit1=finally) in A field,
  catch_offset in BC, finally_offset in jump slot word
- PUTVAR emitted after CATCH at global scope for env-based variable access
- All error sites (GETPROP/PUTPROP null/undefined, CALL non-function,
  NEW_OBJ non-constructor, GETVAR undefined) use vm_throw_value() instead
  of return VM_ERROR~, making errors catchable by try/catch
